stories.title: Yogi says ‘Arigato Gozaimasu’ in Japanese:Meets delegation in Delhi, celebrates Nagasaki governor’s birthday
stories.summary: CM Yogi met with a Japanese delegation in Delhi on Tuesday. He celebrated the birthday of Japanese Governor Kotaro Nagasaki. The CM presented him with an idol of Lord Ganesha. During this, the CM also spoke in Japanese. He said- Friends, there is a very beautiful philosophy in Japan- ‘Ichiego Ichie’, meaning every moment and every meeting is unique. This evening also holds the same sentiment for us. At the end of his address, he said in Japanese, ‘ Arigato Gozaimasu’. That is, thank you very much. The 'UP-Japan Investment Meet 2026 ', which started on 18 August, will continue till 23 August. It is being organized in Delhi and Lucknow. More than 200 prominent industrialists from Japan and CEOs of several companies will participate in it. Read Yogi's 2 big points 1-'Ancient relations between India-Japan, Buddha's compassion in them' Japan is called the land of the rising sun. Uttar Pradesh is the land of the Suryavansh (Solar Dynasty). Lord Shri Ram's Ayodhya is here. Lord Buddha gave his first sermon in Sarnath, UP. Kushinagar, the land of his Mahaparinirvana, is also here. The ancient relations between India and Japan contain Buddha's compassion, life's discipline, and also the middle path. These are also the shared values of both our countries. 2-'Lord Buddha's teachings reached Japan from UP centuries ago' CM said: Lord Buddha's teachings reached Japan from the sacred land of Uttar Pradesh centuries ago. In 752 CE, Indian Acharya Bodhisena played an important role in the eye-opening ceremony of the giant Buddha statue at Todai-ji temple in Nara. This is evidence of the deep cultural and spiritual relations between India and Japan in ancient times. CM said- The centuries-old cultural, spiritual, and people-to-people relations between India and Japan have now transformed into a modern strategic partnership. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japan's leadership have taken the relations between both countries to new heights. CM also mentioned revolutionary Rash Behari Bose. He had taken refuge in Japan, escaping British rule, and later strengthened India's independence movement from Japan. In honor of his role in relations with Japan, he was honored with the 'Order of the Rising Sun'. Know about UP-Japan Investment meet 1- Escorts Kubota to invest ₹2,025 crore, employment for over 3,800 people A major industrial hub for Japanese companies is being developed in the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) area. Escorts Kubota company will invest ₹2,025 crore in Sector-10 of YEIDA. Tractors, construction equipment and other goods will be manufactured here. This is expected to provide employment to over 3,800 people. 2- Investment of ₹1,166 crore in two projects of Minda Minda Corporation will set up two projects in Sector-10 and Sector-24 of YEIDA. These will involve a total investment of ₹1,166 crores. These projects are expected to provide employment to approximately 6,440 people. Ignition switches, steering locks, mechatronic goods, wiring harnesses, and connection systems will be manufactured here. The projects of Escorts Kubota and Minda will bring a total investment of ₹3,191 crores. These are expected to provide employment to more than 10 thousand people. 2- Japanese City to be built on 500 acres The Yogi government is working on a plan to build a Japanese City on 500 acres of land in YEIDA. Japanese companies, along with their suppliers and small ancillary industries, will also be set up here. This will enable companies to easily obtain necessary materials. Additionally, there is hope for growth in new technology, supply chain, and employment opportunities.

stories.title: Dumper runs over 4 boys on one bike:Victims were heading to birthday party; dragged for 10 metres

The collision was so severe that the boys were thrown 10 meters away. In the accident, three died on the spot, while one died during treatment at the hospital. People present at the scene during the accident said that the dumper and bike collided head-on. The dumper driver lost balance while trying to save the bike. After that, he collided and fell into a ditch by the roadside. The incident occurred on Tuesday at 8:30 PM near Bharat Gas Agency on the Nichlaul-Maharajganj road. Read the full story According to eyewitnesses, the accident was so horrific at 8:30 PM on Tuesday that there was screaming and chaos at the scene. Three young men died on the spot in the accident, while one young man was seriously injured. The police, who arrived after being informed by local people, immediately took the injured to the Community Health Center (CHC) Nichlaul, where doctors declared him dead after examination. As soon as information about the accident was received, the police team reached the spot and inspected the scene. After the accident, a large crowd of people gathered at the spot. The police have taken possession of all four bodies and started the process of sending them for post-mortem. It is being reported that the dumper driver lost control while trying to avoid the bike, after which the dumper fell into a ditch by the roadside. Police engaged in investigating the accident The police have started investigating the vehicles involved in the accident. Along with this, information is also being gathered from eyewitnesses regarding the incident. The police are investigating the causes of the accident and the role of the dumper driver.

stories.title: Ayodhya hotel project:Lucknow HC quashes acquisition order, calls Awaas Vikas Parishad’s decision contrary to investment policy
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court's Lucknow bench has quashed the Housing Development Council's decision regarding land acquisition related to a proposed hotel project in Ayodhya. The court clarified that after a project is approved under the government's investment and tourism policy, the concerned departments should not act contrary to their own previous decisions. The bench of Justice Alok Mathur and Justice Amitabh Kumar Rai set aside the order issued by the Housing Commissioner on 29 May, 2024. The bench has directed the state government to take a decision in accordance with law within six weeks regarding the release of this land from acquisition. This case is related to 2,530 square meters of land located in Kudakeshavpur Uparhar village. The Ayodhya Development Authority had approved the map for hotel construction on this land on 17 July, 2023. However, subsequently, the Housing Development Council issued a notification for acquisition of the same land on 19 August, 2023. The court found in its hearing that the acquisition process was initiated after the hotel's plan was approved and the construction work of the project had begun. The court emphasized that government departments should honestly comply with the promises made and decisions taken under policies promoting investment.

stories.title: ‘I am BJP MLA, I’ll get you beaten and jailed':Lakhimpur MLA threatens secretary over phone, says, “You’ll be ruined if I see you”
stories.summary: I am an MLA of the ruling party; if I just look at a tree, it will wither. No matter how powerful someone is, I will have them beaten up and put in jail. The poor public has voted for me; I am not a slave of any rich person. Lakhimpur's BJP MLA Vinod Shankar Awasthi reprimanded the secretary of the cooperative society over the phone. Actually, the MLA had gone out on a tour of the constituency, when farmers stopped him. They said that the secretary is selling government urea and NPK fertilizer at overrate. Urea fertilizer worth ₹260 is being sold at 280. ₹20 extra is being charged. Hearing this, the MLA became angry. He called the officers. After this, he got the amount recovered from 25-30 farmers refunded. The incident took place at 2 pm on 17 August at the cooperative society in Kharwahiya market. Its video surfaced on Tuesday afternoon. After listening to the farmer, MLA called and summoned the officers It is reported that farmers had been complaining for a long time about fertilizer being sold at higher prices at the Khagiapura B-Packs Society. On Monday at 2 pm, the MLA reached near the society. Farmers told him that the secretary was acting arbitrarily and not listening to anyone. On the farmers' complaint, the MLA called the officers and summoned them to the spot for investigation. AD Cooperative Zulfikar, Tehsildar Dhaurahara, and police also reached the spot. During the investigation, the society's secretary, Shridhar Verma, was not found there. Secretary apologized when MLA got angry When the MLA called ADO Cooperative Rajneesh Singh, his number was off. After this, the MLA complained to District Agriculture Officer Surya Pratap Singh. Finally, he called Secretary Shridhar Verma. On the phone, the secretary informed him that he was not present at the committee. The employees are distributing fertilizer. In response, the MLA said, ‘’It is the poor people who have voted and elected me. Such exploitation of them will not be tolerated. After this, the secretary apologized to the farmers.'' The farmers told the MLA, ''The secretary has made a mistake for the first time. Therefore, please forgive him. After this, the MLA warned the secretary that action would be taken if complaints were received in the future.''

stories.title: Panchayat secretary caught with girlfriend:Wife attacked him with slippers, accused him of running a sex racket
stories.summary: A panchayat secretary was caught by his wife with a woman inside a flat in Lucknow, leading to a heated argument between the couple. The wife beat the woman and slapped her five times before hitting her husband twice on the face with her shoes. Police reached the spot after being informed about the commotion and brought the situation under control. The incident took place on 15 August, and a video of the incident has now surfaced. Alsaf Beg, who is posted as a secretary at a gram panchayat under the Mal development block, was found with the woman in a flat at Sulabh Awas on Kursi Road. After receiving information, his wife Saba reached the spot. An argument broke out between the couple, which soon escalated into a physical altercation. The incident took place in the Gudamba area. See 2 pictures... Wife says: Husband beats her every day Wife Saba told the police in her complaint that she was married to Alsaf Beg on 9 June, 2021. Alsaf is posted as a Gram Panchayat Officer. The allegation is that he used to beat her after the marriage. Due to the husband's bad behavior, after some time, his family members threw him out of the house. Since then, she has been living with her husband in a rented house. The couple has a two-and-a-half-year-old daughter. The allegation is that Alsaf does not take care of his wife and daughter. He has threatened to kill her several times. Since the marriage, he often would not return home until late at night on some pretext or another. He would leave his wife and daughter alone. Accusation of threatening by showing off government job Saba has alleged that her husband consumes alcohol and drugs. In an intoxicated state, he beats his wife and daughter. Along with this, he threatens to throw her out of the house and marry someone else by showing off his government job. Complaints were made at the police station several times against the husband, and reconciliation was also arranged between the two, but there was no improvement in his behavior. Saba has also accused her husband of having relationships with other women and being involved in illegal activities. She has also accused her husband of running a sex racket. Action for breach of peace against Panchayat Secretary According to Gudumba Inspector Anjani Kumar Mishra, on 15 August, Saba received information that her husband Alsaf was present with a woman in a flat. Upon receiving the information, she reached Block-B of Sulabh Awas located on Kursi Road. There, Alsaf was found with a woman. After this, the UP-112 team brought both parties to Gudumba police station. Saba has filed a complaint with the police, making several allegations against her husband, including harassment and assault. The dispute between husband and wife has been sent for mediation. Meanwhile, action has been taken against Secretary Alsaf Beg for breach of peace.

stories.title: Retired Army man kills brother-in-law wearing bulletproof vest:Fires 3 shots after in-laws take wife home; mob ties up and beats him
stories.summary: A retired soldier murdered his own brother-in-law in Pratapgarh. He reached his brother-in-law's medical store shop from Sultanpur. There, he opened indiscriminate fire. Before the brother-in-law could understand anything, three bullets had hit him. He fell to the ground, drenched in blood. The accused had arrived wearing a bulletproof jacket. The soldier tried to flee from the spot. The crowd caught him. They tied him with rope and beat him. The police who arrived at the scene somehow saved the accused soldier Kapil Yadav (43) from the crowd. He was admitted to the hospital. People from the vicinity took brother-in-law Devendra Yadav (48) to the district hospital. There, doctors declared him dead. Soldier Kapil Yadav was having a dispute with his wife Priyanka. On Monday, Devendra went to his brother-in-law's house in Sultanpur. From there, he brought his sister Priyanka and the children along with him. Kapil was angry with his brother-in-law over this matter. The incident took place on Tuesday at 12 noon in the Kohandaur police station area, 25 km away from the district headquarters. First, see 3 pictures... Marriage happened 15 years ago, dispute with wife for 6 months Soldier Kapil (43) had married Priyanka 15 years ago. Last year, Kapil had retired from the army. He had started working as a guard at the district hospital in Sultanpur. There had been a dispute between husband and wife for 6 months. On Monday, Kapil had a dispute with Priyanka again over something. Priyanka called her brother Devendra. Devendra reached Priyanka's house in Sultanpur. From there, he brought Priyanka and her children to his home. Fired 10 rounds rapidly Devendra has a medical store shop in Madafarpur market in Pratapgarh. On Monday, he was sitting at the shop. Just then, Kapil reached there from Sultanpur. He was in army uniform. There was an argument between the two. Kapil threatened, saying, ‘How dare you bring Priyanka?’. During this, when the matter escalated, Kapil opened rapid fire. Eyewitnesses said that he fired 10 rounds from a licensed pistol. Three bullets hit Kapil. One in the head, second in the waist, and the third in the leg. When he tried to flee after murder, crowd caught him and tied him with rope The murder in broad daylight caused panic. There was a stampede-like situation in the market. When Kapil tried to flee from the spot after the murder, the crowd chased and caught him. Kapil pointed the pistol at the crowd. However, there were no bullets in it. The crowd overpowered him. When he started fighting, they tied his hands and feet with rope. After this, he was severely beaten. Blood started coming out of his mouth. After about 15-20 minutes, the police arrived. Kapil was somehow rescued from the clutches of the crowd. Kapil Yadav is a resident of Khanapur in Amethi district. Accused said- Had gone to bring children and wife wearing bulletproof jacket Accused Kapil Yadav told at the hospital, ''I had gone in the morning to bring my children and wife Priyanka. My wife has a boy and a girl, whose education was being affected. Earlier, my brother-in-law had threatened me that if you come, I will shoot you. I had said that whatever happens, I will definitely come for the children's future. Due to the threats, I came wearing a bulletproof jacket. As soon as I arrived, father-in-law Prasad Yadav, elder brother-in-law Devendra, and younger brother-in-law Upendra attacked me with iron rods and sticks. Due to the beating with rods and sticks, I fell to the ground. After that, in self-defense, I fired from my pistol.'' SP said- Accused Kapil has murdered his brother-in-law with a licensed pistol. The incident occurred due to a family dispute. The accused has been taken into custody. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Farmer sets himself on fire:Revenue team arrives to hand over possession; accused of demanding ₹50,000
stories.summary: A farmer set himself on fire in front of a revenue and police team that had reached Goharni village in Shamli on Monday evening to hand over possession of a piece of land. While on fire, the farmer jumped into a water-filled field. Police personnel at the spot immediately pulled him out and sent him to the district hospital along with his father and brother. The farmer, Aditya, alleged that the revenue team had demanded ₹50,000 from him in exchange for helping him get possession of the land. The administration, however, said a court had already ruled on the land dispute, and the revenue team had reached the spot with police personnel to implement the order. The administration said the allegations made by the farmer would be investigated. According to the administration, a case concerning around 1.0256 hectares of land under Khasra No. 647/2 in Goharni village had been pending before the SDM court. A final order in the case was issued on 30 April 2013. After this, Veerbala submitted an application seeking possession of the land. The revenue department team visited the site on 30 June, measured the land, and identified the disputed plot. A complaint regarding the land was also raised during the Tehsil Samadhan Diwas on 17 August. Following this, officials ordered that the land be cleared of encroachment. As part of the action, the revenue team reached Goharni village with police personnel on Monday evening. Farmer poured an inflammable substance on himself when revenue team arrived Action was underway in the field on Monday evening in the presence of the revenue and police teams. According to the administration, as soon as the team reached the spot, farmer Aditya suddenly poured an inflammable substance over himself. Before anyone could understand what was happening, he set himself on fire. As flames rose, panic spread among the people and police personnel present at the spot. The farmer then jumped into a water-filled field to save his life. Police personnel immediately pulled him out of the field. His father and brother were also called to the spot. The injured farmer was taken to the district hospital by police personnel along with his family members, where he is undergoing treatment. Farmer alleges ₹50,000 was demanded to hand over land possession After the incident, farmer Aditya made serious allegations against the revenue team. He claimed that ₹50,000 was being demanded from him in exchange for helping him get possession of the land. He said he was distressed over the issue. The farmer's allegations have added a new twist to the case. stories.title: Yogi orders suspension of lekhpal, revenue inspector:Woman says in Janata Darshan, 'They won’t give us passage, complain wherever you want'
stories.summary: CM Yogi is in Gorakhpur today and appeared strict during the public audience at Gorakhnath Temple on Tuesday morning. A woman complained that some influential people were blocking her access and, when she protested, they told her, “Go wherever you want to complain.” The CM became angry after hearing her complaint. The CM directed officials to ensure that the woman was given access. He said that if anyone was preventing her from getting the way, the lekhpal, revenue inspector, and tehsildar should all be suspended. He also warned officials that negligence or attempts to evade responsibility in land-related matters would not be tolerated at any level. He directed that strict action be taken against the responsible employee or officer, depending on the seriousness of the case, wherever negligence was found in the disposal of revenue matters. See 2 pictures of the public audience... CM met around 200 people, personally listened to their problems Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who arrived in Gorakhpur on Monday, held a public darshan at Gorakhnath Temple on Tuesday morning. In the program organized outside Mahant Digvijay Nath Smriti Bhavan, the CM met around 200 people. He approached each petitioner and listened to their problems. People submitted their letters to the Chief Minister, which he read himself to understand the complaints and problems. CM told the people not to worry. The government stands with every needy person. Every victim's problem will be resolved on a priority basis. In some other matters related to land, people also complained about the negligence of revenue employees. On this, the CM directed the District Magistrates of the concerned districts to take strict action against the responsible employees and officers. Assurance of help also given to people who came for treatment Many people had also come to the public audience with appeals for financial assistance for treatment. The Chief Minister assured them that the government will provide all possible help for treatment. He instructed officials to get Ayushman cards made for eligible and needy people. CM said that even after the Ayushman card is made, if financial assistance is needed for treatment, help will be provided from the Chief Minister's Discretionary Fund. He instructed the officials to ensure that no needy person faces difficulties in obtaining treatment and that eligible people receive the benefits of government schemes on time.

stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday launched the 'Chief Minister PRD Family Welfare Scheme' for Provincial Rakshak Dal (PRD) jawans across Uttar Pradesh from Gorakhpur. During the event, 10 PRD jawans were also given cashless medical cards. CM Yogi said the government was going to increase the allowance for PRD jawans to ₹600. At the Yogiraj Baba Gambhirnath Auditorium, ₹3,000 was transferred directly into the bank accounts of PRD jawans as a uniform allowance. Earlier, the foundation stone was laid for a new PRD building to be constructed in Lucknow. ‘UP is no longer a BIMARU state’ CM Yogi said Uttar Pradesh was no longer a 'BIMARU' state and was moving forward on the path of development. He said the state's economy had tripled under the current government. CM Yogi criticised previous governments, saying they used to bow before mafias. He said: “Previous governments allowed people to loot and looted themselves. They used to take the state's money abroad.” He alleged that such leaders had accumulated huge amounts of money for their future generations and believed they could flee abroad if they faced any trouble. See 3 pictures 'Missiles were falling where the money was deposited' Referring to money allegedly kept in Dubai, CM Yogi said: “Those who deposited money in Dubai, during the America-Iran war, missiles were falling exactly where the money had been deposited. The war was happening there, but the leaders were worried.

stories.summary: Following the dog attack on a child on the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) campus, the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) has raised serious questions about the university's security arrangements. The ABVP's BHU unit has submitted a written demand letter to the Dean of Students and the Registrar, seeking immediate and concrete measures to prevent such incidents from recurring on campus. The organisation has given the university administration 48 hours to take action. Meanwhile, six days after the incident, the child remains admitted to the BHU Trauma Centre. According to his father, the child is still unable to speak properly and is communicating by typing on a mobile phone. The university had handed the investigation over to the Proctorial Board, but its final report has not yet been made public. ABVP has demanded that the report be released. Action demanded within 48 hours, agitation threatened Pallav Suman, president of the ABVP BHU unit, said the safety of students should be the university administration's top priority. He said negligence in security arrangements would not be tolerated. Unit co-secretary Raghavendra Pratap Singh said the organisation had asked the administration to take the necessary steps within 48 hours. ABVP has warned that it will launch an agitation if action is not taken within the stipulated period. Child has spent six days in trauma centre The child's father said six days had passed since the incident, but his condition had still not returned to normal. He is unable to speak properly and communicates his needs and thoughts by typing on a mobile phone. According to his father, the child has not yet been given anything to eat and his treatment is continuing. He said he trusted the university administration and hoped justice would be delivered in the matter. Proctorial Board investigating, report awaited After the incident, the university administration assigned the investigation to the Proctorial Board. However, even after six days, the final report has not been made public. ABVP has questioned what aspects were examined during the investigation and what conclusions were reached. The organisation said the administration should make the findings public and clarify what further steps will be taken to address concerns over campus security. ABVP puts forward three major demands ABVP has submitted three key demands to the university administration- Mandatory vaccination: All stray and pet dogs on the campus should be vaccinated. Identification and monitoring: Radio- or RFID-equipped collars should be fitted to dogs to enable their identification and monitoring. Action over Prof Shraddha Singh's residence: In the context of the incident, appropriate and strict action should be taken by immediately vacating the residence of Prof Shraddha Singh.

stories.title: 200 buffaloes removed amid PAC deployment in Lucknow:Locals attacked team on 16 August; Mayor says 'We will clear the entire area'
stories.summary: After the attack on the Lucknow Municipal Corporation's cattle-catching team in Para, the administration has adopted a strict stance. On Tuesday, personnel from three police stations and one company of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) accompanied the municipal team. All personnel were wearing helmets and bulletproof jackets. Under heavy police protection, the municipal team removed around 200 buffaloes from 4 colonies. Mayor Sushma Kharkwal and Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar also reached the spot. The Mayor said an attack on police personnel, whose job is to protect people, was unacceptable. She said the entire area would be cleared of illegally operated dairies and animals. She added that the attackers had targeted both the police and municipal employees, while a sub-inspector had suffered a fractured skull in the assault. Illegal dairy operators attacked team on Sunday On Sunday, a municipal team accompanied by a sub-inspector and other police personnel had reached the area when operators of illegal dairies allegedly attacked them. Based on a complaint by Animal Welfare Officer Avdhesh Kumar, police registered a case against Abrab, Imran, Saloon, Subil, Sarafat, Atiq, Aashif, Warish, Naseem, Ranu, Zeeshan, Nafish and 24 unidentified people. Several suspects were taken into custody. Two women were also arrested on Monday. Mayor: “Inspector was beaten, strict action will be taken” Mayor Sushma Kharkwal said the operation was being conducted jointly by the police and Municipal Corporation. She said: “The way they beat municipal employees and the inspector was completely unacceptable. Strict action will be taken. The entire area will be cleared. Today, the entire area has been cleared. The attackers are being answered today. The police are there to protect you, not to be beaten by you.” See 6 pictures- Action taken in Tikonia, Gayatri Vihar and Gyanendra Vihar The municipal team and police force first carried out action in Tikonia, Gayatri Vihar and Gyanendra Vihar. Buffaloes were removed from around 10 houses and dairies in these areas. Because of the heavy police deployment, residents did not dare to protest in the way they had during the previous operation. After completing the action in these localities, the team moved towards Kulharkatta Road near Haider Canal. Buffaloes were also being caught in Deputy Kheda. Some women abused the team members, but the presence of a large police force prevented the protest from escalating. Police deployed to prevent another attack Personnel from Para, Dubagga and Kakori police stations accompanied the Municipal Corporation's cattle-catching team during Tuesday's operation. Several senior officers, including ACP Kakori Shakeel Ahmed, also reached the site. Municipal Corporation veterinary officer Abhinav Verma said around 200 buffaloes were caught during the campaign. The Municipal Corporation has been continuously removing buffaloes from dairies and sending them to the Kanji House in Thakurganj. The drive to clear illegally operated dairies and remove the animals will continue. Police maintained tight security throughout the operation to prevent a repeat of Sunday's violence. Buffaloes found tied inside houses Operators of illegal dairies had hidden buffaloes inside their homes. Municipal employees entered the houses, untied the animals and loaded them into cattle-catching vehicles. No one protested during this part of the operation. Why is the Municipal Corporation catching buffaloes? The Municipal Corporation has clarified that under the Municipal Corporation Act, 1959, keeping buffaloes within urban limits is prohibited, as they are classified as polluting animals. A maximum of two cows can be kept with a valid licence. The administration says illegally operated dairies and keeping animals such as buffaloes in residential areas can lead to unhygienic conditions and blocked drains. The local administration and Municipal Corporation therefore take action against such activities, treating them as sources of pollution, filth or public nuisance. Two women arrested a day earlier Following Sunday's attack, police arrested two women on Monday and sent them to jail. They were identified as Khushboon (24) and Afreen (26), daughters of Abbas from Mohalla Gadiyana in Adarsh Vihar. According to police, municipal employees and government vehicles were pelted with stones during the attack. The sub-inspector was also allegedly surrounded and beaten. Further action is being taken on the basis of the complaint filed by the animal welfare officer.

stories.summary: The BJP on Tuesday appointed new state in-charges and co-in-charges for Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Gujarat, ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections in all three states. BJP national president Nitin Nabin appointed national general secretary Vinod Tawde as the party’s Uttar Pradesh in-charge, while Gujarat leader Jagdish Ishwarbhai Patel was named co-in-charge. Former Rajasthan BJP president Satish Poonia has been given charge of Punjab, while BJP national general secretary Tarun Chugh has been appointed Gujarat in-charge. The appointments come a day after Nabin announced his new team of office-bearers, which includes 65 party leaders. Vinod Tawde gets key UP responsibility Tawde, a BJP national general secretary, has previously served as the party’s in-charge for Haryana and Bihar. He was appointed Haryana in-charge in November 2020 and was later given responsibility for Bihar in September 2022. He continued as Bihar in-charge in 2024 and was overseeing the state when the BJP won the 2025 Assembly elections. Tawde has also held several organisational positions in Maharashtra and served as a minister in the state government and as Leader of Opposition in the Maharashtra Legislative Council. Jagdish Patel, who has been appointed UP co-in-charge, is a Gujarat BJP leader and former MLA from Amraiwadi. He served as president of the BJP’s Ahmedabad city unit and was appointed a national secretary of the party in August 2026. Poonia gets Punjab, Chugh to handle Gujarat Satish Poonia, a former Rajasthan BJP president and Leader of Opposition, has previously served as Haryana in-charge. He was also the party’s election in-charge for Haryana during the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. Poonia was Haryana in-charge when the BJP secured a third consecutive victory in the state Assembly elections. He was elected to the Rajya Sabha in June 2026. Tarun Chugh, a BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP, has previously handled organisational responsibilities in Telangana, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. He was given charge of these regions in 2020 and continued as Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh in-charge in 2024. BJP prepares for three crucial Assembly elections The latest appointments are significant as Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Gujarat are all scheduled to hold Assembly elections in 2027. Uttar Pradesh has 403 Assembly seats and is currently governed by the BJP under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The party faces a major challenge after its setback in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, when the Samajwadi Party emerged as the largest party in the state. Punjab, which has 117 Assembly seats, is currently ruled by the Aam Aadmi Party under Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann. The AAP won 92 seats in the 2022 Assembly elections. Gujarat has 182 Assembly seats and is governed by the BJP, with Bhupendra Patel as Chief Minister. The BJP won a record 156 seats in the 2022 Assembly elections. With the three states heading towards elections, the BJP’s new appointments are aimed at strengthening the party’s organisational preparations and election strategy.

stories.title: Bulldozers demolish 59-year-old madrasa in UP:Six raze it in 2 hours; police clash with SP workers
stories.summary: More than half of a madrasa was demolished by bulldozers in Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh, on Tuesday. The 59-year-old madrasa had been built on government land. At around 7 am, the SDM and nearly 100 police personnel from five police stations reached Pipra Ramlal village with six bulldozers. The demolition began at the 'Maktab Madrasa', which was spread across 14,000 square feet. Meanwhile, Domariyaganj SP MLA Sayyada Khatoon, SP district president Lalji Yadav, and more than 50 party workers reached the site. They protested against the bulldozer action and raised slogans. When police tried to stop them, an argument broke out. There was also a minor scuffle between the two sides. Tension remained in the area for around half an hour. Police later put up barricades and moved people away from the site. Within two hours, seven rooms, a shop and half of the madrasa's hall were demolished. The incident took place in the Domariyaganj tehsil area, around 50 kilometres from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures of the bulldozer action- 400 children studied at the madrasa; court order issued on 14 August Local residents said Arabia Zia-ul-Uloom Madrasa was established inside the village in 1938. In 1967, it was shifted to the main road in Pipra Ramlal village along the Bansi-Domariyaganj road. The madrasa was initially built on private land, but was gradually expanded onto vacant government land in front of it. Officials said around 400 children studied at the madrasa. According to government records, 9,000 square feet of the madrasa's land is registered as a playground. In 2022, five villagers jointly filed a petition before the Domariyaganj Tehsildar's Court seeking removal of the alleged encroachment from the land. After hearing the case, an eviction order was issued in 2023. Madrasa caretaker Abdul Salam challenged the order before the DM's Court that year. After three years of proceedings, the DM upheld the Tehsildar's Court order on 14 August, 2026, and dismissed the madrasa side's petition. The administration subsequently issued a notice directing the removal of the alleged illegal encroachment. When it was not removed within the stipulated period, demolition began in the presence of Domariyaganj SDM Vivekanand Mishra, Domariyaganj CO Brijesh Verma and Bansi CO Shivendu Singh. Heated argument broke out between police and SP workers SP leaders reached the spot after receiving information about the bulldozer action and asked the police to stop it. They said the action was wrong. The police responded that it was an administrative action and that the madrasa had been built on government land. They asked the SP workers to let them carry out their duties, but they refused to back down. SP leader Kamal Ahmed Khan tried to move towards the madrasa, but Dumariyaganj police station in-charge Shri Prakash Yadav stopped him. He told them not to force their way through, otherwise the police would have to take action. Kamal Khan became angry and said, “Fine, do whatever you want. Will you lay hands on me?” As the situation became tense, other police personnel intervened and calmed him down. MLA Saiyeda Khatoon also urged the SP leaders to remain calm and resolve the matter through peaceful dialogue. SP leader confronts inspector: “Are you going to lay hands on me?” During the confrontation, SP leader Kamal Ahmed Khan tried to move towards the madrasa. Domariyaganj station in-charge inspector Shri Prakash Yadav stopped him. Shri Prakash told him that the action was being carried out on the administration's orders and asked the SP workers not to force their way through, warning: “Otherwise, we will also have to use force.” Kamal Khan became angry and replied: “Fine, do whatever you want. Are you going to lay hands on me?” A heated exchange then broke out between the two. As the commotion intensified, other police personnel intervened and calmed the situation. SP MLA Sayyada Khatoon also appealed to the party leaders to remain calm and talk peacefully.

stories.title: SIT submits final report to govt on Ram Mandir case:Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra not named; 8 accused already in jail
stories.summary: The SIT formed by the Uttar Pradesh government to investigate the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has submitted its final report. According to sources, the report does not name former Trust general secretary Champat Rai or Trust member Dr Anil Mishra. The other eight accused are already in jail. The UP Home Department has handed the report to Ram Mandir Trust president Mahant Nrityagopal Das. It will be placed before the Trust at its meeting on September 2. The Trust had requested the Uttar Pradesh government to order an SIT investigation into the alleged theft of offerings. The state government constituted a three-member SIT on June 13 under the chairmanship of Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant. IG Range Kiran S and Special Secretary, Finance, Neel Ratan Kumar were its other members. The SIT submitted its preliminary report on June 23. The Supreme Court later directed that the SIT investigation be placed under an IPS officer and that a finance expert be included. A new SIT was constituted on July 20, comprising Lucknow Range IG Kiran S, Ayodhya DIG Somen Verma and Ayodhya SSP Gaurav Grover. This SIT is still investigating the alleged theft of offerings. SIT submitted preliminary report on June 23 The alleged theft first came to light on June 7. The UP government's SIT submitted its preliminary report to Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad on June 23. An FIR was registered on June 25 on the complaint of Trust member Krishna Mohan. Eight people, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, were named in the FIR. However, the names of senior office-bearers, including Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra, were not included. Within hours of the FIR being registered, police arrested all eight accused, including Tinnu. They are currently lodged in Faizabad jail. All eight have been accused of stealing cash and jewellery while counting offerings. Following the SIT's preliminary report, general secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr Anil Mishra resigned, taking moral responsibility. The Trust accepted both resignations and removed Gopal Nagarkatte from its list of special invitees. Why did the Supreme Court order a second SIT? Four separate petitions related to the alleged offering theft case have been filed in the Supreme Court. Apart from seeking a CBI investigation, the petitioners have also sought the formation of an expert committee to examine various issues related to the management of donations at the Mandir. The earlier SIT was reporting at the state-government level, whereas the new SIT will submit periodic status reports directly to the Supreme Court. The apex court itself is monitoring the investigation. The Supreme Court observed that police officers have a more direct and effective role in criminal investigations and the technical investigation of theft cases. Therefore, the investigation was handed over to police officers by including the DIG and SSP in the new SIT. SC asks SIT to submit report in sealed cover On Monday, lawyers representing the petitioners told the Supreme Court that they should also be provided with the investigation report so that they could assist the court. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta responded that an investigation report could not be shared with people who were not directly connected with the case. The lawyer then argued, ‘We are not strangers. This petition has been filed on behalf of the people of India. We have a fundamental right to know the truth. If investigation-related information is given to an accused or someone assisting the investigation while the petitioners are kept away from it, they will not be in a position to assist the court.’ The Supreme Court responded firmly, saying, 'We have constituted the SIT. It is accountable and answerable to this court. It must submit its report to us.' The court directed the SIT, which includes a forensic auditor, to submit its status report to the Supreme Court in a sealed cover. The court said it would examine the report first and then decide whether it should be shared with all parties.

stories.title: Ranu earns ₹17,000 by selling neem sticks on train:After killing cousin in Kanpur, stays at Goa hotel with money from foreigner
stories.summary: Shocking information has come to light in the case of Sohail alias Ranu Khan, the main accused in the Sadha murder case in Kanpur. He speaks English well, along with Russian, South Indian, and Bundelkhandi languages. This is why he befriended a foreigner in Goa and stayed in a hotel with his money, while also befriending a Russian girl and traveling around with her. During his escape, he arranged 17 thousand rupees by selling neem twigs for brushing teeth. He had murdered his cousin on the night of August 7 After the brutal murder of his cousin, vehicle driver Mumtaz, at 12 AM on August 7 in Devsadh village of Sadh, the main accused Sohail alias Ranu had absconded. After committing the murder, Ranu reached his sister's house in Hamirpur. From there, he went to Chitrakoot and cut his hair to hide his identity. At one point, the police reached him and showed him his own photo, asking if he had seen this person anywhere. He knew that the police were after him. So he reached Manikpur and boarded a superfast train, fleeing through Bhusawal, Mumbai, Valsad, Surat, Ratnagiri, and reaching Goa. To avoid being asked for a ticket by the TTE on the way, he broke twigs from neem trees, made small bundles, and sold them on the train. During police interrogation, he revealed that he sold neem twigs worth about 17 thousand rupees on the train between Hamirpur and Goa. Had worked as a chef in Kochi, Mumbai, Goa Because of this, neither the TTE caught him, and he also earned money. He told the police that he knows how to speak English, Russian, South Indian, and Bundelkhandi languages well. He has worked as a chef in Kochi, Mumbai, and Goa. He also knows how to cook well. Leveraging this ability, he befriended an Englishman and stayed in a hotel in Goa using his money. Here, he also became good friends with a Russian girl, who also helped him. As police pressure increased, he came to Kanpur to surrender and was caught. Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal stated that Ranu is cunning and also knows several languages. Because of this, during his escape, he continued to deceive and swindle people.

stories.title: Home Ministry seeks report on firing at Varanasi airport:Probe to be completed in a week, action against those responsible for security lapse
stories.summary: On the morning of August 16, two employees were injured when a pistol accidentally discharged while being checked at Varanasi's Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport. The incident is being treated as a major security lapse. The Ministry of Home Affairs has now sought a detailed report on the matter. Central agencies are also investigating the incident. The report is expected to be prepared within a week and will identify those responsible for the security lapse. Further action against the officials concerned may then be decided. Shiv Sena leader detained after pistol goes off On August 16, Shiv Sena leader Kamlesh Rai, a resident of Azamgarh, arrived at the airport with his wife. During the security check, his pistol accidentally discharged, injuring two airport employees. The incident caused panic at the airport. Security agencies detained Kamlesh and later handed him over to the police. Following the intervention of the Ministry of Home Affairs, a detailed investigation is now under way. Everyone questioned separately, CCTV footage scrutinised Airport Director Puneet Gupta said investigating agencies were present at the airport the day after the incident. Airline officials, Airport Authority employees, those involved in the incident and security personnel were questioned separately. CCTV footage of the incident and the surrounding security process was also scrutinised. The biggest question being examined is how the passenger's licensed pistol was allowed to reach the point where it was being handled inside the airport despite the initial security checks. Security rules allegedly not followed while checking pistol According to the airport director, prescribed safety standards were not followed while the weapon was being handled. CCTV footage reportedly shows that, under the rules, the security personnel was supposed to check the pistol. Instead, Kamlesh himself took out the weapon and began checking it. Airport officials say private security personnel can sometimes come under pressure from influential individuals and may hesitate to enforce security protocols strictly. This has raised further questions about the security arrangements at the airport. What happened on the day of the incident? At around 9.30 am on August 16, Kamlesh Rai, an Azamgarh resident and Shiv Sena leader in Mumbai, was travelling to Mumbai with his wife on Air India Express flight IX-1810 from Varanasi airport. He had already declared the pistol he was carrying before boarding the aircraft. During the weapon inspection, a bullet entered the chamber. As the trigger was pressed, the pistol discharged. After receiving information from the Airport Authority, police reached the spot. They found a pistol and 21 cartridges in Kamlesh's possession. He was questioned for around five hours before Phulpur police took him to the police station. Bullet injures two airport employees The bullet initially struck the floor before hitting the thigh of Suman (32), a female employee from Gaya, Bihar, who was standing nearby. Bullet fragments then struck Rohit Raj's hand. Both employees were injured and covered in blood. They were immediately taken to hospital for treatment. Kamlesh is former Mumbai corporator Kamlesh Rai, who is from Azamgarh, is a Shiv Sena leader and former corporator in Mumbai. His social media profiles contain photographs with Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and Dhananjay Singh. Airport was on high alert during Independence Day period Puneet Gupta, Director of Varanasi airport at Babatpur, said the airport authorities had been informed in advance that Kamlesh would be travelling with a pistol. The airport had been declared a high-alert zone from August 11 to 20 because of the Independence Day security arrangements. The incident has therefore raised questions not only about the handling of the weapon but also about the entire security process, the conduct of the personnel involved and the effectiveness of the investigation itself.

stories.title: Rain in 15 cities including Lucknow, schools shut in 7:Ratneshwar and Brahmeshwar Mahadev temples 70% submerged in Varanasi; alert in 75 districts
stories.summary: The monsoon spell continues across Uttar Pradesh. Intermittent rain has been falling in 15 cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki and Saharanpur, since 3 am on Tuesday. Dense, dark clouds have kept the skies gloomy, making it appear dark even in the morning. Schools in Prayagraj, Mirzapur, Kaushambi, Bhadohi, Hardoi, Amethi and Jaunpur have been closed today. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of the state. 3-4 feet of water fills Prayagraj colonies After heavy rain on Monday, colonies and lanes in Prayagraj's Kareli area were inundated with 3-4 feet of water. Cars and motorcycles were submerged. Police and NDRF teams rescued residents from the affected areas and moved them to safer locations. Meanwhile, more than 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Yamuna, are in spate across UP. More than 100 temples near Varanasi ghats submerged Water has entered more than 100 small temples located along the ghats in Varanasi. The Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple at Manikarnika Ghat and the Brahmeshwar Mahadev Temple at Dashashwamedh Ghat are around 70% submerged. Only their domes remain visible above the water. 500+ homes flooded in Kanpur and Unnao Areas along the Ganga in Kanpur and Unnao have been inundated, with water entering more than 500 homes. Residents have been forced to stay on rooftops. In Chitrakoot, rising water levels in the Mandakini and Bardaha rivers have submerged the steps at Ramghat. 10-metre-wide crater opens on Ganga Expressway On Monday, 65 cities, including Ghaziabad, Kanpur and Varanasi, received rainfall. In Unnao, a deep crater around 10 metres wide opened near milestone 421 on the Ganga Expressway at Sonik, on the Meerut-Prayagraj carriageway. The ground near the side railing also subsided. See pictures of rain- Rain to intensify from August 19 According to Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh- The monsoon has become active due to the formation of a low-pressure area, the northward shift of the monsoon trough and moisture coming from the Bay of Bengal. Monsoon activity is expected to intensify further between August 19 and 23. The rain spell will continue under the influence of the low-pressure system developing over the Bay of Bengal. Heavy rain is likely on August 20 and 21.

stories.title: Farmer's neck cut by Chinese manjha in Gorakhpur:7 stitches after string catches him while riding to buy vegetables
stories.summary: A farmer riding a motorcycle in Nausad, under the Gida police station area of Gorakhpur, suffered a deep cut to his neck after getting entangled in Chinese 'Manjha' on Monday evening . Blood began gushing from his neck following the accident. Despite the injury, the farmer managed to remove his T-shirt and tie it around his neck to control the bleeding. He then somehow reached a doctor at a nearby intersection, where he received seven stitches. Now know the full story Rampratap Nishad (55), a farmer from Nausad, was riding his bike to Haraiya market to buy vegetables at around 6.30 pm on Monday. While he was on his way, a Chinese 'Manjha' suddenly became entangled around his neck. The sharp string cut into his neck, causing him to fall from his motorcycle. Tied T-shirt around neck to stop bleeding Rampratap said that blood started gushing from his neck immediately after the accident. He quickly removed his T-shirt and tied it around his neck in an attempt to stop the bleeding. Despite his injury, he somehow managed to reach a doctor at the nearby intersection for treatment. Doctor puts seven stitches After examining Rampratap, the doctor treated the wound and put seven stitches on the cut area. His condition was subsequently reported to be stable. The incident has increased concern among local residents over the continued use of Chinese manjha. People have demanded an effective ban on the sale and use of the prohibited ‘Manjha’ (Kite String)

stories.title: Centre relaxed rules for Anjaneya 7 times:Will he get another extension; why does the government favour the senior IAS officer so much?
stories.summary: The deputation of IAS officer Anjaneya Singh, who brought SP strongman Azam Khan from political prominence to the brink of ruin, has ended in UP. He has handed over charge as Moradabad Divisional Commissioner to the Moradabad DM and gone on leave. His deputation has been extended seven times since he came to UP from his parent cadre, Sikkim. So, will Anjaneya's deputation be extended again? What could be the reason? Read in UP Explainer. Can Anjaneya Singh's deputation be extended for the 8th time? If yes, what could be the reason? Nothing can be said with certainty at this stage. However, sources say Anjaneya may get another extension, or service extension. The UP government has already sent a proposal to the Centre. There are six main political and administrative reasons behind the move. Political Reasons i) Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says that while serving as DM of Rampur, Anjaneya Singh took strict legal action against SP leader Azam Khan and his family. From Johar University to pursuing dozens of cases against Azam, he implemented the government's agenda on the ground. His role in giving the BJP a political advantage in SP strongholds such as Rampur and Moradabad is considered extremely important. ii) According to senior journalist Ratanmani Lal, the government is highly impressed by Anjaneya Singh's working style and administrative grip. To manage the Moradabad division in Western UP, which is considered politically and communally sensitive, the BJP government does not want to take a risk with a new or unfamiliar officer during an election year. iii) To balance political equations in Western UP and prevent any laxity on the law-and-order front, the government needs an experienced administrative face who is familiar with the region. Administrative reasons i) Anjaneya Singh has completed a long tenure of 5.5 years as Commissioner of the Moradabad division. He has a deep understanding of the region's law and order, communal sensitivity and geographical situation, which a new officer would not have. ii) Several cases involving Azam Khan and his close associates, along with legal proceedings related to land attachment and recovery, are at crucial stages in the courts. The state government believes that changing officers at this juncture could weaken the prosecution of these cases. iii) The Sikkim government has had no objection to Anjaneya Singh continuing in UP and has issued a No Objection Certificate (NOC). This makes it easier for the Centre to consider extending his tenure. Can a proposal to extend his deputation be rejected for any reason? Yes, that is possible. In fact, the Central Government sent Anjaneya to UP after relaxing two rules under the 'All India Service Manual'. First Rule: An All India Service (IAS/IPS) officer cannot normally be sent on deputation to their home state. Anjaneya, however, is originally from Mau district in UP. Second Rule: For an IAS officer, the maximum period of deputation outside their cadre to another state cannot normally exceed seven years, even under special circumstances. Anjaneya has already spent 11 years in UP. Under Rule 3 of the Manual, the Central Government can relax any rule in the 'public interest or extraordinary circumstances'. In Anjaneya's case, the Central Government has done so seven times. Experts believe that another extension could weaken the structure of the cadre system. Sikkim has a small cadre with limited strength. The absence of a senior and experienced IAS officer from the 2005 batch for 11 years affects the state's administration. Keeping the interests and governance needs of small states in mind, the Centre could order Anjaneya to return to Sikkim. Can a proposal to extend his deputation be rejected for any reason? Yes, that is possible. In fact, the Central Government sent Anjaneya to UP after relaxing two rules under the 'All India Service Manual'. First Rule: An All India Service (IAS/IPS) officer cannot normally be sent on deputation to their home state. Anjaneya, however, is originally from Mau district in UP. Second Rule: For an IAS officer, the maximum period of deputation outside their cadre to another state cannot normally exceed seven years, even under special circumstances. Anjaneya has already spent 11 years in UP. Under Rule 3 of the Manual, the Central Government can relax any rule in the 'public interest or extraordinary circumstances'. In Anjaneya's case, the Central Government has done so seven times. Experts believe that another extension could weaken the structure of the cadre system. Sikkim has a small cadre with limited strength. The absence of a senior and experienced IAS officer from the 2005 batch for 11 years affects the state's administration. Keeping the interests and governance needs of small states in mind, the Centre could order Anjaneya to return to Sikkim. Instead of extending his tenure, can the Centre also call him on central deputation? Under the normal rules, this cannot be done immediately. Anjaneya Singh, a 2005-batch IAS officer, is eligible to work as a 'Joint Secretary' at the Centre. However, since he is currently serving in UP instead of his parent cadre, he would have to return to Sikkim and complete a two-year 'cooling-off period'. According to sources, keeping open the possibility that the extension proposal could be rejected, Anjaneya Singh is trying for an appointment in Delhi through the Sikkim government. Anjaneya wants to be appointed as 'Resident Commissioner' at Sikkim House in Delhi. This would allow him to remain outside Sikkim while technically serving his parent cadre. After completing the two-year cooling-off period at Sikkim House, he would try to get included in the 'empanelment list' for central deputation. The list is prepared by the Central Government after a strict screening process and determines which officers are suitable for various positions at the Centre. Once an officer's name appears on the list, they can be called for central deputation from their parent cadre when a suitable ministry position becomes vacant. If the Centre wants to call Anjaneya directly for central deputation, it would have to exempt him from the entire process by invoking 'public interest or extraordinary circumstances' under Rule 3 of the Manual. This would amount to relaxing the rules for Anjaneya for the eighth time. How did Anjaneya Singh get deputed to his home state? There are two provisions for deputing an All India Service officer to their home state- First: Marriage, when the officer is married to an officer from another cadre. Second: Extreme personal or family hardship, this can include serious illness of parents or family members, the need to care for elderly parents, or a threat to life. The first provision does not apply in Anjaneya Singh's case. It is possible that he received deputation to his home state under the second provision. However, the government never officially disclosed whether this was the reason for his posting. In February 2015, then Home Minister Rajnath Singh recommended Anjaneya's deputation to UP. Despite the state being governed by the Samajwadi Party at the time, Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav approved the recommendation.

BJP’s new team signals UP election formula:5 big faces dropped, 6 new leaders in focus; understand the signs
stories.summary: The BJP’s new national team under president Nitin Nabin gives Uttar Pradesh a significant representation, with eight leaders from the state receiving key responsibilities. Rekha Verma and Prof Tariq Mansoor have been retained as national vice-presidents, while six new faces have been inducted. The changes appear aimed at balancing caste and regional equations ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Five prominent leaders, including Laxmikant Vajpayee and Radha Mohan Das Agarwal, have not found a place in the new national organisation. The reshuffle can be understood through three key questions: Why were two leaders retained? Why were six new faces inducted? And why were five senior leaders left out? Nitin Nabin visited Uttar Pradesh in July and stressed better coordination between the government, organisation and NDA allies. The new national team also appears to reflect the need for leaders who can contribute directly to the BJP’s 2027 election campaign. Why were Rekha Verma and Tariq Mansoor retained? Kurmi and women voters Rekha Verma’s continuation is significant for the BJP’s OBC strategy. The Kurmi community is among the largest OBC groups in Uttar Pradesh after Yadavs. A section of Kurmi voters shifted towards the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. By retaining Verma, the BJP has signalled that Kurmi representation remains important at the national level. Her presence also strengthens the party’s representation among women. Verma has organisational experience, including her role as the BJP’s co-in-charge of Uttarakhand. Her experience in handling organisational responsibilities in states could also prove useful to the new team. Pasmanda Muslim outreach Tariq Mansoor, former vice-chancellor of Aligarh Muslim University and an MLC, remains one of the BJP’s prominent educated Muslim faces. The party has been trying to expand its outreach among Pasmanda Muslims in Uttar Pradesh. Retaining Mansoor could help the BJP take its message of inclusive development to sections of the Muslim community, particularly educated and middle-class voters. The move could also be part of an attempt to reduce one-sided Muslim consolidation behind the Samajwadi Party in the 2027 election. Why did six new faces get a place? Smriti Irani returns to the organisational front Smriti Irani’s political activity had reduced after her defeat to Rahul Gandhi in Amethi in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Her appointment as a national general secretary brings her back to the BJP’s organisational front. Irani remains a prominent BJP leader because of her victory over Rahul Gandhi in Amethi in 2019 and her tenure as a Union minister. Her appointment from the Uttar Pradesh quota suggests that the party could give her an important role in the state ahead of the 2027 elections. She could also be useful in the BJP’s outreach to women voters and its political campaign against the Congress. Harish Dwivedi to strengthen eastern UP Harish Dwivedi’s appointment as national general secretary is significant for eastern Uttar Pradesh. He has remained active in the organisation and has considerable experience in the state’s politics. Eastern UP remains crucial for the BJP after the party suffered setbacks in the region in the 2022 Assembly election and the 2024 Lok Sabha election. His elevation could also help the BJP address concerns among Brahmin leaders. Brahmins are estimated to account for around 12-14% of Uttar Pradesh’s population and can influence electoral outcomes in several constituencies. Bhola Singh strengthens Dalit outreach Dr Bhola Singh has been elected from Bulandshahr for three consecutive terms and comes from the Khatik community. He is considered one of the BJP’s prominent Dalit faces in western Uttar Pradesh. His electoral record and organisational experience are seen as key reasons behind his elevation. The Khatik community forms an important section of Uttar Pradesh’s Dalit electorate and has traditionally supported the BJP. Giving Singh a place in the national team signals the party’s intention to retain and strengthen its traditional Dalit support base. Sangeeta Yadav targets OBC and women voters Sangeeta Yadav, a Rajya Sabha member from the Gorakhpur region, is among the BJP’s prominent women and OBC leaders. Her organisational work and association with eastern Uttar Pradesh are believed to have contributed to her inclusion in the new team. Her elevation could help the BJP strengthen its outreach among women and OBC voters in eastern UP. Her Yadav background may also allow the party to signal a greater presence among a community traditionally associated with the Samajwadi Party. Amar Pal Maurya gets key OBC role Giving Amar Pal Maurya responsibility in the BJP’s OBC organisation is perhaps the clearest indication of the party’s 2027 strategy. The BJP’s success in Uttar Pradesh has been strongly linked to support from non-Yadav OBC groups, including Maurya, Kurmi, Saini, Lodhi, Nishad, Rajbhar, Pal and Prajapati communities. By elevating Maurya at the national level, the party appears to be positioning a leader who can help consolidate this wider social coalition. The appointment therefore appears to have a clear electoral dimension beyond routine organisational work. Kunwar Basit Ali to lead minority outreach Kunwar Basit Ali headed the Uttar Pradesh BJP Minority Morcha for nearly five years and remained active in strengthening the organisation. His organisational experience is believed to have helped him secure a larger national responsibility. By appointing him as national president of the Minority Morcha, the BJP could be looking to expand its reach among Muslim voters in western Uttar Pradesh, particularly Pasmanda Muslims and young voters. Even a small shift in Muslim voting patterns in Muslim-dominated constituencies could potentially affect the outcome of several Assembly seats. Nagendra Kumar’s influence in the new team Most of the Uttar Pradesh leaders included in Nitin Nabin’s new team are considered close to BJP national organisational secretary Nagendra Kumar. Kumar has previously served as the BJP’s state general secretary (organisation) in Uttar Pradesh and has extensive experience in the state. Sources indicate that his views were taken into account while deciding which leaders from Uttar Pradesh should be included in Nabin’s new team. Why were five senior leaders left out? Laxmikant Vajpayee Senior Brahmin leader Laxmikant Vajpayee is an experienced organisational figure. He was among the former Uttar Pradesh BJP presidents who met Nitin Nabin during his July visit to the state. His exclusion from the new national team does not necessarily mean the party is sidelining him. His experience could still be used during the Uttar Pradesh election campaign. Arun Singh Arun Singh served for a long period as BJP national general secretary and headquarters in-charge. He remained active in party affairs until June 2026. His exclusion from the new team is being viewed more as a change in responsibilities than as a decline in his influence or relevance within the party. Radha Mohan Das Agarwal Radha Mohan Das Agarwal has served as an MLA from Gorakhpur four times and is currently a Rajya Sabha member. His political relationship with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has also frequently been discussed. Given his experience and political influence, the BJP could still use him actively during the Uttar Pradesh election. Rajesh Agarwal Rajesh Agarwal served as the party’s treasurer in the previous national team but has not been included this time. The change is being seen as part of a broader organisational reshuffle. The BJP has frequently given new faces opportunities instead of retaining the same person in a position for a long period. Surendra Singh Nagar Surendra Singh Nagar served as a national secretary in the previous team and handled organisational responsibilities. In 2024, he was also appointed Bihar co-in-charge. His exclusion from the new team does not necessarily indicate the end of his role in the party. He could be given responsibility for a particular state or region during the election campaign. What does the reshuffle indicate? The BJP’s new Uttar Pradesh team combines caste representation, regional balance, women’s outreach, OBC consolidation and efforts to expand its presence among Muslim voters. With the 2027 Assembly election approaching, the reshuffle appears to be less about simply replacing old faces and more about positioning leaders who can contribute to the party’s electoral strategy in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Rain floods 5,000 homes in Prayagraj:Water rises up to 6 feet in several houses; residents ask, 'What will we eat, where will we go?'
stories.summary: Prayagraj received 90 mm of rain on Monday after showers began at 1 am on Sunday and continued until Monday afternoon. The heavy rain caused waterlogging of up to 4 feet in more than 5,000 houses. Residents in low-lying areas were forced to move to upper floors or rooftops, while refrigerators, sofas, beds and other household items were submerged. Cars and two-wheelers parked in the Kareli area were also submerged. Around 200 cars in Kareli alone were pushed or towed to garages using tow chains by the evening. More than 1,000 bikes and scooters were also submerged and became unusable. Residents told Dainik Bhaskar about the difficulties they were facing. Usha Devi, a resident of Mundera, said, “There is water everywhere in our house. There are small children at home. Because of the waterlogging, even getting food and drinking water has become difficult. We do not know what to eat or where to go.” In Mundera, children held pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and demanded a solution to the waterlogging problem. One child said they were unable to go to school. The washrooms were submerged, and sewers were overflowing. 3 pictures of the flood situation Read people's conversations Waterlogging from Solah Market to Naini The situation is also severe in several areas, including Solah Market, B Block, Gaus Nagar, Shams Nagar, JK Nagar, Gaddha Colony, Islam Nagar in Kareli, Chakdaudi, Chak Faizullah, Punjabi Hata, Yamunanagar in Naini, Tagore Town and Civil Lines. Along with rainwater, dirty water from major drains has entered homes, leaving residents struggling with severe waterlogging. The situation has raised questions over the effectiveness of the work carried out after around Rs 7,500 crore was spent to develop Prayagraj as a Smart City ahead of the Mahakumbh. Rahul Yadav: Drainage line not linked to main sewer Rahul Yadav of Mundera said the area's drainage line was never connected to the main sewer line further ahead. He said the severe waterlogging could have been avoided if the connection had been completed on time. He accused Municipal Corporation officials and sewer contractors of negligence. Yadav said the problem was reported around six months ago to former minister Siddharth Nath Singh, Mayor Ganesh Kesarwani and councillor Shiv Kumar through IGRS and speed post. However, he said, no work had been carried out on the ground despite repeated assurances. Bachcha Kumar: Complaints yield no result Bachcha Kumar of Mundera said around 1,000 people live in a settlement in Ward No. 18, which gets submerged whenever it rains. He alleged that instead of properly connecting the sewer line to the drainage system, a 10-inch pipe was installed merely as a formality. As a result, rainwater and sewage enter people's homes and even kitchens. Residents have been writing to the Municipal Commissioner, District Magistrate, Mayor Ganesh Kesarwani, local MLA Siddharth Nath Singh and the councillor for the past six months. They have also met officials in person, but no solution has been found. He said residents have been given assurances about tenders for road and drain construction for the past five years. Meanwhile, waterlogging has become so severe that people are unable to cook food in their homes. Khursheed: Councillors must act Khursheed of Kareli said around six feet of water flooded the area and entered people's homes, damaging refrigerators, televisions and other household items. Residents managed to drain the water themselves, but no responsible official reached the spot. He said garbage blocking the drains was also preventing the water from flowing out. According to him, Municipal Corporation officials cannot know the problems of every street, making it the councillors' responsibility to report such issues and ensure they are resolved. Vinod: When will it be fixed? Vinod of George Town said the same problem occurs whenever it rains. He questioned when the waterlogging problem would finally be resolved and said no new sewer-cleaning work had been carried out in the area for a long time. He said the main reason for the waterlogging was that the drains and sewer lines in the area were completely blocked. With the drainage system unable to carry water away, it remains on roads and in low-lying areas. ₹7500 crore received for the development of the city during Mahakumbh In the name of making Prayagraj a smart city, crores of rupees were spent on paper in the last few years. But, you can see what the situation became with just 90 mm of rain. During Mahakumbh, Prayagraj was given 7500 crore rupees. Out of this, ₹5500 crore were used to build roads, sewer lines, drinking water projects, and large bridges across the city. The Municipal Corporation received 1636 crore rupees for urban systems and city management. The work of digging up the city's main roads and alleys to lay sewer lines has been going on for several years. For this purpose, the National Mission for Clean Ganga's Ganga Pollution Control Unit Division was established. Wherever this unit laid sewer lines in the city, even after the construction work was completed, the roads caved in, and the ground's structure weakened. Crores of rupees were spent in the name of laying sewer and drainage lines. The situation is such that wherever sewer line work was done, the problem of waterlogging during rains became even worse. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav wrote on social media X- It is taught in history that cities and civilizations developed along river banks. In UP's BJP rule, this picture could be of any city. There is a major city in UP where the mismanagement of drainage due to corruption has become so infamous that roads turn into rivers every other day. That city has become a model of such mismanagement.At a factual level, this is described as 'George Town', the most affluent area of Smart City Prayagraj, where even the police station is submerged. The people of the country are asking whether this area falls under the BJP MLA from City North, or if it has flowed into the assembly constituency of the BJP MLA from City South. By the way, it is heard that a scam of 1 lakh crore rupees has occurred in the development of Prayagraj during BJP rule.

Pickup collides with truck in MP’s Bhind, 8 killed:23 injured, were returning to UP from Gwalior; crash occurs while avoiding cattle on highway
stories.summary: Eight labourers were killed and 23 others, including the driver, were injured after a speeding pickup truck collided head-on with a lorry on National Highway-719 in Bhind late on Monday night. The accident occurred around 1am near Chhimka village in Gohad as the labourers were returning to Lakhimpur Kheri in Uttar Pradesh after completing paddy transplantation work in Gwalior. Five bodies have been kept in Gohad and three in Gwalior. Six victims have been identified, while two remain unidentified. There were 29 labourers travelling in the pickup. Initial reports had put the toll at four deaths and 25 injuries. Gohad Chauraha police reached the spot after the accident and, with help from local residents, rescued the injured and took them to hospital. Five of the victims’ bodies have been kept in Gohad and three in Gwalior. Identification of the deceased is under way. The lorry driver was also injured, while some seriously injured victims have reportedly been referred for further treatment. Pictures from the accident site Pickup swerves to avoid cattle Gohad Chauraha police station in-charge Ramnaresh Yadav said the pickup was estimated to be travelling at around 80-90 kmph. According to the preliminary investigation, several cows were sitting on the highway near Chhimka village. When the cattle suddenly appeared in front of the vehicle, the driver tried to swerve to avoid them. The pickup then collided with the oncoming lorry. The impact was so severe that the pickup was badly damaged and several labourers suffered serious injuries. Police and local residents helped pull the injured passengers out of the wreckage before taking them to hospital. Labourers were returning after paddy work Yadav said the labourers had travelled to the Gwalior area for paddy transplantation work. After completing the work, they were returning to their villages in Lakhimpur Kheri when the pickup crashed near Chhimka during the overnight journey. Cattle pose accident risk on highway The preliminary investigation suggests that the attempt to avoid cattle sitting on the road was the main cause of the crash. Police said the risk of accidents increases when cattle suddenly appear in front of vehicles travelling at high speed at night. Traffic on the highway was disrupted for some time after the crash. Police later removed the damaged vehicles from the road and restored normal traffic.

stories.title: Bank manager wife killed in Lucknow:SBI officer husband beats her at office gate, shoots her in forehead when employees rush over
stories.summary: Dainik Bhaskar has obtained exclusive CCTV footage of the murder of Divya Mishra, a relationship manager at ICICI Bank in Lucknow. In the footage, Divya is seen entering the bank. Her husband, Manas Bajpai, stops her at the gate. An argument ensues between them. Then Manas starts beating Divya. Seeing the assault, the bank guards and employees rushed to save Divya. Meanwhile, Manas shot Divya in the forehead. As soon as the shot was fired, the guards and employees backed away. After this, Manas ran towards his house. He reached his house, 2 km away, where he also murdered his sister Sheeba and finally shot himself. See 2 pictures Shot amidst the crowd Most of the CCTV cameras installed in the bank are angled inwards. One CCTV camera is angled outwards. The incident has been captured in it. It is visible that vehicles are coming and going outside the bank. There is a crowd on the road. Manas commits the crime without caring about any of this. According to CCTV, Divya is entering the bank at 12:20 PM on Thursday. Manas stops her outside the bank and beats her. Within 1 minute, he shoots her and flees. After he leaves, the bank guards and other employees reach Divya. After killing his wife, he killed his sister and then committed suicide. After killing Divya, Manas reaches his house in Husadiya around 12:30 PM. According to eyewitnesses, Manas was drenched in sweat. After going inside, he first closes the room door. Then he plays Hanuman Chalisa loudly on the TV. After this, he shoots and kills his sister Sheeba. Then he shoots himself and commits suicide.
