stories.title: Free 3 days bus travel for women on Raksha Bandhan:Male companions to also get discount; Yogi tells private operators not to overcharge
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government has announced free bus travel for women in Uttar Pradesh during Raksha Bandhan. Women will be able to travel free of cost on state-run roadways buses from 6am on August 27 to midnight on August 29. Each woman passenger can also travel with one companion free of charge. The facility will also be available on more than 900 buses operated by the Urban Development Department. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath issued the directions during a meeting with officials on Sunday to review transport and traffic arrangements for Raksha Bandhan. CM says, Raksha Bandhan is on August 28. A large number of women will travel to their maternal homes during the festival. In view of this, women and one companion will be allowed to travel free of cost on UP Roadways buses. Additional buses will also be operated. The CM has directed officials in all districts to hold meetings with bus, taxi and auto-tempo unions by August 25. He said private vehicles must not charge arbitrary fares and passengers should be charged only the prescribed fare. Strict action will be taken against overloading, overcharging and misbehaviour with passengers. Taxi and e-rickshaw drivers will also be verified. Dainik Bhaskar had already revealed this 11 days ago. Extra buses to run as women travel home for Raksha Bandhan Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on August 28, and a large number of women are expected to travel to their parental homes and return during the festival. The Chief Minister directed officials to operate additional buses to meet the expected rush. He also asked officials to hold meetings with bus, taxi and auto-rickshaw unions in all districts by August 25. Transport operators have been instructed to charge only the prescribed fares, while action will be taken against overloading, overcharging and misbehaviour with passengers. Taxi and e-rickshaw drivers will also undergo verification. UP Roadways to run additional buses from August 26 to 31 Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh has directed officials to operate additional buses from August 26 to 31 to ensure smooth travel during Raksha Bandhan. All buses of the state transport corporation will remain operational during this period to manage the expected passenger rush. Officials have also been instructed to ensure cleanliness and adequate drinking water at all bus stations. Better lighting and fan arrangements will be made in waiting rooms, while a 24-hour control room will remain operational throughout the period. Restrictions to be relaxed on select routes during festival rush Transport Corporation MD Prabhu N Singh said, “Restrictions on buses travelling from Delhi towards Ghaziabad, Meerut and Moradabad via Moradabad-Bareilly would be relaxed. Similarly, restrictions on routes from Delhi towards Ghaziabad, Agra and Etawah via Aligarh-Kanpur would also be eased.” He added, “Additional buses will also be deployed for western Uttar Pradesh routes if passenger occupancy reaches 60% at the originating point.” Raksha Bandhan: Roadways employees’ leave cancelled Transport Corporation MD Prabhu N. Singh said restrictions on buses operating from Delhi to Ghaziabad, Meerut and Moradabad via Muradabad-Bareilly will be reduced. Similarly, restrictions on buses running from Delhi to Ghaziabad, Agra and Etawah via Aligarh-Kanpur will also be relaxed. If buses have 60% passengers at the originating point for routes to western UP, additional buses will be operated. No leave for Roadways staff for six days Except in special circumstances such as the death of a family member or personal illness, officials, supervisors, drivers and conductors involved in bus operations will not be granted leave. Officials deployed during the festival will not be allowed to remain absent from their workplace without permission. Violators will face disciplinary action. Employees completing the target will get a bonus MD Prabhu N. Singh said drivers and conductors who complete 1,800 km of bus operations during the six-day festival period will receive an incentive of ₹1,200. Contract drivers and conductors will get an additional 55 paise per kilometre for operating buses beyond 1,800 km during this period. Technical staff who remain present every day at depots and regional workshops during the festival period will receive an incentive of ₹500. Raksha Bandhan to be celebrated on August 28 Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on August 28 this year. According to the information provided, the festival will be observed without the Bhadra period, allowing sisters to tie rakhi throughout the day. The full moon period will begin at 8.31am on August 27 and continue until 9.18am on August 28. Rakhi can be tied during this period.

stories.title: Fish served at Ajay Rai’s conference in Ayodhya:BJP MLA calls it an insult to Sanatan, organiser says, 'Constitution was followed'
stories.summary: UP Congress President Ajay Rai reached Ayodhya on Sunday. Here, he recited the Hanuman Chalisa at Hanumangarhi. Then he visited Ramlala. After this, Ajay Rai participated in the Congress workers' conference held at Tarun Bazar in the Goshainganj assembly constituency. This is about 38 kilometers away from Hanumangarhi. A fish feast was organized at this conference. This conference was organized by Ram Nihal Nishad, who recently joined Congress from BJP. He said - It is not written anywhere in the Constitution that fish should not be eaten in Sawan. We are following the Constitution. On the other hand, BJP MLA Ved Prakash Gupta said- During the month of Sawan, crores of Sanatanis are engrossed in the worship of Lord Shiva. At that time, consuming fish is an open display of Congress's anti-Sanatan mindset. Congress should understand that the faith of the Sanatan society is not a political laboratory. Visiting Ayodhya, bowing down in temples, and then consuming fish exposes the dual character of Congress. The public will respond to those who toy with Sanatan faith. Earlier, on 11 August, Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad in the UP government had called fish vegetarian. He had said - fish prepared without garlic and onion is vegetarian. The emblem of the UP government and the Constitution of India features fish, arrow, and bow. This is the symbol of the Nishad community, of which we are proud. Ram Nihal said, ‘Both types of food were prepared’ Ram Nihal Nishad was the president of the BJP's executive committee. On 23 June, he had joined the Congress. This was his first program after joining the Congress. He is claiming a ticket from the Congress for the Gosaiganj assembly seat. Ram Nihal Nishad informed that two types of food were prepared at the conference held at Arpit Marriage Lawn in Tarun development block. Besides fish, there was also vegetarian food. UP BJP chief says, ‘Insulting Sanatan is Congress’s identity’ UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary criticised the alleged fish feast organised during the welcome of the Uttar Pradesh Congress president in Ayodhya, calling it “condemnable and unforgivable.” He accused Congress of repeatedly hurting the religious beliefs and sentiments of Sanatan followers for “vote-bank politics” and said the event during Sawan showed disrespect for Ayodhya’s sanctity, Kanwariyas and saints. BJP Mahanagar president Kamlesh Srivastava also condemned the event, saying it insulted Sanatan traditions and devotees’ sentiments. He demanded that Congress apologise publicly and stop its “appeasement politics.” He said that the people of Ayodhya will never accept such a mockery of religious sentiments. Meanwhile, BJP District President Radheshyam Tyagi said that Ajay Rai has come to Ayodhya in the holy month of Sawan to visit temples. However, a fish feast was organized at the conference he attended. Former Mayor said - Hurt Hindu sentiments Former Mayor Hrishikesh Upadhyay also accused Congress of being anti-Sanatan. He said - Congress does not even celebrate Hindu festivals. They were calling Lord Ram imaginary; now they come to visit the Ram temple. After this, they hold a Congress conference. Then they work to hurt the sentiments of Hindus. Meanwhile, Congress District President Chetanarayan Singh said- I don't know about the fish feast incident. We went with President Ajay Rai. We came back with him. If that's the case, Ram Nihal Nishad should not have done that. Now read 5 important things said by Ajay Rai at the conference

stories.title: Manoj Tiwari’s brother's last rites performed at Manikarnika Ghat:MP carried his bier, died at AIIMS
stories.summary: Sadhu Sharan Tiwari, elder brother of BJP MP and Bhojpuri actor-singer Manoj Tiwari, passed away on Saturday. He breathed his last at AIIMS, New Delhi, at 1:15 PM. Sadhu Sharan, affectionately called 'Sadhu Bhaiya' by the family, was the eldest of four brothers and one sister. His last rites were performed on Sunday at 5 PM at Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi. Manoj Tiwari also walked on foot during his brother's final journey. Sadhu Sharan Tiwari had retired from the post of General Manager at ONGC. He served in several places, including Kolkata, Nazira-Sivasagar in Assam, and Mumbai. After retirement, he was living at his residence in Chitaipur, Varanasi. Manoj Tiwari described his elder brother as the guardian of the family and his source of inspiration. He said that Sadhu Sharan played a crucial role in advancing his singing career. Journey from IIT-BHU Engineering to GM at ONGC Sadhu Sharan Tiwari was also very good at studies. He obtained an engineering degree from IIT BHU. After this, he started working at Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC). During his job, he worked at various places, including Kolkata, Nazira-Sivasagar in Assam, and Mumbai. After serving for a long time, he retired from the post of General Manager (GM). After retirement, he made Varanasi his home and started living in his house located in Chitaipur. Manoj Tiwari said, ‘He was like a God’ Manoj Tiwari described his elder brother as the guardian and guide of the family. He said that Sadhu Sharan was like God to him. In the family too, his position was that of the eldest member and guide. He also made a significant contribution to Manoj Tiwari's musical journey. He encouraged his younger brother to progress in the field of singing and guided him at every step. According to Manoj Tiwari, Sadhu Sharan inspired him to move forward on the path to success. Recited a poem at the last meeting Manoj Tiwari also recalled his last meeting with his elder brother. He said that Sadhu Sharan's nature was such that he would explain something to him in every meeting. In their last meeting too, he had recited a poem to Manoj Tiwari. At that time, the MP had no idea that this would be his last meeting with his brother. Last rites performed at Manikarnika Ghat After his demise at AIIMS in Delhi on Saturday, Sadhu Sharan Tiwari's body was brought to Varanasi. The last rites were performed at Manikarnika Ghat on Sunday around 5 PM. Manoj Tiwari also participated in the final journey along with family members and close relatives. The MP walked on foot in his elder brother's funeral procession. During this time, there was an atmosphere of mourning among family and acquaintances.

stories.title: Wife slashes husband from chest to private parts:Removes intestines and stuffs them in a sack; half liver and kidney missing
stories.summary: A woman murdered her husband in Kurukshetra, Haryana, cutting him from the chest to the private parts with a sharp weapon. She removed his intestines and put them in a plastic sack. While she was carrying out the crime, the landlord arrived. On seeing him, she jumped from the roof and was later admitted to hospital. The incident took place on Saturday, while photos related to the case surfaced on Sunday. The postmortem also revealed that about half the liver and the right kidney were missing from the deceased's body. The police are now investigating the case of missing organs from the body along with the reason for the murder. It has also come to light that the woman used to practice witchcraft. Living in a rented house for one year The deceased has been identified as Rajesh (40), a resident of Dhampur village in Sitapur district of Uttar Pradesh. He had been living for the past one year in Kurukshetra in a rented house near Raj Palace on Pehowa Road with his wife, Vimala Devi. He worked in water supply at PB RO Water Trading Company located on Pehowa Road. Landlord said - Saw her putting intestines in a sack Landlord Rinku said that on Saturday around 5 pm, he heard Rajesh and Vimla screaming from the room. When he reached the terrace, Rajesh was lying drenched in blood with deep wounds on his stomach. He saw that Vimla was putting Rajesh's intestines, which had come out of his stomach, into a sack. Rinku said that, seeing him, Vimla got nervous and jumped down from the terrace. She got injured from the fall. The police team has found three knives of different sizes at the spot. They had no children after marriage According to the landlord, Vimla also practiced witchcraft, and there were frequent disputes between the husband and wife. They had been married for several years and had no children. However, the real reason for the murder is not yet clear. Forensic expert said - There was a 37-centimeter-long wound Forensic expert Dr. Gaurav Kaushik said that when the body came to him, it did not have half a liver and one kidney. There was a 37-centimeter-long and deep incision on the deceased's stomach. The intestines were protruding from the incision. It is the police's responsibility to recover the deceased's half liver and one kidney. Woman will be questioned after treatment KUK police station in-charge Surendra Sandhu says that after the postmortem, the body has been handed over to the family members. The accused woman is currently undergoing treatment. Once her condition improves, she will be arrested and interrogated.

stories.title: 4 arrested in ₹1.16 billion cyber fraud case:143 NCRP complaints linked to 41 bank accounts; fake firms used to commit fraud
stories.summary: Varanasi's Cyber Crime Police and Chetganj Police have arrested four notorious cyber criminals. Of the four arrested criminals, one is from Sasaram in Bihar, and three are residents of Varanasi. All were involved in cyber crimes worth ₹1 billion 4 crore and were providing accounts and their details to cyber criminals sitting far away by creating fake firms. 143 NCRP complaints have been registered against 41 bank accounts found with them. Currently, police have sent all of them to jail in a case registered at Chetganj police station. After police interrogation, two other criminals, Prateek Tiwari alias Bunty and Romil Verma, are being searched for. See pictures... Arrested from Karaundi area ACP Crime Vinay Dwivedi informed that a case was registered at Chetganj police station, in which information about cyber fraud was given. Based on this case, the cyber crime team and Chetganj police station personnel were searching for the criminals. In this sequence, police received information that some suspicious persons of criminal nature were present near Vivekanandpuri Colony, Karaundi. Acting on this, police conducted a raid and arrested them. The criminals arrested on the spot gave their names as Nitish Kumar Pandey, Dushyant Singh, Himanshu Jha and Rehan. Fraud was being committed in the name of fake firm In this regard, ACP Crime Vinay Dwivedi informed - A special campaign is being run against cyber criminals. Today, on Sunday, the cyber crime team and Chetganj police station have nabbed a gang. This gang was opening bank accounts by creating fake firms in the names of people from Banaras and those coming from outside, luring them with commission. They kept all the details of the accounts that were opened. Through these, all the cyber frauds that are committed through gaming and other methods, the money would come into these accounts. Fraud of more than ₹1 billion 16 crores The ACP further informed - Among the arrested criminals, one Nitish Kumar Pandey, resident of Deehi, Shivsagar police station, Rohtas, Sasaram, who was currently residing in Vivekanandpuri Colony, Chitaipur, revealed - He used to provide all these accounts to the cyber criminals sitting above, and they would send the cyber fraud money into these. A total transaction of ₹1,168,658,321 has taken place in these 41 accounts, on which NCRP complaints have been filed. Sent to jail The ACP informed that, among all these criminals, criminal records have been found against Nitish Kumar Pandey. Criminal records of others are also being searched.

stories.summary: A female police officer in Meerut, Anu Collis, who was suspended 7 days ago over an objectionable reel, went live on YouTube for the first time on Saturday. She responded to the influencer Amit Kilhor, who had first made her video go viral. Anu said, ''I have been locked in a room for many days. I feel like ending my life, such thoughts are coming to my mind. You know how difficult it is to get a government job.'' Anu was wearing the same dress in which her video had gone viral. She said, ''Amit Kilhor has now deleted that video from his social media account. Now he is apologizing to my brother.'' First, know about Anu... Anu Collis is a UP Police Sub-Inspector from the 2023 batch. She is originally from Prayagraj. In Meerut, she was first posted at Rohta police station, Brahmpuri, and was later posted at the SSP office. On 16 August, 2026 (Sunday), she was suspended with immediate effect on the orders of the then SSP Avinash Pandey in a case of violation of police conduct rules and an alleged objectionable video going viral. Influencer Amit Kilhor had trolled her by sharing a video. He wrote, ''Anu Collis makes her obscene videos by putting QR codes, goes live. She takes funding. After the video went viral, an investigation was launched against Anu. SP Crime Avanish Kumar is investigating this.'' Now read what lady constable Anu said, read verbatim... ''My name is Anu Collis. You may have seen one of my videos on social media. An influencer, Amit Kilhor, shared the video on his Instagram account and tagged the Uttar Pradesh DGP, Chief Minister, my department, and several others. I want to ask Amit Kilhor: Why did you take my personal photos and videos from my social media accounts and share them without my permission? Did you ever ask for my consent? By sharing my personal content without permission, you committed a cybercrime. Why did you delete the video later? You are now calling my brother and apologising, saying it was a mistake. You have ruined my life and destroyed everything I worked for. My 20–25 years of hard work, career, and future have been affected. I have been completely defamed. I was accused of making obscene videos and content. What exactly did you find obscene about my content? What was your problem with it? I am coming live today because no one took my side. My brother put forth his point, but not many people saw it. Obviously, in today's world, who watches what boys have to say? Amit bhaiya, I want to ask you something. If you were so concerned about my department or about me, and you thought I was doing something obscene, then why didn't you file a complaint? You had my number. Why didn't you complain to my department? You could have filed an FIR against me or complained to my department. Why didn't you tell my SSP sir, whom you know very well and for whom you gave a long lecture? What was the problem in doing that? Were you getting fewer views? You took my photo without my permission and put it on your channel just for views.'' This is the frock whose screenshot was taken ''Amit bhaiya, this is the same frock whose screenshot you took. Take the screenshot now. Everyone, take its screenshot and upload it, saying Anu Rani's another obscene video has gone viral. You want to earn views. I bought this frock with my mom from a mall in Agra. My mom liked it a lot. You can see this frock. It is a normal and beautiful frock. My name is Anu Collis. My nickname is Selina. I am an Anglo-Indian girl and Roman Catholic. Wearing such clothes is normal in my house. My parents have no problem, and my brother also has no problem. We wear such clothes here. If you have a problem, then don't watch. Amit bhaiya, what did you gain by ruining my life? I have been in a closed room for five days and am very distressed. I am having thoughts of harming myself. I am receiving death threats. My family is being spoken about inappropriately. Wrong things are being said about my brother too. My mother is very simple, and she is also having to hear a lot.'' You made a video just for views ‘’It is being said that I do sex chat. Does YouTube promote sex chat? If it does, then I am saying that this is my name, and I stand by my words. I am giving it in writing that I will not resign. You can take my screenshot and send it to my department, the cyber police station, or my SSP sir. Send it to whoever you want to send it to.'' Senior Inspector said - You have defamed the department Anu said that today I went to my office. There, I met a very senior inspector whom I respect a lot. But he told me, "You have defamed the department." He said this, even though someone had created a video of him and made it viral using AI. How many people will I have to explain that I am right and that wrong has been done to me? I am silent; it doesn't mean that I am wrong. stories.title: Symbolic funeral procession of upper-caste MPs and MLAs held:Over 300 people take to streets and call themselves ‘constitutional untouchables’
stories.summary: Brahmins and Thakurs associated with the Savarna (upper- caste) Morcha organization staged a strong protest on Sunday in Lucknow. People from other categories also joined them. More than 300 people gathered at Women Power Line intersection around 12 PM and started chanting slogans for UGC rollback. They held placards that read 'Constitutional Untouchables'. After protesting for half an hour at the intersection, they started moving towards Baikunth Dham cremation ground. When such a large crowd took to the streets, all three roads leading from Women Power Line intersection towards Baikunth Dham, Hazratganj, and VIP Guest House were jammed. The protesters also took out a symbolic funeral procession for the Savarna MPs and MLAs. When they reached Baikunth Dham cremation ground, they sat there and chanted 'Hi-Hi' (slogans of condemnation). The protesters said that 'we are constitutional untouchables'. We have been kept away from our interests. Paths are being closed for future generations as well. Only when the UGC chapter is completely closed, and reservation is abolished, should Modiji dream of 2029. During the symbolic funeral procession of upper-caste MPs and MLAs, protesters chanted slogans: ‘He is dead, brother, he is dead, our leader is dead.’ Police from 5 police stations were deployed during the protest. Protesters were detained near Baikunth Dham and sent to Eco Garden. These people had arrived to protest at the invitation of Sandeep Singh, president of Savarna Morcha. See 5 pictures- After walking some distance, people took out a symbolic funeral procession for the upper-caste MPs and MLAs.

stories.title: 60 extra buses to run in Gorakhpur for Raksha Bandhan:Services to increase from 26 August, women and one companion to travel free from 27 Aug night
stories.summary: 60 additional buses will be run in Gorakhpur Local. In view of the possibility of an increase in the number of passengers on Rakshabandhan in Gorakhpur, the roadways have intensified preparations. Bus frequencies will also be increased from 26 August. The focus will be mainly on the Gorakhpur to Lucknow, Varanasi, Deoria, Basti, and Kushinagar routes. On the day of Rakshabandhan, women will get the facility of free travel in buses. From the night of 27 August to the night of 28 August, women will be able to travel in UP Roadways buses without fare. One co-passenger will also be given the facility of free travel with them. 60 additional buses, number will increase if needed On Raksha Bandhan, there is a possibility of an increase in passenger crowds at Gorakhpur bus stands. In view of this, the transport corporation has arranged additional buses. 60 additional buses will be run on different routes of Gorakhpur Local. From 26 August, the frequency of buses will also increase. If the number of passengers suddenly increases on any route, an additional bus will be sent there immediately. More pressure on Lucknow-Varanasi route The number of passengers is high on routes from Gorakhpur to Lucknow, Varanasi, Deoria, Basti, and Kushinagar. On Raksha Bandhan, the pressure on these routes is expected to increase further. Therefore, along with increasing the availability of buses on these routes, their frequency will also be increased. Free travel for women from the night of 27th On Rakshabandhan, women will get the facility of free bus travel for 24 hours. From the night of 27 August to the night of 28 August, women passengers will be able to travel without fare. One co-passenger will also be able to travel for free with them. Before and after this period, normal fare will apply. All depots alert, focus on security too RM Love Kumar Singh informed that all depots have been alerted regarding Rakshabandhan. Additional buses will be deployed on the spot according to the number of passengers. Special attention will also be given to the safety and convenience of women, so that passengers do not face any kind of problem during the festival.

stories.title: Gorakhpur man attempts suicide by jumping into Rapti:PAC team rescues him within minutes, hands him to police
stories.summary: On Sunday morning, a young man allegedly jumped into the Rapti river in Gorakhpur in an apparent suicide attempt. Within seconds, he began drowning in the deep water, triggering panic at the spot. However, a flood relief team from the 26th Battalion PAC, stationed nearby, immediately launched a rescue operation and pulled him to safety. The incident took place at Ramghat in the Nausad area. A major tragedy was averted because of the team’s quick response and presence of mind. Twenty-five-year-old Laddu Manjhi, a resident of the Majhaulia police station area, reached Ramghat at around 9 am and jumped into the river without telling anyone. The strong current and depth of the river quickly left him struggling in the water. The situation turned critical before people nearby could react. Rescue operation launched by motorboat Seeing the young man drowning, people at the ghat raised an alarm and immediately alerted the PAC team stationed nearby. All eyes turned towards the river as people feared for his life. The B Team of the 26th Battalion PAC, deployed at Ramghat for flood relief operations, immediately sprang into action. Under the leadership of team leader Rana Pratap Chauhan, the jawans boarded a motorboat and entered the river. Despite the strong current and depth, the team reached the young man within minutes and pulled him out of the water. Young man handed over to police After the rescue, the young man was brought safely to the riverbank and given first aid. He was later handed over to the local police. According to police, Manjhi is a resident of West Champaran in Bihar and had been under stress for some time. Police said he jumped into the river after becoming distressed. He is currently safe, and his condition is reported to be normal. The PAC personnel were praised for their courage and quick response. Team leader Rana Pratap Chauhan said the jawans took the right decision at the right time, helping save a life. Head Constable Baldev Prasad and Constables Jitendra Kumar, Ravi Gautam, Vikas Jaiswal and Ravindra Paswan were part of the rescue operation. The operation was successfully completed through the combined efforts of the team.

stories.title: Medical Representative burnt alive inside Wagon-R:Driving seat turned into pyre, short circuit locked doors; man was on his way to meet his mother
stories.summary: A 50-year-old man was burnt alive after his Wagon-R caught fire in Barabanki on Sunday morning. The incident occurred around 10.30 am when the car suddenly caught fire and quickly turned into a ball of flames. All four doors became locked. Rajanarayan Verma, who was sitting in the driver’s seat, became trapped inside. He tried to open the door but could not escape. Villagers rushed to the spot after seeing the flames but were unable to approach the burning car. They alerted police and the fire brigade and tried to douse the flames with water. By the time the teams arrived, the fire had been brought under control. The car door was broken open, and Rajanarayan’s badly burnt body was found stuck to the seat. The body was recovered and sent for post-mortem. Police said the car was a petrol variant and the initial investigation suggests a short circuit caused the fire. The vehicle has been seized. The incident took place in the Safdarganj police station area, around 15km from the district headquarters on the Barabanki-Ayodhya road. See the horrific pictures On his way to meet mother, man died just 2km from home Rajanarayan Verma worked as a stamp vendor at the Barabanki registry office. He was originally from Bariyarpur village and lived with his wife in a house in the Vijaynagar area of the city. His daughter is married, while his son lives in Andhra Pradesh and is doing B.Tech. Rajanarayan’s parents, Mewa Lal Verma and Babita Verma, lived in the village. His brother, Jung Bahadur Verma, worked in property dealing in the city, and Rajanarayan also worked with him. Earlier, he had worked as a medical representative (MR) for 10 years. According to the family, Rajanarayan attended a relative’s event on Saturday night. On Sunday morning, he left for Bariyarpur village in his Wagon-R (UP 41 R 8292). He turned towards the Bhaudra road in the Safdarganj area from the Barabanki-Ayodhya road. When he reached a canal just 2km from home, smoke suddenly started coming from inside the car. Within moments, the vehicle caught fire. Safdarganj police station in-charge Amar Chaurasia said- Information was received about a car catching fire. The police team reached the spot and took possession of the body and sent it for post-mortem. Initial investigation revealed that the fire was caused by a short circuit in the wiring. Police are investigating the circumstances of the accident and the actual causes of the fire.

stories.title: Lucknow murder case:Divya’s YouTuber sister lashes out at police, asks where Manas got 3 weapons, says mafia rule is better than such policing
stories.summary: In the Lucknow murder case, Pragya Mishra, the YouTuber sister of ICICI Bank relationship manager Divya, has questioned the police investigation. She said a bank employee was allegedly planning murders with three weapons, yet Lucknow Police had no clue about it. She said such policing was worse than the mafia era, when people at least knew whom to be wary of. Late on Sunday night, Pragya posted more than 25 questions on X. She said that if an ordinary bank employee could get access to three firearms, including two pistols and a country-made pistol, Lucknow residents needed to remain alert. According to the family, Manas was timid and could not even kill an ant. There was not even a strong stick at his home. Pragya questioned how the three weapons reached him and who trained or provoked him to commit such a heinous crime. She said the truth must come out and demanded that the case be handed over to another agency. She also sought justice for her sister Divya and Shiba. Manas's maternal uncle Avdhesh Shukla also described him as timid. He said Manas would hesitate to even leave the house alone at night and that the family had no weapons beforehand. The family therefore had no information about where he obtained the three firearms. On August 20, SBI field officer Manas Bajpayee allegedly murdered his wife outside the bank. He then went home, where he allegedly killed his sister Shiba before taking his own life. Read Pragya's questions- Was the word 'cheat' written to mislead the police? Pragya questioned who was motivating him for this massacre? He couldn't bring all the necessary vegetables for cooking from the market at once. How did he get rare pistols? Which weapons were used in whose murder? The word 'cheat' was written in the final status. If Manas knew that Divya was cheating on him, then in the divorce case he would have gotten the upper hand by proving his wife characterless. Was the word 'cheat' written to mislead the police? Did someone take advantage of Manas's mental state? Did someone have their eye on the alleged ₹1.5 crore worth dowry present in Manas's house? Manas was a psycho. He was habituated to domestic violence, but showed civility in society. He couldn't kill an ant. In such a case, the murderer wouldn't have grown pistols and revolvers in the house. He must have brought them from somewhere. Manas didn't shoot any of the three from a distance. He shot everyone point-blank in the head. Was this a plan, or did Manas kill Divya? Did someone else kill Manas and Shiba? Where was Manas for 35-45 minutes after Divya's murder? Pragya said: The distance between the bank and home was 10-15 minutes. Where was Manas for 35-45 minutes after Divya's murder? This should be investigated. She asked whether Manas stopped somewhere on the way and, if he stopped, whom did he meet? Did he go to the coach? Demand for investigation into presence of third person in the house as well Pragya also questioned whether there was any third person present in Manas's house besides him. Was there any other way to enter and exit Manas's house? Which weapon was used to kill which person among the three weapons? The police should investigate these aspects. Until the source of the weapons, Manas's activities, and the role of people who were in contact with him are clear, the case should not be considered completely solved. Wrote - The claim of demanding ₹1.5 crore alimony is false Pragya wrote that a false claim was being circulated that Divya had demanded ₹1.5 crore in alimony from Manas. She clarified that alimony and ‘stridhan’ are different, with a woman having an absolute right over her stridhan. Stridhan refers to money, jewellery, gifts or other assets a woman receives before, during or after marriage that belong to her. Pragya said alimony is generally sought during or after divorce proceedings. In Divya’s case, the divorce petition had been filed less than a year earlier, and the legal process involves several stages before a divorce is finalised. Divya submitted bills and photos in the court case Divya's case had only reached Level 2 or 3, meaning mediation and counseling. There are also 6 rounds of counseling. In Divya's case, only one round had taken place. The talk of permanent alimony is just misinformation. Now let's come to ‘Stridhan’. ‘Stridhan’ refers to gifts received by the bride at the wedding or jewellery given to her. ‘Stridhan’ cannot simply be handed over. Evidence, such as photographs or bills, must be submitted in court to establish that the items belonged to the woman. Judges generally consider jewellery and other items visible in wedding photographs, along with any available purchase bills. Divya had submitted both bills and photographs. I do not know the exact amount of stridhan she had demanded. However, if the demand was for ₹1.5 crore, it indicates the substantial amount of stridhan Divya’s parents may have given her at the time of marriage. After marital separation, a husband cannot claim or retain his wife’s stridhan. Alimony, however, depends on the circumstances and the wife’s financial position. If the wife is financially independent, she may not be entitled to alimony. Divya was reportedly in a higher position than Manas and was financially stronger. Therefore, the reference to alimony appears to be an attempt to malign her. Friend revealed - Lawyer had provided the weapons Police are interrogating people who were in contact with Manas. During this, one of Manas's friends revealed that a lawyer from Sitapur had provided weapons to Manas. Manas and the lawyer had met during bank-related work. However, police have not confirmed the lawyer provided weapons. It should be noted that two 9mm pistols and one country-made pistol were found near Manas's dead body. Both pistols were loaded. The country-made pistol also had a cartridge. Police are investigating the serial numbers of the weapons, cartridges, and evidence related to firing. Locked iPhone hides many important clues Police have recovered Manas’s iPhone, but its data has not yet been accessed because the phone is locked. Investigators are seeking the password from his friends and relatives. DCP East Dr Diksha Sharma said forcibly unlocking the phone could risk data loss, so police are proceeding cautiously. Call records and mobile location data have already provided some key information. Police are verifying Manas’s movements on the day of the incident and identifying people he was in contact with. A list of those who spoke to him before the incident is also being prepared, and they will be questioned to piece together the sequence of events. No written complaint has been received so far. Police said all aspects will be investigated once the family submits a formal complaint. Questions raised about the last WhatsApp status too According to Pragya, after the murder of his wife Divya, a status appeared on Manas's WhatsApp. It mentioned killing his wife and then killing his sister before committing suicide. The status also mentioned that Pragya and Bharat were aware of the incident. Now Pragya has questioned whether this status was actually written by Manas. She says that Manas usually wrote in Hinglish, whereas this status was in English. The police should conduct a technical investigation to determine from which device and at what time the status was updated. 'Where was Manas for 35-45 minutes after Divya's murder?' Pragya also questioned the time Manas took to travel from the bank to his home. She said the journey normally takes 10–15 minutes, yet Manas took around 35–45 minutes after Divya’s murder. She asked where he spent that time, whether he stopped somewhere, whom he met, and whether he went to his alleged coach’s place. Pragya urged police to answer all these questions. She said if the source of the weapons remains unclear, the investigation should be handed over to another agency. According to her, Divya and Sheeba will get justice only when the complete truth emerges. Maternal uncle says, ‘Property will be donated if no one claims it’ Manas's maternal uncle Avdhesh Shukla said Manas's aunt and cousin Neha immersed the siblings' ashes in the Ganga in Kanpur. Manas owned a house near Husadiya Chowraha, while the family had no agricultural land. The house is currently sealed by police after the dispute. Shukla said they would have no objection if a close relative claimed the property through a court order. If no one comes forward and the property falls under their responsibility, they will donate it to a temple or trust. Manas lost both parents to illness Manas's father, RK Bajpayee, died of a heart attack, while his mother, Anju, later died of cancer. After their deaths, Manas took responsibility for his sister Sheeba, who the family said had mental health issues. Meanwhile, tensions had grown in Manas's married life, with an ongoing divorce case and increasing suspicion between the couple. Police are investigating whether these circumstances played a role in the tragedy. This is how the incident unfolded On August 20, SBI field officer Manas Bajpayee allegedly shot dead his wife Divya Mishra, an ICICI Bank relationship manager, outside her workplace before fleeing. Around 12.30 pm, he reached his house in Husaria, about 2km away, locked himself inside and allegedly shot his sister Sheeba before killing himself. Neighbours heard gunshots, broke open the door and found the siblings lying in a pool of blood. The incident occurred under the Gomtinagar police station limits. Police officers, forensic teams, and Police Commissioner Tarun Gaba reached the spot and began the investigation.

stories.title: Mayawati says, 'Demand for reservation on economic basis not right':Dalits have faced casteism for centuries, don’t protect reservation opponents
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati has lashed out at the demand for reservation based on economic criteria at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. She said on Sunday that Dalits have been victims of casteism for centuries. In such a situation, the demand for reservation based on economic criteria is not right. Targeting Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, Mayawati wrote on 'X': Rahul, who sat on dharna outside the police station in Delhi, did not go to get the anti-reservation protest happening at Jantar Mantar right next door stopped. He did not even try to go and explain to the protesters. This clearly exposes Congress's anti-reservation mentality. The BSP supremo appealed to the central and state governments not to give any kind of shelter or protection to anti-reservation elements. She told political parties that cheap politics should be stopped on sensitive and important issues like reservation. New demand for reservation based on economic grounds is not right at all Mayawati termed the demand for reservation based on economic grounds as anti-national and a blow to the spirit of the Constitution. She made it clear that Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST) and Other Backward Classes (OBC) have been harassed for centuries. Constitutional measures in the form of reservation were created to protect them from this casteist oppression. In such a situation, the new demand to implement reservation based on economic grounds is not appropriate at all. Baba Saheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar had said that 'renunciation of casteism is the greatest patriotism.' People not getting benefits is not due to reservation, but a result of corruption BSP supremo said - Every year, huge budgets are spent by governments to eradicate poverty. Not receiving its benefits is the result of government system failure and corruption, not reservation. The real benefit of economic reservation (EWS) implemented for poor families of general category is not reaching them; there is more deception in that too. Attempt to strengthen Dalit and deprived vote bank Political experts say that by opposing reservation on economic basis, Mayawati is trying to strengthen BSP's traditional Dalit and deprived vote bank. BSP's politics has long revolved around the issue of social justice and rights of deprived sections. At a time when protests took place at Delhi's Jantar Mantar demanding changes in the reservation system and reservation on an economic basis, Mayawati is trying to present herself as the strongest advocate of reservation and constitutional rights. Know about the 'Remove Reservation Movement'... It should be noted that a protest against reservation was held at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on Friday, 21 August. A large number of people gathered in the 'Remove Reservation Movement'. They demanded the implementation of reservation based on economic criteria while opposing the caste-based reservation system. The protesters also demanded changes in some UGC rules and the reservation system. Keeping the movement in view, Delhi Police made tight security arrangements. Some protesters were also taken into custody.

stories.title: UP cooks to get free treatment worth up to ₹5-lakh:₹1,000 for sarees, honorarium also raised by ₹1,000; Yogi's 4 big announcements
stories.summary: In Lucknow, CM Yogi announced to double the allowance for sarees, after increasing the honorarium of cooks who prepare mid-day meals by 1 thousand rupees. He said - now cooks will receive an honorarium of 3 thousand rupees per month. Instead of an annual allowance of 500 rupees for sarees, 1 thousand rupees will now be given. CM Yogi was addressing the felicitation ceremony of cooks associated with the PM Poshan Yojana on Sunday. At the event, he honored 11 cooks on stage. They were given a check for the increased honorarium, a cashless health card, and a safety kit. Around 1500 cooks from across the state were invited to the ceremony. In addition, felicitation ceremonies were also organized at the tehsil and district levels. A day before the event, the Yogi government had approved an increase of 1 thousand rupees in the honorarium of cooks preparing mid-day meals in schools. This decision, taken by cabinet by circulation, will benefit over 3 lakh 53 thousand cooks in UP. Cooks were currently receiving an honorarium of 2 thousand rupees per month, which has been increased to 3 thousand rupees. Additionally, 500 rupees for a saree and 400 rupees for gloves are given every year. In UP, there is a provision for 2 cooks for up to 25 children, 3 cooks for 26 to 100 children, and 4 cooks for 101 to 200 children. Information regarding arrangements related to bank and UPI QR codes was also provided at the ceremony. Cooks were also given head covers, gloves, and apron kits for hygiene and safety while preparing food. Our test is also coming, you have to vote by pressing the machine: Brajesh Pathak Addressing the felicitation ceremony, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, speaking in Awadhi, appealed to vote for BJP. He said, "Just as boys have exams and start studying, similarly, our exam is also coming. Now, what do you have to do in the exam... you have to press the voting machine. Just as you buy vegetables and pots after checking them thoroughly, similarly, compare in the elections too." He said, "Before 2017, there were goons in the villages. There was no electricity in the villages. Electricity used to come for one week during the day, and one week during the night. When relatives visited, a generator had to be run. But now, electricity is coming 24 hours a day. Now, if anyone looks at our sisters and daughters with ill intent, they will lose their lives, they won't be spared. stories.title: 2 girls drown friend to death at Mathura shelter home:Pretended to cry after killing her; said they wanted to go home
stories.summary: In Mathura’s Vrindavan, two teenage girls allegedly drowned their 14-year-old friend in the bathroom of a government girls’ home. Police said the two wanted to leave the shelter and believed that if a girl died there, the institution could be shut down and all the residents sent home. They allegedly planned the killing with this intention. After the incident, when police arrived, the accused girls allegedly pretended to cry and created a commotion. They also encouraged other girls to join them and raised slogans demanding justice for the deceased teenager. Attempts were also allegedly made to damage the CCTV cameras. Police managed to bring the situation under control. The post-mortem report was released on Saturday and confirmed that the teenager died by drowning. When police examined CCTV footage, they found that three girls had entered the bathroom, but only two came out around 45 minutes later. Based on this, police questioned the two girls, who allegedly confessed to the crime. The Government Girls’ Home is located in the Chaitanya Vihar area of Vrindavan and houses around 140 girls. Both accused teenagers are 15 years old, one is from Pilibhit and the other from Aligarh. Pragati Khare, superintendent of the Girls’ Home, has filed an FIR naming the two teenagers and three other girls allegedly involved in the conspiracy. Girls say they wanted to leave the shelter According to police sources, the two accused told investigators that they were unhappy at the shelter home and wanted to leave. They allegedly said someone had told them that if a girl died at the shelter, the institution could be shut down and all the girls sent back home. The two then allegedly conspired to kill their friend. On Saturday, when the teenager went to the bathroom, they followed her inside, drowned her and then came out. The incident came to light when another girl went to the bathroom a short while later and discovered what had happened. Officials at the girls’ home informed the police, who arrived and began questioning the residents. During this time, the girls allegedly created a commotion, claiming that the facilities at the home were poor and that the institution was unfit for living. They also threatened to protest if their friend did not get justice. Police pacified them and sent the body for post-mortem. SSP: Girls confessed after being shown CCTV footage The teenager’s post-mortem was conducted at the district hospital on Saturday. The SSP said police examined CCTV footage after the incident and found that the teenager’s room had an attached bathroom. The footage showed three girls entering the bathroom, while only two came out. When the two girls were questioned and shown the footage, they allegedly confessed to the killing, the SSP said. Shelter administration: Teenager was good at studies According to the State Girls’ Home administration, the girl’s father died shortly after her birth, while her mother suffered from a mental illness and later died. She was subsequently brought to the State Girls’ Protection Home. The administration said she was good at studies and keen to learn. Considering her conduct, the home authorities allowed her to attend school. She was studying at Sandipani Muni School and wanted to become financially independent through education.

stories.title: Assembly speaker Satish Mahana leaves midway through national anthem:Suddenly walks off stage, gets into car and leaves
stories.summary: UP Assembly Speaker Satish Mahana left the program in Unnao in the middle of the national anthem. On Saturday, he arrived as the chief guest at the session of the Principals' Council and the educational seminar. As per protocol, the police gave him a guard of honor. Immediately after this, the national anthem began. In the middle of the national anthem, Satish Mahana saluted and descended towards the back of the stage. During this, his supporters, who were standing some distance away, also reached him and started touching his feet. After this, Mahana got into the car and left. The whole incident is from a school in Pooran Nagar. Its video surfaced on Sunday. Program organizers told Dainik Bhaskar - The national anthem was playing quite far from where Satish Mahana was present. See 2 pictures- Stayed for 40 minutes at the event, said - if institutions are strong, the country will be strong Satish Mahana reached Aastha Auditorium of SVM Inter College around 4 PM on Saturday. He remained at the event for about 40 minutes. During this, the book 'Shiksha Prabha' was also released. Satish Mahana appealed to principals and academicians to honestly fulfill their responsibilities. He said that educational institutions are the foundation of the country's development. If the country's institutions are strong, the country will also be strong. He said that the amount given for the Ram Temple is a dedication at the feet of God. The talk of asking for it back is hurtful to the devotees. Congress leader asked - Is this not an insult to the national anthem? Dinesh Shukla, leader of Unnao Congress Committee, alleged that the Speaker of the Assembly took the guard of honor under protocol and left during the national anthem. He questioned - Is this not an insult to the national anthem? Had warned to resign in the monsoon session On August 5, during the monsoon session of the assembly, Satish Mahana had warned to resign. Regarding the uproar by the SP, he had said, There is pain in my heart. For the first time, I felt that either there was a shortcoming in our efforts somewhere, or Dr. Ambedkar's statement is correct that the shortcoming is not in the constitution, but in individuals. He had said, My long political innings is now in its final stage. I will have to seriously consider whether what I did in the last four and a half years was appropriate or inappropriate. I will also consider whether I am worthy of this chair or not, and will make a decision soon.

stories.title: Sanjay Nishad says he wants no assembly election seat:'Govt can take away my ministry, just give SC reservation to Nishads'
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government’s Cabinet Minister Dr Sanjay Nishad has adopted an all-or-nothing stance on the Nishad community’s demand for Scheduled Caste (SC) status. In an interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Nishad said that if the Nishad community is granted SC status, his party will not seek a single seat from the BJP in the 2027 Assembly elections. The Nishad Party, he said, will continue to remain with the BJP. Nishad claims that the Kewat, Mallah, Manjhi and Majhwar castes are already included in the SC list. However, he says they are being kept in the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category in Uttar Pradesh, denying them their constitutional rights. He says the demand is not new, but a fight to secure rights already guaranteed by the Constitution. Read the full interview You had said that you would resign as minister if reservation was not granted. What will be your next step? Sanjay Nishad: The government believes that by giving us a ministerial position, it has silenced us. But that is not the case. If the government wants, it can take back my ministry in exchange for reservation. We demand that our community be removed from the 9% OBC quota and included in the 9% SC quota, and that ‘Majhwar’ certificates be issued. If this happens, the Nishad Party will not ask the BJP for a single seat in the 2027 elections. We will campaign for the BJP across the state. What will you do if the Nishad community does not get SC reservation? Sanjay Nishad: In a democracy, it is not the power of the gun but the power of the vote and the voice that matters. Earlier, I was alone. Today, 200 MLAs stand with us in the Assembly. We will put our demands before Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the BJP leadership. Our goal is to secure our constitutional share. NDA has been in power at the Centre and in the state for 11 years. So where is the problem? Sanjay Nishad: This question should be asked to the BJP. Women have been given 33% reservation, and the economically weaker sections among the upper castes have been given 10% reservation. The judges are the same, Modi and Yogi. I am an advocate and will continue to raise this issue. I have hope only from Modi and Yogi. Opposition alleges that you remember the reservation issue only when elections are approaching. Sanjay Nishad: Those making these allegations are themselves robbers. For 30 years, the BSP and SP kept us entangled in this issue. When our community was already included in the Scheduled Caste list, placing us in the OBC category was the biggest betrayal. The SP raises the issue of Muslim reservation in Delhi, but finds it difficult to speak about the fishermen community. I am the lawyer of my community, and in a democracy, the House is the place for advocacy. For the first time in 70 years, the Nishad Party has reached both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council. If the Nishad community gets its rights, the politics of the cycle, elephant and paw will end forever. How much damage will Mukesh Sahani’s entry into UP elections cause? Sanjay Nishad: There is a difference between a political party and a broker. A broker is concerned only with making a livelihood, whereas only those with education and political thought can argue and appeal for their community. Taking advantage of our community’s poverty, some people are trying to mislead voters by offering ₹100, ₹500 or ₹2,000. Society should ask where this money is coming from and which parties are operating them from behind the scenes. Why do you call your community nationalist? Sanjay Nishad: Yes, this is true. The castes belonging to the Nishad community fought against the British and the Mughals and were displaced. The British formed regiments in the names of castes that supported them and rewarded them. Those who fought alongside the British were rewarded, while those who fought for the country are now begging on the streets. It is alleged that you are promoting only your sons in politics Sanjay Nishad: This allegation is completely false. Piyush Ranjan and Vinod Bind are not my sons. We raised funds and helped make Vinod Bind from Bhadohi an MP through the Nishad Party quota so that the voice of our community could reach Parliament. Mithai Lal, Ravi Mani and Janaknandani from our organisation are members of three commissions. Several other workers, including Kamlesh Kumari and Chandan Nishad, hold different positions. Eighteen workers are councillors in urban local bodies. If there are 56 leaders from the same family in the Samajwadi Party, nobody raises questions. But if a Nishad’s son becomes an MP or MLA, it creates a controversy. My sons are educated; one of them is an engineer. He left his job in 2013 and entered politics to serve society. If the Nishad Party has grown so much, why did the BJP take back two seats in the by-elections? Sanjay Nishad: We will win those seats back. We had taken 16 seats from the BJP in 2022. When the BJP said the political atmosphere was challenging and we lost 43 seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, we understood the situation. We are friends. The meaning of friendship is precisely this: when an alliance is weak in one area, its partners help each other. You have been demanding SC status for Nishads for 11 years. When will it happen? Sanjay Nishad: This is not a new demand. It is a right given to us by the Constitution. In the Constitution, ‘Majhwar’ is listed at number 53 and ‘Manjhi’ at number 66. In the President’s notification, Kewat, Mallah, Manjhi and Majhwar are listed under the Scheduled Castes. Keeping them in the OBC category is completely unconstitutional. What proof do you have that the Nishad community is included in the SC list? Sanjay Nishad: There is strong evidence. The Registrar General of India (RGI) acknowledged in January 2022 that these castes are included in the SC list. In 2016, the Governor also clarified that these castes would not remain in the OBC category. The reality today is that a large share of the OBC quota is being taken by milkmen (Yadavs), while a large share of the SC quota is being taken by leather-working communities (Dalits). Our fight is simply to reclaim the rights that have been taken away from us. Did the BJP promise to include the Nishad community in the SC category? Sanjay Nishad: The BJP included it in its ‘Fishermen Vision’ and election manifesto. Chief Minister Yogi also admitted in the House that the Nishad community is entitled to SC status. I am waiting for that promise to be fulfilled. In 1871, the British declared 193 castes as ‘Criminal Castes’. Even after independence, these communities were ignored. Today, people talk about ‘Gen-Z’. We talk about ‘Delta’, communities that wield shovels and remain homeless. Now our community is becoming educated. In 2024, the SP won several Nishad-dominated seats. How did that happen? Sanjay Nishad: Reservation is a sensitive issue on which the opposition misled people. The BJP should resolve the matter. For 70 years, nobody has produced authentic documents. The real issue is that brokers whose livelihoods depend on this system mislead society and the BJP. The SP and BSP are parties that snatch rights, while the BJP is at least taking steps towards granting them. Akhilesh has mentioned the Nishad Party getting 31 seats in the NDA. What do you say? Sanjay Nishad: Nothing happens simply because someone writes it down. The SP chief has written it incorrectly. If the Nishad population is 18% of the state’s population, then he should have written 72 seats. During their tenure, they could not give even a single seat to our community. When the Nishad Party supported them in the 2018 by-election, they won seats such as Gorakhpur and Phulpur. In 2019, the SP and BSP came together, but even then they could not achieve anything without us. How many seats will the NDA win in 2027? Sanjay Nishad: The NDA will win. Nishads will ensure its victory. By pressing the elephant and cycle buttons, our share was lost. The SP and BSP took away 28 lakh jobs in Uttar Pradesh. According to the Social Justice Committee, of the 14 lakh jobs, 99.99% went to Yadavs, while of the seven lakh SC jobs, 6.5 lakh went to Dalits. If we assume an average of ₹2 lakh per job, ₹28 billion is reaching Yadav and Dalit families every year. Where is the share of us ‘Delta’ people, the Nishad community?

stories.title: Man buys knife a week before killing wife, daughter:Accused says he could not afford expenses; worried about family’s future without son
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, a man allegedly stabbed his wife and elder daughter to death and attacked his younger daughter with a knife. The younger daughter survived after sustaining a minor injury. During police interrogation, the accused said he was distressed because he did not have a son and feared what would happen to his family after his death. He also said he was struggling to manage household expenses. A week ago, he allegedly decided to kill his wife and both daughters. He bought a chicken-cutting knife from Ghazipur Fish Market and hid it among clothes at home. Three days before the incident, he allegedly tried to carry out the murders at night but lost his nerve. On Friday night, following an argument with his wife, he attacked her while she was asleep and later killed his elder daughter. The incident took place around midnight on Friday in Lokpriya Vihar Colony, Khoda, around 28 km from the district headquarters. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the accused’s younger daughter. What did the accused reveal during police interrogation? Read the report further. Accused worked as fish market clerk Raja Ansari, 45, a resident of Madhiyayi village in Bihar’s Araria district, had been living in Khoda, Ghaziabad, for three years. His wife, Tabassum, 35, and their two daughters lived with him. Raja worked as a clerk at the Ghazipur fish market in Delhi and earned ₹34,000 a month. At around 12.15 am on Friday, Raja allegedly stabbed his wife Tabassum and elder daughter Sana to death. His younger daughter also suffered a minor stab wound but survived. Tried to kill them three days earlier Raja allegedly gave changing accounts during police interrogation. At times, he cited financial problems and his inability to manage household expenses. At other times, he said he was worried about not having a son and what would happen to his family after his death. He allegedly told police that he believed his family would not survive without him and therefore decided to kill everyone. Raja said he had taken a chicken-cutting knife from the Ghazipur fish market a week earlier and brought it home, where he hid it among his clothes. He said he had decided to kill his wife and both daughters. Three days earlier, he allegedly considered killing them at night but could not go through with it because he lost his nerve. Wife told parents about argument, angered him further Raja said he returned home from the market at around 7 pm on Friday, when both daughters were eating together. He then went to his room. At around 9 pm, he and Tabassum had dinner, after which the daughters went to sleep in another room. He said an argument then broke out between him and his wife. The two went into one room. At around 10 pm, Tabassum allegedly told her parents about the argument over the phone. Raja said this made him even angrier, and he decided that he would kill his wife as soon as she fell asleep. At around 12.15 am, believing that Tabassum was asleep, he allegedly took out the large knife hidden among his clothes and attacked her neck. However, she was awake and raised her hand, causing him to miss his intended target. When Tabassum began screaming, Raja allegedly attacked her again. During the struggle, he stabbed her in the stomach. She fell outside the room and began writhing in pain. He then allegedly stabbed her several more times in the stomach and shoulder. Daughter went to washroom, attacked from behind Raja said his elder daughter came out of the other room and walked towards the washroom. After attacking his wife, he followed Sana and allegedly grabbed her from behind before slitting her throat. Her neck bone was also cut, according to the account. After killing his wife and elder daughter, Raja allegedly tried to attack his younger daughter as well. She suffered one stab wound but managed to run downstairs while screaming. Raja said he tried to catch her but could not see her in the darkness. He feared that neighbours would arrive and kill him if he went downstairs, so he stayed inside. The younger daughter then alerted neighbours and told them that her father had killed her mother and sister. Someone subsequently called the police. Younger daughter: Dad often beat Mum behind closed doors The injured younger daughter, an eighth-grade student, told Dainik Bhaskar that her father had also tried to kill her and that she was stabbed once. She said her father killed her mother and elder sister Sana, but she managed to escape and run downstairs. She raised an alarm and called for help. When the police arrived, they asked her what had happened. She said her father did not beat her mother in front of the two sisters, but frequently assaulted her behind closed doors. Her mother remained silent out of fear, she said, because she did not know what might happen if she spoke out. The girl said she did not remember exactly how her mother was killed. Her mother’s body was lying on the floor, while Sana’s body was near the washroom door. Accused: 'I did something very wrong' Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Raja said he initially felt no remorse after killing his wife and daughter, but later regretted his actions. He said, Now I regret what I have done. If I go to jail, what will happen to my younger daughter? Who will look after her? I was depressed. That is why I killed them. I did something very wrong, and the consequences will also be bad. Raja said he had moved to Delhi from Bihar with his wife and children 12 years ago. They initially lived in rented accommodation near Ghazipur in Delhi. Three years ago, his father-in-law bought a house in Khoda. He said he had been troubled by depression and remained distressed over his circumstances.

stories.title: Did Akhilesh’s allies rise from ‘nobody to somebody’?:Congress rose from 1 to 6 seats, BSP from 0 to 10 in LS polls; Jayant-Rajbhar also gained strength
stories.summary: We made some alliances, the alliance partners came from who knows where. Tell me, we turned a ‘chavanni’ (25 paise coin) into a ‘rupee’ (100 paise), yet they left us. The remark by Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav was aimed at Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) chief Jayant Chaudhary. Jayant’s supporters have now protested against the statement, while BSP chief Mayawati has also criticised Akhilesh. Calling him arrogant, Mayawati said the remark showed his “undignified conduct” and demanded that he apologise not only to Jayant Chaudhary but also to the entire Jat community. This raises a question: how much truth is there in Akhilesh’s ‘chavanni’ remark? Did the parties that allied with the SP in different elections actually become stronger after joining hands with it? In today’s Sunday Big Story, we examine the last four elections to assess whether the SP’s allies benefited politically from their alliances with Akhilesh or suffered losses. 2024 Lok Sabha elections: Allies gain ground In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP contested 62 seats in Uttar Pradesh and won 37. In the previous two Lok Sabha elections, it had won only five seats each. Several of its allies also performed better. Congress makes a comeback: Congress contested 17 seats as part of the alliance and won six. In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the party had won only one seat in Uttar Pradesh — Rae Bareli. Its then president Rahul Gandhi also lost from Amethi. Congress was not in an alliance with the SP at the time. Jan Adhikar Party gets its first MP: Party chief Babu Singh Kushwaha, once a prominent leader in the BSP government, had lost two elections after his name surfaced in the NRHM scam. In 2024, Akhilesh fielded him from Jaunpur on the SP symbol. Kushwaha won and became an MP for the first time. Trinamool Congress fails to open account: TMC candidate Lalitesh Pati Tripathi lost from the Bhadohi Lok Sabha seat and finished second. 2022 Assembly elections: RLD and SBSP gain, others struggle Ahead of the 2022 Assembly elections, there was speculation that Congress and the SP would form an alliance. However, shortly before the polls, both parties announced that they would contest separately. RLD: Jayant Chaudhary’s party contested 33 seats and won eight. In the 2017 Assembly elections, RLD had won only one seat and was not in alliance with the SP. SBSP: Om Prakash Rajbhar’s Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) contested 19 seats and won six. It was the party’s best performance in any Assembly election at that point. In 2017, SBSP had allied with the BJP and won four seats. In 2012, it contested independently and lost all 52 seats. Apna Dal (K): Apna Dal (Kamerawadi) contested six seats and won one — Sirathu. Its candidate Pallavi Patel defeated then Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya. In the 2017 Assembly elections, all Apna Dal (K) candidates had lost. Mahan Dal: Keshav Dev Maurya’s Mahan Dal fielded 14 candidates in 2017, but all lost. In 2022, the party was given eight seats under the SP alliance. Its candidates contested on the SP’s bicycle symbol, but all eight lost. Janwadi Party: The Janwadi Party (Socialist) had won no seats in the 2017 Assembly elections. In 2022, it contested in alliance with the SP, with Akhilesh giving it the Bindki Assembly seat. The party again failed to win a seat. 2019 Lok Sabha elections: BSP gains the most In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the SP and BSP came together after nearly two-and-a-half decades. The alliance did not field candidates against Congress in Amethi and Rae Bareli. BSP: The BSP contested 38 seats, while the SP contested 37. BSP won 10 seats, whereas the SP managed only five. The BSP benefited the most from the alliance. It had failed to win a single seat in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections. However, the alliance was dissolved after the election. RLD: RLD contested three seats as the third partner in the alliance but lost all three. 2017 Assembly elections: Congress suffers losses The SP performed poorly in the 2017 Assembly elections. It contested 298 seats but was reduced to 47. The party had allied with Congress for the polls. Congress: Congress contested 105 seats and won only seven. In the 2012 Assembly elections, 28 Congress MLAs had been elected. The party therefore lost 21 seats compared with 2012. Experts: Major allies benefited from SP alliance in last three elections Senior journalist Samiratmaj Mishra says the SP has allowed its allies to contest more seats than the BJP has in recent alliances. While there may be political reasons behind the seat-sharing arrangements, he says giving an alliance partner more seats also reflects the respect shown to that party. Whether those seats are converted into victories is a separate issue. Mishra says, Looking at the last three elections, Akhilesh Yadav’s ‘chavanni to rupee’ remark appears to have some basis. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, 2022 Assembly elections and 2019 Lok Sabha elections, major parties that allied with the SP benefited in terms of seats won. The picture was different in 2017, when Congress was the SP’s only major alliance partner and lost 21 seats compared with 2012. Before that, the SP contested the 2012 elections on its own and formed the government without an alliance. The term ‘chavanni’ was first used by Jayant Chaudhary. He later switched alliances and joined hands with the BJP. SP spokesperson: We have always strengthened allies SP spokesperson Manoj Kaka says the party has consistently given its alliance partners more opportunities. He says, Look at the figures. Congress had one seat; when it came with us in 2024, it reached six. In 2019, BSP won 10 seats, whereas it had zero earlier. Jayant Singh should also look at his party’s previous figures. Kaka says Akhilesh did not name anyone in his ‘chavanni to rupee’ remark. He rejects Jayant Chaudhary’s claim that the statement insults the Jat community. He says, Our party also has MLAs and MPs from the Jat community. Chaudhary Charan Singh remains our ideal. If anyone is pursuing politics based on his political values and ideas, it is the SP and Akhilesh Yadav.

stories.title: MP Imran Masood’s daughter assaulted, thrown out of home:Nephew says, 'Shayan mistreated his sister, broke up family for politics'
stories.summary: After Congress MP Imran Masood’s son-in-law, Shayan Masood, joined the Samajwadi Party in Saharanpur, a family dispute has come to light. On Saturday, Imran’s nephew Hamza Noman Masood went live on Facebook and accused his brother-in-law Shayan Masood and his father, Shadan Masood, of assaulting his sister and throwing her out of the house. Hamza said, “The family has been silently enduring many things for nearly five years. But after the atrocities committed against my sister and the harassment faced by the family, it is no longer possible to remain silent. My brother-in-law has crossed all limits in mistreating my sister. I will not remain silent anymore.” 5 major things said by Hamza Noman Masood 1. Beating and abusing sister: Brother-in-law Shayan Masood and his family beat and abused my sister (Subia Masood). They threw her out of the house. Our family kept quiet for the sake of relationships and respect. I have many recordings. There are recordings of conversations inside the house as well. If the dispute continues to escalate like this, I will make these recordings and videos public. 2. Ruined sister's life for politics and ticket: My sister was harassed for political reasons. For about 5 years, sister's life kept getting ruined, but the family endured a lot due to relationships and respect. My sister and her one-year-old child are now our responsibility. Shayaan didn't even give money for the child's diapers. Our family will take responsibility for sister and her child ourselves. My sister doesn't need anyone's money or support. 3. Enemies are inquiring about health, but our own have turned against us: When my father fell ill, even people from the opposing political camp called to inquire about his health. However, our own relatives are engaged in political activities against the family during this difficult time. Chaudhary family and Fazur Rahman, among many others, called regarding father's health. When even political opponents can inquire about the family's well-being during illness, why are our own people standing against the family at this time? 4. Talks were held to remove Imran Masood and me from the way: Hamza claimed that I have such conversations and recordings in which talks were made about removing uncle Imran Masood and me from the way. I did not want to make these recordings public until now. But, due to continuous rhetoric, I had to put forth my point publicly. 5. We showed patience, the public will decide: My father is fighting for his life in the hospital; on the other hand, my sister and nephew are troubled. Despite this, we have held onto the garment of patience. Allah will do justice, and now the decision is in the hands of the public. My sister is not alone. Political activity increased after Shayan joined SP Imran Masood's son-in-law Shayan Masood left Congress and joined SP on August 20 (Thursday). He was inducted into the party by SP chief Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow. After joining SP, Shayan had raised questions about Imran Masood's political line. Shayan had said that he does not agree with Imran Masood's ideology. If BJP has to be defeated, then one must speak against BJP. But, Imran Masood is continuously speaking against Akhilesh Yadav. Speaking against Akhilesh Yadav benefits BJP. This is why I have left Imran Masood's side and joined hands with Akhilesh Yadav. After joining SP, Shayan praised the party's PDA policy and spoke about working to strengthen the party in Western UP and deliver better electoral results. Matter has reached from political differences to family dispute After recent developments in the Masood family, the controversy no longer appears to be limited to just political differences. On one hand, Shayan Masood has left Congress and joined SP and raised questions about Imran Masood's political strategy. On the other hand, Hamza Noman has publicly made serious allegations of disputes within the family, atrocities against his sister, and political conspiracy through Facebook Live.

stories.title: Sambhal SP KK Bishnoi breaks down at farewell:Tears keep flowing despite DM consoling him; hall erupts in applause
stories.summary: "I will have to leave my fellow partners; it's very difficult..." Saying this, Sambhal SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi started crying. When he became emotional, DM Ankit Khandelwal, who was sitting next to him, comforted him, but then he too started crying. There was silence in the hall for about 2 minutes. After this, the SP wiped his tears and drank water. Then applause started in the hall. Sambhal SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi was transferred to Bijnor on 20 August. His farewell ceremony was organized on 22 August in the conference room of Bahjoi's Police Line, where the DM and SP became emotional. SP recalled his tenure The farewell ceremony lasted 3 hours. During which the SP recalled his tenure in Sambhal. Other police personnel also expressed their thoughts for him. Notably, IPS Krishna Kumar Bishnoi has completed his 710-day tenure as SP of Sambhal. Police officers and social workers bid farewell to the SP with flowers. The SP, in his address, mentioned the incident of violence that occurred on 24 November, 2024. He specifically praised the work of CO Sambhal Kuldeep Kumar. The SP stated that in this incident, the police and administration faced the circumstances. He particularly thanked CO Sambhal Kuldeep Kumar for his significant role in drafting cases, leading the SIT, and collecting evidence. Sambhal Police handled every case excellently K.K. Bishnoi stated that 284 petitions related to the Sambhal violence have been disposed of by the High Court so far. These include bail-related cases. Some petitions have also been disposed of by the Supreme Court. He emphasized that no adverse order ever came against the Sambhal police, as the police handled every case excellently. He also praised those police personnel who worked despite sustaining injuries. Land returned to farmer Sambhal SP also narrated the story of a victim farmer. He said that a farmer was not getting the right to his land, worth more than ₹50 lakh, for 10 years. But on his instructions, consolidation officers returned the land to the farmer in just two days. It is worth noting that Sambhal SP and IPS officer Krishna Kumar (KK) Bishnoi was married to Bareilly SP Anshika Verma on 29 March, 2026. Their wedding was solemnized with traditional rituals in Jodhpur and Barmer, Rajasthan. IPS Krishna Kumar Bishnoi was transferred from Gorakhpur SP City and came to Sambhal as SP Sambhal on 10 September, 2024.
