stories.title: Thief enters Noida flat wearing salwar suit:Steals ₹2 lakh in 13 minutes, face covered with red dupatta
stories.summary: Two lakh rupees cash was stolen from a flat in Mahagun Meadows Society in Greater Noida. In the incident that took place on Saturday evening, the thief entered the flat wearing a salwar suit. He broke the locker, took the cash, and fled. The theft was captured on CCTV cameras. The CCTV shows that the thief entered the flat around 7:40 PM. He was wearing a black salwar suit. His face was covered with a red dupatta. 13 minutes later, at 7:53 PM, he exited the flat. A broken mirror was also found in the kitchen. The incident took place in Sector-150. Watch the footage of the incident Husband and wife had gone to sister's house, returned to find the locker broken Flat owner Abhishek Sharma said he lives in Tower-B with his wife Sejal Goyal. On Saturday evening, both went to his sister's house. During this, their domestic helper called his wife's mobile phone and inquired about their presence at home. “Late at night, around 12 o'clock, when we returned to the flat, we found the locker broken. The ₹2 lakh cash kept in it was missing,” Abhishek said, adding that he checked the CCTV footage and the entire incident of theft came to light. Suspected domestic helper and electrician Abhishek suspected his domestic helper and electrician of being involved in the theft. A complaint has been filed at Knowledge Park Kotwali. Based on the complaint, the police have registered a case and started investigation. Knowledge Park Station House Officer Vinod Kumar said- Efforts are being made to identify the suspect based on CCTV footage and other evidence.

stories.title: CEC gets emotional after visit to his school:Says ‘That was one era, this is another’; tells students, ‘Lucknow is my Karmabhoomi’
stories.summary: India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, is on a two-day visit to Lucknow. At 11 AM, he arrived at Colvin Taluqdars College, the school where he studied. Here, he interacted with 11th and 12th class students on topics such as democracy, elections, and the right to vote. He also toured the school premises. During this, he appeared emotional. He said- Lucknow is not just a city for him, but his workplace. The things this college taught us were very useful to me later in life. That was one era, this is also an era. I told the children that school teachers give a lot of things, one should be receptive to those ideas. Gyanesh Kumar passed his 10th-class examination from Colvin Taluqdars College in 1979 and his 12th-class examination in 1981. He secured the first position in the UP Board both times. The Chief Election Commissioner also spoke to officials from 20 districts and 1500 school students and principals at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. He informed the students about the process of becoming a voter, casting a vote, and vote counting. Chief Election Commissioner's 2 major points- 1- The coming generation should be aware of their rights and duties The Chief Election Commissioner told the students, 'Voting is not just a right but a means of participation in building the country's future.' The generation that will become voters in the coming time should be aware of their rights and duties from now on. 2- BLOs play an important role in strengthening democracy The Chief Election Commissioner emphasised transparency in the election process and voter participation. He highlighted the crucial role of Booth Level Officers (BLO). He said they are directly connected to the voters and play a significant role in strengthening the democratic system. Programmes will also be held in all universities and schools in the state to explain the transparency of the election process and the entire procedure. Chief Election Commissioner to interact with 500 BLOs tomorrow The Chief Election Commissioner will interact with about 500 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) from Lucknow and surrounding districts at the Mars Hall of Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. BLOs will share their problems, grounded experiences, and suggestions with him. Issues such as adding new names to the voter list, door-to-door verification, and updating information of deceased or relocated voters will be discussed.

stories.title: Chaos at auction of 243 buffaloes, fistfight breaks out:SP MLA, MP Chandrashekhar’s supporters stage protest; police detain them
stories.summary: In Lucknow, the Municipal Corporation auctioned 243 buffaloes for ₹58,89,000. The auction commenced at 11:00 am on Monday. At around 1:00 pm, workers from the SP Youth Brigade and MP Chandrashekhar's Azad Samaj Party created a commotion. They kicked and punched a youth who had arrived from Sitapur. SP workers alleged that people from outside Lucknow had come for the auction, including several butchers. Seeing the commotion escalate, the police intervened. Shortly after, SP MLA Armaan Khan from the Lucknow West assembly constituency arrived at the spot. He sat on a dharna along with party workers. The police forcibly removed the protesters, carrying them one by one to load them onto a bus, and took them to Eco Garden. MLA Armaan submitted a letter to Additional Municipal Commissioner Dr Arvind Kumar Rao, demanding that the auction be stopped. Several illegal dairies were operating in the Para area. On 16 August, a Municipal Corporation team accompanied by police personnel arrived to clear the encroachments. However, local residents attacked a sub-inspector. Following this, a drive was conducted on 17 and 18 August. A total of 241 female buffaloes, 1 male buffalo, and 1 female calf were seized from the illegal dairies and kept in the Kanji House. The base price for one buffalo was fixed at ₹21,000. To participate in the auction, a deposit of ₹1,02,000 was required.

stories.title: 50 cops in bulletproof jackets raid Kanpur RTO office:22 agents chased and caught, several flee by jumping walls; ₹1 lakh recovered from clerk
stories.summary: A team of district administration officials and 50 police personnel raided the RTO office in Kanpur. Everyone barged inside wearing bulletproof jackets and had both gates of the office shut. Seeing the raid, agents (touts) began running helter-skelter. Illegal vendors outside the RTO closed their shops and fled. The police personnel gave chase and caught 22 touts. However, amid the chaos, several touts managed to escape by scaling the boundary wall. During this, police personnel also got into a scuffle with a lawyer. The team found a shortage of ₹15,000 with Vipin Kumar, a clerk in the Cash Department. Meanwhile, ₹1 lakh in cash was found on challan clerk Mridul Mishra, who failed to account for the money. ADCP Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke interrogated RTO RI (Regional Inspector) Santosh Yadav behind closed doors. Meanwhile, SDM Sadar Anubhav Singh stated that a truck driver had lodged a complaint. The ARTO had issued a challan against him for pollution, a non-functional truck horn, and not wearing a seat belt. He was charged ₹26,700, whereas a receipt for only ₹21,700 was issued to him. Following this, the raid was carried out today (Monday) at around 1:30 PM. During the operation, the police team maintained surveillance using drones. Challan clerk found with ₹1 lakh cash, failed to account for it During the raid, the team from the district administration and the Crime Branch, alongside ARTO Alok Kumar, searched documents in every single department. During this, officials also checked the laptops and computers of officers and employees. After first raiding the Cash Department, the SOG team reached Sarathi Bhawan. Here, they went to Counter No. 6, where biometric processing for vehicle driving licences takes place. Here, they interrogated employee Mujahid Farooqui, a resident of Azamgarh. Mujahid stated that biometric processing could not take place until 12 noon due to the server/website not functioning. Between 12 noon and 3:30 PM, 15 biometrics were completed. SDM states action taken following corruption complaint SDM Anubhav Singh stated that complaints regarding the department had been received for quite some time. Kamta Prasad, a truck driver residing in the Lalpura police station area of Hamirpur district, had lodged a complaint on Saturday (22 August). ARTO Somlata Yadav had issued a challan for his truck on the Bhaunti Bypass. A challan was also issued for not having a seat belt and a heavy driving licence, whereas trucks do not have seat belts. Kamta possessed a heavy driving licence. Despite this, a challan was issued against him. Following this, the district administration formed a team and conducted a raid. After the raid, which lasted for nearly three hours, the police team handed over all 22 touts to the Kakadev police station. The SDM stated that the investigation team inspected the entire RTO premises. During this, essential documents, CCTV footage, and digital recordings were taken into custody. Initial investigation has revealed irregularities in the maintenance of cash. Discrepancies of ₹5,000 to ₹7,000 and other amounts were also found at various locations. All documents and evidence are currently being examined. Once the investigation is complete, the report will be submitted to senior officers. Strict further action will be taken based on this. Truck driver states — ARTO charged ₹26,700, issued receipt for ₹21,700 Truck driver Kamta Prasad stated: “I drive a truck for JK Cement. On Saturday, I was carrying a load of cement from Bharuwa to Mandhana. On the Bhaunti Bypass, ARTO Somlata Yadav issued me a challan of ₹26,750. Non-usage of seat belt in the truck and irregularities regarding a non-functional horn were cited as reasons for the action.” “After paying the challan, I received a receipt for ₹21,700, whereas a payment of ₹26,700 was taken. Upon receiving a receipt for ₹5,000 less, I complained to the officers, but I was turned away. Following this, I lodged a complaint with the district administration,” he said.

stories.title: ‘Possessed by Goddess Kali,’ woman removes husband’s intestines after murder:Victim’s liver and kidney missing
stories.summary: New revelation has emerged in the murder case of Rajesh, a resident of Sitapur, UP, in Kurukshetra, Haryana. Landlord Rinku's mother Amro Devi stated that after the murder, Rajesh's wife Vimla was telling people around- The goddess Kali had possessed me, that's why I killed Rajesh. According to Amro Devi, Vimla jumped from the roof after the incident. When police arrived, she became unconscious. Amro also claimed that Vimla practiced exorcism. Meanwhile, a forensic examination found that half of Rajesh’s liver and one kidney were missing. The incident took place on Saturday when the accused, Vimla, allegedly made a deep incision from Rajesh’s chest to his private parts and stuffed his intestines into a sack. Vimla was Rajesh’s third wife. The couple had a love marriage in Sitapur. Rajesh had divorced his first two wives. About a year ago, he moved from Sitapur to Kurukshetra, where he lived with Vimla in a rented house. The couple had no children. 2 new facts emerge in Rajesh murder case 1. Colleague said, ‘He used to drink alcohol even during the day’ Rajesh worked at PB RO Water Trading Company on Pehowa Road in Kurukshetra, located near his rented house. A colleague, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Rajesh was addicted to alcohol and would sometimes drink even during the day. According to the colleague, Vimala often stopped him from drinking. However, Rajesh never mentioned any quarrel or dispute with his wife. 2. Neighbors saw Vimala eating raw rice and sugar There are only a few houses around the building where Rajesh lived on rent. An empty plot lies on one side, while a garden is on the other. A dharamshala is also located nearby. People in the area were reluctant to speak about the case. One local resident said Vimala mostly stayed inside her room and rarely interacted with neighbors. Some people also claimed they had seen her eating raw rice and sugar several times. Now, know what happened on the day of the incident… Landlord Rinku said that Rajesh lived on the first floor with his wife Vimala. There were frequent quarrels between the husband and wife. On Saturday evening (22 Aug), screaming sounds continued to come from Rajesh and Vimala's room for a long time. Hearing Rajesh's scream, Rinku went upstairs. There Rajesh was lying on the ground drenched in blood. He had a deep wound on his stomach. Vimala was filling his intestines into a plastic sack. Seeing Rinku, Vimala jumped from the roof. Forensic expert said, ‘The wound was 37 cm long’ Forensic expert Dr. Gaurav Kaushik said, “When the body reached them, half of his liver and one kidney were missing. There was a 37-centimeter long and deep incision on the deceased's stomach. The intestines were protruding from the incision.” Dr. Kaushik said that it is the police's responsibility to recover where the deceased's half liver and one kidney are. Woman to be questioned after treatment KUK Police Station In-charge Surendra Sandhu said, After murdering her husband, the accused wife jumped from the roof. This caused injury to her spinal cord. She is admitted in Loknayak Jayprakash Hospital. She will be arrested and interrogated after discharge. Only then will the real reason behind the murder be known.

stories.title: Mosquito bites girl at school, professor father complains to DM:Says, 'School takes full fees, who will be responsible if she falls ill?'
stories.summary: Professor's 6 year old daughter studying in LKG was bitten by a mosquito at school in Moradabad. When the child told her father at home, he complained about the school by emailing DM Dr. Rajendra Painsia. The professor father said, If his daughter falls ill due to the mosquito bite, who will be responsible? Professor Dr. Sonu Singh said, “It is the school's responsibility to provide children with a clean and safe environment. They charge fees. In such a case, the DM should determine the school's accountability in the matter.” Dr. Sonu Singh is an Assistant Professor at Amity University Noida. On 19 August, he complained by sending an email to the DM. Not only this, the professor father said, “He has researched neuropsychology and neurosciences in America for 8 years. Therefore, he understands very well the dangers of diseases caused by mosquitoes.” The case concerns Shirdi Sai Public School on Kanth Road. Complained about mosquito bites earlier, but school took no action The professor said in the complaint, “When my daughter was bitten by a mosquito in school for the first time, this was complained about to the school administration in the school diary. Despite this, no effective action was taken by the school. After this, she was bitten by a mosquito again. That's why we had to complain about the school.” Full fees paid, but school failed to fulfill its responsibility He said, “As parents we leave our children in the trust of the school. We expect that the school will provide them with a safe environment. But even after depositing full fees, the school is not fulfilling its responsibility.” DIOS says – Ordered fogging at school District Magistrate Dr. Rajendra Pensia said, “DIOS has been directed to ensure special attention to cleanliness not only at the concerned school but also at all schools in the district.” DIOS Ritu Tomar said, "I'm aware of the professor’s complaint and has directed the private school to conduct fogging. She added that action will be taken if the instructions are not followed.

stories.title: ED raids former BSP MLA Rana’s premises:Officers arrive in vehicles with ‘Bol Bam’ stickers; searches at 3 locations in Muzaffarnagar
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted raids at three locations linked to former BSP MLA Shahnawaz Rana in Muzaffarnagar on Monday. The ED team arrived around 8 AM in 12 vehicles bearing ‘Bol Bam’ stickers. Around 50 police personnel and CRPF jawans have been deployed, and no one is being allowed to enter or leave the premises. The searches are being conducted at the former MLA’s Rana House on Meerut Road, his newspaper office, and the office of Jammudip Import-Export in Model Town. Rana House also houses the residences of his uncle, former MP Kadir Rana, and former MLA Noor Saleem Rana. The locations being searched include Rana House, the former MLA’s residence on Meerut Road, his newspaper office, and the Jammudip Import-Export office in Model Town. Around 50 police personnel and CRPF jawans have been deployed at all three locations. No one is being allowed to enter or leave the premises, while ED officials are examining documents inside. Rana House also houses the residences of the former MLA’s uncle, former MP Kadir Rana, and former MLA Noor Saleem Rana. Apart from Muzaffarnagar, the ED is conducting searches at six locations in Ghaziabad and Faridabad. According to sources, the action has been taken under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and is reportedly linked to alleged manipulation of input tax credit and tax evasion. The ED has not yet officially disclosed which documents or materials are being examined. Photos of the ED raids Shahnawaz Rana was jailed over alleges attack on GST team Shahnawaz Rana was arrested on December 5, 2024, for allegedly attacking a GST team that had gone to conduct a raid at the steel factory owned by Rana and his uncle, former MP Kadir Rana. During the same period, a case of alleged fraud involving a fake company was also registered at Civil Lines police station against Kadir Rana’s son, Shah Azam. Both were sent to jail and were initially lodged in Muzaffarnagar Jail, before being shifted to Chitrakoot Jail. In August 2025, Shahnawaz Rana was granted bail by the Allahabad High Court and has remained out of jail since then. The news is being continuously updated...

stories.title: Yogi says Rahul wants to ruin country with urban Naxals:'Look at Ajay Rai’s shamelessness-he bowed before Hanumangarhi, chanted Ram-Ram, then feasted on fish outside'
stories.summary: CM Yogi hit back at Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Manusmriti In Rae Bareli. He said, “Rahul ji, the country may not expect much from you as Rahul Gandhi, but as the Leader of the Opposition in Parliament, you are accountable to democracy. You should apologise to the country.” Yogi said, After taking the oath of the Constitution, you consider it your birthright to criticise India’s traditions and heritage. You want to ruin the country’s future by placing it in the hands of urban Naxals. Rahul Gandhi had mentioned Manusmriti two days earlier and called the belief that women are the property of their father, husband or children “shameful.” He said a woman’s identity is not defined by her father, husband or son, but by her own identity. He also said women should have complete freedom to pursue education, employment, property ownership and make their own decisions. He said, “Women face violence in three forms: female infanticide, physical abuse and economic restrictions.” Gandhi argued that women should have complete freedom to pursue education, jobs, property ownership and make their own decisions. The CM inaugurated an auditorium built at a cost of ₹21 crore in memory of freedom fighter Rana Beni Madhav Baksh Singh. He was a prominent figure in the 1857 First War of Independence and was also known as ‘Awadh Kesari’. Monday marks his 222nd birth anniversary. See pictures… Yogi targets Ajay Rai over fish feast: “Even a chameleon would feel ashamed” CM Yogi criticised Congress’s UP president Ajay Rai over the fish feast held in Ayodhya. He said Congress leaders were insulting India’s heritage and questioned Rai’s conduct after his visit to Hanumangarhi. Yogi said, They visit Hanumangarhi and then go outside and feast on fish. They chant ‘Ram-Ram’. There should be a limit to shamelessness. If they wanted to eat fish, why did they go to the temple? He added, “Looking at their double standards, even a chameleon would feel ashamed.” Yogi accused Rai of pretending to bow before Bajrangbali at the temple and then attending a fish feast. “Rai bowed before mafia who killed his brother” Targeting Ajay Rai, Yogi alleged that Mukhtar Ansari had killed his brother, but Rai did not speak against him and instead “bowed before” the mafia. He said the BJP government later “crushed that mafia.” Rai visited Hanumangarhi before attending Congress event Ajay Rai had visited Ayodhya on Sunday. He recited the Hanuman Chalisa at Hanumangarhi and then offered prayers at Ram Lalla. Later, he attended a Congress workers’ conference at Tarun Bazar in the Gosaiganj Assembly constituency, around 38 km from Hanumangarhi. A fish feast was organised at the event. 3. Congress does not accept Savarkar, Bose and Sardar Patel CM Yogi said Congress should apologise to the people for repeatedly insulting freedom fighters. He said Veer Savarkar was sentenced to life imprisonment twice in the same lifetime and was only 28 at the time. Both Savarkar brothers were imprisoned in the Cellular Jail, and he could not meet his brother for nearly 10 years. Yogi recalled that Savarkar once saw his brother while being taken to the oil press and realised that he too was imprisoned in the same jail. He also alleged that when the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government named Port Blair Airport after Savarkar, Congress later removed his name. Yogi said Congress also does not accept the contributions of Subhas Chandra Bose and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. 4. Prime Minister is not an individual, but an institution Yogi said insulting Indian institutions or making derogatory remarks against the Prime Minister amounts to insulting an institution, not merely an individual. He said such actions must be opposed and recalled the “dark shadow” of the 1975 Emergency. He alleged that Congress leaders defame Uttar Pradesh outside the state and insult India when they travel abroad. He also accused them of seeking proof from soldiers fighting enemies at the borders and of directly or indirectly supporting anti-national elements. Yogi further alleged that Congress has questioned the existence of Lord Ram in Ayodhya. 5. ‘The world worships Ayodhya, yet you are questioning it’ CM Yogi said India remains a part of a person wherever they go and highlighted the global respect for Uttar Pradesh and the Awadh region. He said, “If you say you belong to the Awadh region, the whole world is ready to honour you. Yet they are now raising questions about Ayodhya.”

stories.title: ₹40 crore fraud in Gorakhpur:Company lures investors with promise to double money in 400 days; 2,000 people fall victim
stories.summary: A case of fraud worth 40 crores has come to light in Gorakhpur. It is alleged that approximately 2000 people were defrauded by luring them with promises of doubling their deposited amount in 400 days and providing a daily profit of 0.5 percent. Investors from Gorakhpur and Lucknow have accused the company of embezzling their money. It is alleged that the company initially paid interest to investors, but later stopped returning the principal amount by making excuses of company closure and other reasons. The post-dated cheques given to investors are also bouncing due to insufficient funds in the account. Investors have submitted a petition to the SSP for action. Noose tightens around CMD and associates People who fell victim to the fraud mentioned in their petition that the company's CMD and his associates motivated people to invest by providing online IDs and passwords through team leaders from various districts of UP. It was claimed, “The company would give returns at the rate of 0.5 percent per day for 400 days and the deposited amount would double. It was also claimed that a notary affidavit would be provided for securing deposits less than ₹10 lakh and a land agreement for amounts exceeding ₹10 lakh.” Investors allege, "The company paid 0.5% daily returns credited to their accounts until 11 January, 2026. After that, payments were delayed, with the company citing a software update and the CMD’s wife’s wedding as reasons. Investors allege, “The company paid the accrued income in accounts at the rate of 0.5 percent per day until 11 January, 2026. After that, payments started being delayed citing software updates and the CMD's wife's wedding.” In April 2026, investors started demanding their deposited money back. It is alleged that post-dated cheques were issued for the amount to be returned by the company, but the cheques are continuously bouncing due to insufficient funds in the account. Complaint also filed at Ashiana police station in Lucknow Investors said, “They also filed a complaint at Ashiana police station in Lucknow, but no action has been taken yet against the main ringleader of the gang and others, and attempts are being made to suppress the matter.” After that, a complaint has also been filed against the company in Gorakhpur. Investors have demanded from the authorities to get their deposited money back, take action against the accused, and investigate the company's directors.

stories.title: Attack on Gopiradha Girls Inter College bus, FIR filed:Girls harassed; conductor and transport in-charge abducted and extortion demanded
stories.summary: The conductor of the bus of Gopiradha Girls Inter College located in Ravindrapuri, Varanasi, has filed a case at Lanka police station under several sections including kidnapping, extortion, and assault. The allegation is that on 14 August, a Scorpio vehicle scraped against the school bus in the Chittupura area of Lanka police station jurisdiction. Following this, the Scorpio occupants assaulted him and later entered the bus and misbehaved with the girl students. After that, they took him away and upon reaching the school, also abducted the transport manager. Later, they also extorted money in the name of getting the Scorpio's dent repaired. The allegation is that all of them had pistols and were repeatedly threatening to take them to Bihar and kill them. Meanwhile, the police have registered a case under relevant sections and initiated further action. Bus conductor filed a written complaint Gopiradha Balika Inter College's bus number UP65 LT 8727 conductor Satish Yadav filed a report with the police stating. On 14 August, I was with Ravishankar Rai taking 40 girl students home after school dismissal. When the bus reached near Shankar Ji temple ahead of Lanka Chittupur Gate, at that time a speeding Scorpio UP65GD 0627 brushed against the bus. Upon this, the Scorpio's driver and the person sitting inside got down and started hurling abuses and broke the bus window. Girl students allegedly harassed, conductor beaten and kidnapped Satish stated, “When I tried to stop them, they climbed into the bus and started beating me and picked me up and locked me in the Scorpio. While taking me with them, both were saying give money for the dent or we will kill you. After this, they threatened me by showing a pistol and kept me locked in the Scorpio driving around for some time.” He added, “After that they reached the school and misbehaved with the guard, transport in-charge and manager, and also put the transport in-charge in the Scorpio and started beating him.” Drank alcohol, demanded money for dent by brandishing pistol Satish told, “After this, the accused beat both the people and threatened to kill them by showing a pistol and went to Nadesar and demanded money for the car's dent and threatened to take them to Bihar and kill them if they didn't pay, and took 7200 rupees. After that they released them. In this regard, a complaint has been filed to register a case.” Police registered FIR Lanka police station in-charge Rajkumar said, “After receiving the complaint, a case has been registered at the police station under BNS sections 281, 351(3), 352, 324(2), 115(2), 126(2), 127(2), 308(2) and 3(5). stories.title: Last Monday of Sawan today:Long queues of devotees at Kanpur temples; Anandeshwar Temple opens doors at 2am
stories.summary: Today is the last Monday of the holy month of Sawan, and a large number of devotees are expected to arrive at Shri Anandeshwar Temple in Kanpur. The temple administration has estimated that around 4 lakh devotees will come for darshan. Devotees started queuing for darshan from 12 AM on Sunday night. After the Mangala Aarti at 2 AM, the temple gates were opened for darshan. Considering the crowd, the temple and district administration have made extensive arrangements for security and darshan. According to the temple administration, more than 25,000 devotees had darshan in just 4 hours, by 6 AM. Devotees are seen standing in long queues outside the temple. Devotees in the queue are having darshan while chanting "Har Har Mahadev" and "Bam Bam Bhole". Ashutosh Ansh, media in-charge of Juna Akhara, said, “Maharaj Harigiri has ordered that all devotees coming to the temple should be allowed darshan. The Shayan Aarti will be performed at night only after all devotees have completed their darshan.”

stories.title: Farmer leader vows to protest with family against SSP:Beaten after being made to dance to ‘Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai’; SP MLA seeks punishment like goons
stories.summary: “I was made to dance to the song ‘Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai...’ Meerut SSP Avinash Pandey and the Inspector abused me in their chamber, beat me and kicked me with their boots. I suffered internal injuries, and one of my eyes also swelled up. Even after five days, no case has been registered against the policemen. Evidence of the assault is being destroyed. If my case is not registered within two days, I will protest with my wife and children.” Farmer leader Digvijay Bhati made these allegations in a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar. Meanwhile, SP MLA Atul Pradhan has come forward to demand justice for Bhati. He said, “Action should be taken against those responsible just as it is taken against goons and criminals who break the law.” Read the full story based on conversations with Digvijay Bhati and Atul Pradhan... Digvijay said, ‘I wasn’t even given a medical examination’ Bharatiya Kisan Union (BR Ambedkar) President Dr. Digvijay Bhati said, “The incident is from 19 August. My case has not been registered till now. The police have not even taken my written complaint yet. My medical examination has also not been conducted. I have been continuously troubled since the incident. I have not bathed since the beating.” Digvijay Bhati has demanded an SIT investigation into the case. He said, “The investigation should be monitored by a former judge, so that the investigation can be conducted in an impartial manner. We fear that police department officers might influence the investigation. I was called before the DIG Saharanpur for investigation.” I was asked if I could identify those who beat me, but no one was presented before me for identification. On Saturday, I was called to the ADG office for a statement, where even after waiting for about two hours, I could not meet the ADG. SP MLA said, ‘Suspending policemen is not punishment’ SP MLA from Sardhana, Atul Pradhan said, “Those who have broken the law should face strict action according to the law. I have informed the new SSP of Meerut about the entire matter.” Assurance has been given for further action based on investigation. However, my demand is that the investigation should be impartial. Many aspects of the case have already become public. Now action should be taken based on correct facts. He said that only a few policemen have been lined up so far, which I do not consider a punishment. Police officials have been told not to view the matter from a religious and caste perspective, but to deliver impartial justice. 'Will protest at police stations if no action is taken' Atul Pradhan said, “If action is not taken in the matter according to law, I will protest with SP workers. If necessary, protests will also be held at police stations. I have spoken to DIG Saharanpur over the phone. The DIG has said that statements are being recorded. Further action will be taken based on the investigation.” The entire matter is being investigated by DIG Saharanpur Abhishek Singh. He had spoken to the victim's side on Friday. Further interrogation and statements are being recorded in the matter. Digvijay Bhati and Atul Pradhan held a press conference on 21 August Dr. Digvijay Bhati said that on 19 August, I and Mohit Jatav, district president of Bharatiya Kisan Union (BR Ambedkar), went to meet SSP Avinash Pandey. The police had sent 8-10 of us to jail in the Lalita Gautam murder case protest matter. We had no fault and we were not involved in the protest. That's why we went to present our case to the Captain Sahab. When we met the SSP, he got furious. He started speaking in abusive language- "Wearing a 40 rupee kurta-pajama, you become a leader, will you confront us?" When we protested against the abusive language, the SSP dragged us into his chamber and beat us with kicks, punches, and shoes. After this, he told Civil Lines in-charge Akhilesh Gaud to see how much hospitality you can show. Then he took us to the SOG (SOG) office. In a closed room, both our hands and feet were tied and we were beaten with sticks. We were released at 2 AM when Atul Pradhan arrived. A condition was laid that if the matter came in the media, our condition would be made worse. 'SSP had already planned our encounter' Digvijay Bhati said while crying, "We were not involved in the 8 July protest, yet we were targeted. We came forward to get justice for a poor family. If this keeps happening, no one will come forward to help anyone in need. Mohit Jatav said, “He is a leader of his community. Before going to the office, he had a phone conversation with the police officer. The behavior on the phone was completely different from the behavior in person. The SSP had already planned our encounter. He told the policemen to shoot me once and then carry out the encounter. I will take care of everything.” SP MLA said, ‘SSP is mentally ill’ SP MLA Atul Pradhan said, “The brutality committed by the SSP and Inspector is concerning. The government should take cognizance of the entire incident and register a case. The kind of act committed by the SSP after sitting in a responsible position clearly shows that he is mentally ill. The government should get him treated.” The SP MLA said, “After carrying out this entire act, Digvijay and Mohit were forcibly made to write a letter. It stated that they had an accident with a scooter. Whereas, nothing like that happened. If the SSP has any evidence of this, let him present it. The evidence of his brutality is present in the CCTV installed in his office.”

stories.title: Imran’s daughter ousted from in-laws’ home, son-in-law joins SP:Saharanpur’s Masood family feud makes headlines; power struggle enters third generation
stories.summary: Family feud involving Congress MP Imran Masood is once again in the spotlight in Saharanpur. Amid allegations that his daughter was assaulted and thrown out of her in-laws’ home, his son-in-law Shayan Masood joined the Samajwadi Party and opened a front against the Congress MP. He said Imran Masood’s approach benefits the BJP. On one side is Rasheed Masood’s son Shazan Masood. On the other is his nephew and Congress MP Imran Masood, who has established a strong political identity of his own. Imran’s twin brother, Noman Masood, has also been trying to find his footing in politics. Now, Shayan’s move to the SP has brought the family feud into the open. On Saturday, 22 August, Imran’s nephew Hamza Noman Masood went live on Facebook and accused his brother-in-law Shayan Masood of assaulting his sister and throwing her out of the house. However, Hamza said that after what happened to his sister, “it is no longer possible to remain silent.” Shayan, meanwhile, said he could respond to the allegations but added that personal family matters should not be dragged into the public domain. Shayan’s SP entry exposes Qazi family feud The Qazi family’s influence in Western UP politics is once again in the spotlight after Shayan Masood joined the Samajwadi Party. The family has shaped Saharanpur politics for nearly five decades, but its third generation is now changing the political equations. Former Union Minister late Qazi Rasheed Masood established the family’s political legacy. Today, the contest is mainly between his son Shazan Masood and nephew, Congress MP Imran Masood, who has built a strong political identity of his own. Imran’s twin brother Noman Masood has also been trying to establish his political base. Third generation enters the political battle Shayan’s SP entry has also brought the family feud into the open. On 22 August, Imran’s nephew Hamza Noman Masood went live on Facebook and accused Shayan of assaulting his sister and throwing her out of the house. Hamza said, "The family had remained silent for nearly five years, but “after what happened to my sister, it is no longer possible to remain silent.” The dispute now reflects a larger battle over political power, legacy and the rise of the third generation. Rasheed Masood gave nephew Imran a political identity, then their paths diverged The political relationship between Qazi Rashid Masood and Imran Masood was once very strong. Imran advanced his early politics under the shadow of his uncle Rashid Masood. In 2007, he contested as an independent from the Muzaffarnagar assembly seat and defeated SP's then minister Jagdish Rana. After this, Imran's political stature continued to grow. In 2012, he contested elections from the Nakud assembly seat on a Congress ticket and secured around 85 thousand votes. However, he lost the election. This is where the ground began to be prepared for the next major political battle within the Qazi family. After 2012, the political paths of Imran and Qazi Rasheed Masood diverged. Imran joined the Congress, while Rasheed Masood rejoined the SP. 2014 marked the beginning of their political distance The 2014 Lok Sabha election is considered a decisive turning point in the politics of the Qazi family. The SP had decided to give the ticket for the Saharanpur Lok Sabha seat to Imran Masood, but before that he had already left the party. After this, the SP gave the ticket to Shajan Masood, son of Qazi Rasheed Masood. Imran contested this election from Congress. Two faces from the same family came face to face from different parties. The result also reflected the picture of this family political contest. Imran came second, while Shajan came fourth. After this election, the political distance in the family deepened further. This is where the question arose - who would be the real heir to Qazi Rasheed Masood's political legacy? His son Shajan or that nephew, for whom he himself had prepared the political ground for a long time? After Rasheed Masood’s demise, new challenges emerged for son Shazan After the demise of Qazi Rasheed Masood on 5 October, 2020, the political picture of the family changed further. The biggest challenge before Rasheed Masood's son Shazan was to prepare his own separate political ground. This is where a new political competition began to appear within the family. On the other hand, Imran Masood continued to expand his politics. While in Congress, he strengthened his hold in Saharanpur politics. His role in district politics was considered so influential that his influence was also discussed in the political equations of several assembly seats. Thus, two political centers emerged from the same family. On one side, Shazan Masood as the heir of Rasheed Masood, and on the other side, Imran Masood who had already established his own separate political identity. Imran’s twin brother Noman has faced defeat in every election In this political story of the Qazi family, Imran Masood's twin brother Noman Masood cannot be ignored. Noman has also tried his luck in electoral politics several times. In 2017, he contested elections from the Gangoh assembly seat on a Congress ticket and came second. He also contested the 2019 by-election on a Congress ticket but could not win. Later in 2022, he contested from the same seat on a BSP ticket and lost. This means Noman has also been continuously searching for his political ground in family politics. Third generation of the Qazi family enters politics The entry of the third generation of the Qazi family into politics has made the story even more interesting. Shazan Masood's son Shayan Masood left Congress on 20 August and joined SP. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav inducted him into the party. After Shayan joined SP, he expressed disagreement with the politics of his father-in-law, Congress MP Imran Masood. Shayan stated that if one has to fight a political battle against BJP, then one must speak against BJP. His allegation was that Imran Masood is continuously speaking against Akhilesh Yadav. This benefits the BJP. He cited this political difference as the reason for separating from Imran. Politically speaking, Shayan's joining SP is not just changing parties. This is an attempt by the third generation of the Qazi family to establish their own political identity. Nephew alleges, ‘Shayan abused sister, beat her and threw her out of the house’ Who will carry forward Rasheed Masood’s legacy? The biggest political question facing the Qazi family is who will carry forward the legacy of Qazi Rasheed Masood? Will it be Imran Masood, whom Rasheed Masood gave political ground in the early days? Will son Shazan Masood succeed in strengthening his father's legacy again? Will Noman Masood be able to create his own separate political identity? Or will Shayan Masood become the face of the new generation and give a new direction to the family's politics?

stories.title: IAS officer who brought down Azam Khan’s stronghold denied extension:Sangeeta Singh appointed Moradabad commissioner; 17 IAS officers transferred in UP
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh government transferred 17 IAS officers late Sunday night. Aligarh Divisional Commissioner Sangeeta Singh has been appointed the new Divisional Commissioner of Moradabad. Meanwhile, Moradabad Commissioner Anjaneya Singh, who had taken strong action against SP leader Azam Khan in Rampur, did not receive an eighth service extension. The state government has relieved him, paving the way for his return to the Sikkim cadre. However, he is reportedly trying to secure a posting as Sikkim’s Resident Commissioner in New Delhi. Meanwhile, UP Jal Nigam (Rural) MD Dr. Rajasekhar has been removed. Sources say Jal Shakti Minister Swatantradev Singh was unhappy with his working style. Chaitra V has also been removed following the displeasure of Minister Dayashankar Dayalu. Amid reports of a sugar shortage, waiting IAS officer Amrit Pal Kaur has been given a key responsibility. She has been appointed Joint Managing Director of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation. Anjaneya Singh served as Moradabad Divisional Commissioner from 6 March, 2021, to 14 August, 2026, for around five years and five months. His service extension ended on 14 August. The next day, 15 August, he handed over charge to Moradabad DM Rajendra Pensia and went on two months’ leave. Amid sugar shortage reports, IAS officer Amritpal Kaur gets key responsibility Major change has been made amid reports of sugar shortage in the state. IAS officer Amritpal Kaur of the 2019 batch has been appointed Joint Managing Director of Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation Limited. She was previously awaiting posting. Amritpal Kaur is originally from Nanowal Khurd village in Gurdaspur district, Punjab. She secured the 44th rank nationwide in the UPSC Civil Services Examination-2018. Subsequently, she was selected for the Indian Administrative Service in the 2019 batch and allotted the Uttar Pradesh cadre. 17 IAS officers transferred in UP: Why Anjaneya Singh, Dr Rajasekhar and Chaitra V were sidelined The Uttar Pradesh government transferred 17 IAS officers late Sunday night. Aligarh Divisional Commissioner Sangeeta Singh has been appointed the new Divisional Commissioner of Moradabad. Meanwhile, IAS officer Anjaneya Singh, who took strong action against SP leader Azam Khan during his tenure in Rampur, did not receive an eighth service extension. The government has relieved him, paving the way for his return to the Sikkim cadre. However, he is reportedly trying to get posted as Sikkim’s Resident Commissioner in New Delhi. Apart from Anjaneya Singh, Dr Rajasekhar and Chaitra V have also been moved from their key assignments. Here is a look at the major transfers and the reasons being reported behind them. Who got posted where? See the complete list Anjaneya served as Moradabad Commissioner for 5 years and 5 months Anjaneya Singh served as Moradabad Divisional Commissioner from 6 March, 2021, to 14 August, 2026 around five years and five months. His service extension ended on 14 August. On 15 August, he handed over charge to Moradabad DM Rajendra Pensia and went on two months’ leave. Anjaneya Singh is a 2005-batch IAS officer of the Sikkim cadre. He was brought to Uttar Pradesh during the Akhilesh Yadav government at the request of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. He subsequently received seven extensions to continue serving in UP. He has spent only around eight years in his parent Sikkim cadre, while his total tenure in Uttar Pradesh has now crossed 11 years. Anjaneya was the Rampur DM during the 2019 Lok Sabha election campaign, when Azam Khan made controversial remarks about the district magistrate. During his tenure, several strict actions were taken against Azam Khan. Khan was later convicted and sentenced to three years in a hate-speech case. Why was Dr Rajasekhar transferred? Dr Rajasekhar, a 2004-batch IAS officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre, has been removed as Managing Director of UP Jal Nigam (Rural). He has now been appointed Secretary in the Planning Department, a posting considered less influential compared with his previous assignment. His transfer is being linked to complaints regarding the implementation of the Har Ghar Nal scheme in rural areas. There were also reports of differences between Rajasekhar and Jal Shakti Minister Swatantradev Singh over his working style. He reportedly did not have a good working relationship with the department’s Additional Chief Secretary Anurag Srivastava either. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had also expressed displeasure during a meeting recently. Rajasekhar has been replaced by Yogi Kumar, Commissioner and Registrar of the Cooperative Department, who has been given the important responsibility of MD, UP Jal Nigam (Rural). Chaitra V moved after differences with department Chaitra V, who was serving as Director General, AYUSH and Mission Director, National AYUSH Mission, has been moved to the Revenue Board as Member (Judicial). According to reports, differences had developed between Chaitra V and Principal Secretary Ranjan Kumar as well as Minister Dayashankar Mishra 'Dayalu' over her working style. The matter had also reportedly reached the Chief Minister. Chaitra V had made headlines in August 2025 after accusing Lucknow hotel businessman Naren Raj of mentally harassing her. She had lodged an FIR at Alambagh police station, alleging that the businessman was repeatedly harassing her and pressuring her to introduce him to prominent hotel entrepreneurs. Police had registered a case and started an investigation based on her complaint. Amrit Pal Kaur gets key responsibility amid sugar shortage reports Waiting IAS officer Amrit Pal Kaur has been appointed Joint Managing Director of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation. Meanwhile, the charge of Joint Managing Director has been withdrawn from Navneet Sehra, Additional Excise Commissioner and Joint Managing Director of the Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation. Chaitra V., who was serving as Director General, AYUSH and Mission Director, National AYUSH Mission, has been moved to the Revenue Board and appointed Member (Judicial). Reports suggest that she was facing differences with the department’s Principal Secretary Ranjan Kumar and Minister Dayashankar Mishra ‘Dayalu’ over her working style. Both were reportedly unhappy with her functioning, and the matter had also reached CM Yogi Adityanath. IAS officer Chaitra V. had made headlines in August 2025 after accusing Lucknow hotel businessman Naren Raj of serious mental harassment. She lodged an FIR at Alambagh police station, alleging that the businessman was repeatedly harassing her and pressuring her to introduce him to prominent hotel entrepreneurs. Police registered a case based on her complaint and started an investigation. Ravindra Kumar loses Jal Nigam charge Urban Development Department Secretary Ravindra Kumar has been relieved of the additional charge of Managing Director, UP Jal Nigam (Urban), and State Mission Director, AMRUT. Masoom Ali Sarwar has been given additional charge of both posts. He has been relieved of the charge of Secretary, Planning Department. Kumar Prashant gets key post; LDA Secretary shifted to Animal Husbandry Department Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) Secretary Vivek Srivastava has been transferred and appointed Special Secretary in the Animal Husbandry Department. Meanwhile, Kumar Prashant, who had been serving as Secretary of the State Information Commission for a long time, has been appointed Managing Director in the UP Jal Nigam (Rural), and Commissioner Registrar in the Cooperative Department. Other major transfers Overall, the reshuffle has affected several important departments, including Jal Nigam, Cooperative, Higher Education, Animal Husbandry, Revenue and the State Information Commission. Amritpal Kaur is originally from Nanowal Khurd village in Gurdaspur, Punjab. She secured 44th rank across India in the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2018 and was selected for the Indian Administrative Service in the 2019 batch, receiving the Uttar Pradesh cadre. She studied Electrical Engineering at Punjab Engineering College, Chandigarh. Amritpal Kaur has also served as the Chief Development Officer (CDO) of Chitrakoot.

stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh has recorded 15% less rainfall this year, and the impact is clearly visible on the state's dams. Eleven dams currently have less than 10% water, with some almost completely empty. What's striking is that the state's five largest dams — Rihand, Matatila, Obra, Meja and Sharda Sagar — have, on average, filled to only around 50% of capacity. These five dams together generate 429.6 MW of electricity and supply irrigation water to 18-20 districts across UP and Madhya Pradesh, with Sharda Sagar and Matatila supplying the most water. The concern is that a shortfall in the water quota could affect both power generation and irrigation. Here's a district-by-district look at the state's major dams. Three of the five biggest dams on the verge of running dry Dam nearly dry, only 3.7% water — Sharda Sagar: Sharda Sagar is an entirely earthen dam, counted among the largest earthen dams in Asia. It is almost completely dry, with only 3.7% (12,060 thousand cubic metres) of water. For lakhs of farmers in Pilibhit, Lakhimpur Kheri and Shahjahanpur, this is nothing short of a disaster. Irrigating standing paddy and sugarcane crops will become difficult. With the reservoir running empty, the water table in surrounding areas will fall sharply, and handpumps will begin to fail. Wildlife from the Pilibhit Tiger Reserve and Dudhwa could move towards human settlements in search of water. Only 12.9% water, against 45% last year — Obra: The 28-million-cubic-metre-capacity Obra dam is also in poor shape, currently holding just 12.9% (3,600 thousand cubic metres) of water, compared to 45.7% at this time last year. The water shortage is expected to affect the output of both Obra's hydro and thermal power plants. In a hydro power plant, water from the dam falls onto turbines under high pressure, spinning them so the generator can produce electricity — so lower water levels mean the turbines cannot run at full capacity, reducing hydro power generation. In a thermal power plant, coal is burned to convert water into steam, which spins the turbine to generate electricity. These plants also need large volumes of water to keep machinery cool, and a fall in dam water levels could affect the cooling-water supply. Drinking water and the irrigation canal network in Sonbhadra could also be badly hit. Lower water levels can reduce oxygen levels in the reservoir, putting aquatic life at risk. Only 15% water, irrigation crisis all but certain — Meja: The Meja dam has accumulated just 15% (45,730 thousand cubic metres) of water, putting pressure on farmers. If there is no heavy monsoon rainfall in the coming weeks, a severe drinking water and irrigation crisis in the plateau regions of Mirzapur during the summer season is all but certain. 73% full last year, only 41% this year — Matatila: The Matatila dam, built on the Betwa river, has filled to only 41.1% (around 2.31 lakh thousand cubic metres), compared to 72.9% at this time last year. However, this amount is sufficient for the initial sowing and first irrigation of rabi crops (wheat, gram, peas). There will be no drinking water crisis in Lalitpur, Jhansi and nearby towns for the next few months, and the local grid will continue to get support from the turbines running at limited capacity. Around 58.9% of the dam's capacity remains empty. If the remaining monsoon days or winter do not bring good rainfall, Bundelkhand could face a severe water crisis during the peak summer heat of April-May, making it difficult to get water to the far ends of the canal network. Dam 40% empty this monsoon — Rihand: Sonbhadra and Mirzapur together account for 3% of the country's total power generation. Rihand dam, the lifeline of these districts, is in considerably better shape this time — the vast reservoir currently holds 60.1% water, compared to just 32.4% in August last year. With improved water levels at Rihand, not only will the hydro power plant run at full capacity, but Sonbhadra's large thermal power plants will also get enough water for cooling their machinery.

stories.title: Judge writes IAS officer Durga Shakti Nagpal threatened him:Says, “What kind of values do you have? You don’t even know how to speak”
stories.summary: UP’s woman IAS officer Durga Shakti Nagpal is once again in the headlines. She is currently the Commissioner of Devipatan Division. Senior Division Civil Judge Shabina Khan of Gonda wrote a letter to the District Judge against the IAS officer, alleging: “The Commissioner is misusing her position. She put undue pressure on me regarding a pending case and threatened to complain to the High Court. She also questioned my values. I am hurt by this.” In her letter, the judge detailed the conversation she had with the IAS officer and requested that the case be transferred to another court. Following her request, the case was transferred to the court of Civil Judge (FTC) Naveen, Gonda Senior Division. The next hearing is scheduled for August 24, i.e. today. 30 year old case, woman judge alleges pressure from IAS officer This entire matter is related to the 'Jyoti Vidya Mandir vs Municipality' case, which has been pending in the lower court for about 30 years. Since the case is quite old, the court was conducting hearings expeditiously. The case has reached close to disposal. The allegation is that Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal was pressuring the Civil Judge in connection with this very case. Read the sequence of events described by the Civil Judge in her letter ‘I’ll get the case transferred’, IAS officer questioned judge’s upbringing The Civil Judge wrote in the letter that when she tried to explain her point to the Commissioner, she refused to listen. The Commissioner said, “You didn't even give me a chance to speak. You are not receiving my phone calls. I feel like what kind of upbringing do you have?” To this, Civil Judge Shabina Khan replied that she is not obligated to inform about leave period or time. Nor can she discuss cases on fake calls or unknown numbers. She clarified that government lawyers are present in court to represent the government's side. Even after this, the Commissioner expressed her anger by referring to being a senior IAS officer. She said, “I will get the case transferred to the High Court." The judge agreed to this, saying that she can absolutely get the case transferred. Demand to transfer the case to another court accepted Civil Judge Shabina Khan wrote in a letter to the District Judge that the Commissioner misused the influence of his position. He attempted to put undue pressure on her by threatening to file a complaint in the High Court. She requested that in the interest of impartial justice, the case pending in her court be transferred to another court. Her request has been accepted. Commissioner may face contempt proceedings The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court has taken seriously the allegation that Civil Judge Shalini Khan was pressured over a pending land dispute. Justice Syed Qamar Hasan Rizvi said the alleged pressure exerted through a phone call to the judge appears, prima facie, to be a direct attack on judicial independence and an obstruction of the administration of justice. The court said the matter needs to be considered under criminal contempt. It directed that, after seeking guidelines from the Chief Justice, the matter be placed before the appropriate court.

stories.title: Young man falls into boiling jaggery pan, burns alive:Suffers for 1 minute; went to Maharashtra from Lakhimpur to earn ₹70,000
stories.summary: 25 year old youth from Lakhimpur died after falling into a pan of boiling jaggery at a jaggery plant in Maharashtra. He remained trapped in the boiling jaggery for nearly a minute and kept crying, “Save me, brother, save me.” Hearing his cries, his colleagues rushed to help and pulled him out after a lot of effort. By then, he had suffered severe burns and his skin had peeled off. He was taken to a hospital, where he died during treatment. The incident took place on 21 August, and the video surfaced around 9 pm on Sunday. The youth had gone to Maharashtra to work and earn money to repay his family’s ₹70,000 debt. See 4 pictures of the accident... Now, read the full story... Had gone to Maharashtra with 15 others for work Danish (25), a resident of Moodi village in Isanagar, Lakhimpur, had been married for two years. About four months ago, he went to Maharashtra with 15 others for work. He is survived by his wife, two month old son, parents, and elder brother and sister. His elder brother, Guddu, had a debt of ₹70,000, which Danish had gone to Maharashtra to help repay. Now, know how the accident happened… 21 August at 2:25 PM, in the plant, jaggery was boiling in two large cauldrons. All the workers were busy with their respective tasks. Danish came and stood right at the edge of the cauldron. After a while, he felt dizzy and lost his balance. In the blink of an eye, he fell straight into the cauldron of boiling jaggery. He screamed loudly, Save me! Save me! Oh brother, save me! There was chaos throughout the entire plant. Fellow workers ran to the cauldron. No one could understand how to get Danish out. Just then, one worker tried to pull him out with a large ladle. Another also picked up a ladle. When he couldn't be pulled out, without caring for their own lives, two three workers stepped forward and pulled him out of the boiling jaggery. They laid him down on the ground away from the cauldron. The skin of his entire body had peeled off. Danish kept screaming due to pain and burning. Some workers shouted, Bring water! Pour water on him! Hurry up! Family created a ruckus in the village, police showed them CCTV footage After receiving information about the accident, Maharashtra Police conducted a post-mortem of the body. After this, the body was sent to Moodi village. As soon as the body reached the village on Saturday, mourning engulfed the family. Family members accused the laborers who had gone to Maharashtra with Danish and started creating a ruckus. Upon receiving information, Isanagar police reached the village. The police showed the family members the CCTV footage from the plant. After watching the footage, the family members calmed down. CO Shamsher Bahadur Singh said, “The incident had occurred at a jaggery plant in Maharashtra. A police team was sent as a precaution when the body reached the village.” He said, “No written complaint has been received against anyone in the matter so far.”

stories.title: Helicopter wind knocks bikers off road:Banners and hoardings tear; flowers showered on Kanwariyas in Jhansi
stories.summary: Chaos broke out in Jhansi as flowers were showered on Kanwariyas from a helicopter. The helicopter flew very low, creating strong winds from its rotors that affected pedestrians and motorcyclists on the road. Several people lost their balance and fell due to the powerful gusts, while hoardings and banners were blown away. An eyewitness said, “The hoardings and banners were torn, and everything was in disarray. Tables were blown away. The helicopter had come down very low.” The incident took place on Thursday, and a video surfaced on Friday showing the helicopter flying at a low altitude. First, see 4 pictures Commissioner and IG Range had showered flowers BJP leader Sanjeev Shringirishi had taken out a Kanwar Yatra from Orchha to Siddheshwar Temple in Jhansi under the banner of Bundelkhand Kanwar Yatra Committee. The organizers claimed that around 16,000 people participated in the yatra. A state government helicopter was called with the help of Babina MLA to shower flowers on the Kanwariyas. Commissioner Bimal Dubey and IG Range Akash Kulhari showered flowers on the Kanwariyas and devotees of Shiva from the helicopter. The Commissioner had said - Kanwar Yatra has special religious significance in the month of Sawan. It is a matter of joy that a helicopter was arranged in Jhansi to shower flowers on the Kanwariyas. Second time the helicopter returned, the altitude was low As the Kanwariyas' procession reached Elite Chowk, the helicopter took off from the Police Line ground. The first time, the helicopter flew at a safe altitude and showered flowers on the Kanwariyas from there. Then, when the helicopter reached above Elite Chowk for the second time, its altitude became quite low. As the helicopter descended, strong winds started blowing from its rotors. At the chowk, Kanwariyas were on one lane of the road, while vehicles were moving on the other lane. Several bike riders fell on the road due to the helicopter's wind. The wind was so strong that hoardings and banners along the roadside also started flying. People questioned safety standards After this incident, people are raising questions as to why the helicopter was brought to such a low altitude to shower flowers. Were the prescribed safety standards followed during the helicopter's operation? The Kanwar Yatra started from Orchha and reached Siddheshwar Temple via Satar, Orchha Tigailla, Bhagwantpura, Risala Chungi, Bus Stand, Kachehri Chauraha, Jail Chauraha, Elite Chauraha, Jeevanshah and BKD Chauraha. Here, Lord Shiva was offered water (Jalabhishek). It was during this time that flowers were showered.

stories.title: UP to curb app based cab drivers’ arbitrary practices:₹100 fine for refusing pickups; drivers to get ₹5 lakh insurance
stories.summary: Those who book cabs through apps and travel will now get relief from arbitrary fares and poor service in UP. The Yogi government has implemented new rules-2026 for app-based cabs, passenger transport, delivery, and logistics services. The name of the rules is Uttar Pradesh Motor Vehicles (Aggregator and Distribution Service Provider)-2026. Under this, rules have been set from fares to driver verification, passenger insurance, and complaint resolution. The government has also launched the UP My Fleet portal for monitoring. Two aggregators providing facilities to customers and their 3,15,218 vehicles are onboarded on this portal. Now, when demand for cabs increases at a particular time, companies will be able to increase fares by a maximum of 50% above the base fare. This means it will not be easy to charge arbitrary fares in the name of peak time or high demand. If, after booking, the driver does not reach to pick up the passenger without proper reason, a fine of ₹100 will be imposed. There is a provision to give this amount to the passenger as a benefit on the next trip. Drivers to get ₹5 lakh health, ₹10 lakh term insurance Police and character verification will be conducted for every driver associated with aggregators. Apart from this, psychological testing of drivers and refresher training from time to time will also be done. Provision has been made to provide health insurance of ₹5 lakh and term insurance of ₹10 lakh for drivers. Meanwhile, it will be the responsibility of the aggregator to insure every passenger. Company will have a grievance officer Every app company will have to appoint a Grievance Redressal Officer. Passengers will be able to directly lodge complaints related to fares, bookings, drivers, or services. Fines can also be imposed on the company for violating rules or motor vehicle laws. ₹5 lakh fee for aggregator license The application fee for an aggregator has been fixed at ₹25,000 and the license fee at ₹5 lakh. The security deposit will also be determined based on the number of vehicles. Delivery and logistics companies also within the ambit of rules The new arrangement is not limited to just app cabs. Digital platforms that connect drivers with e-commerce companies, vendors or other people for delivery of parcels, packages and couriers will also come under its purview. Vehicle pollution will also be monitored Through the UP My Fleet portal, information about vehicles associated with aggregators, compliance with rules, and pollution status will be monitored. The government has also emphasized promoting electric vehicles instead of petrol-diesel vehicles and gradually converting the fleet to EVs.

stories.title: Japanese student takes selfie with CM Yogi:Puts arm around his shoulder; student says, ‘I wore 'Bindi' for first time, loved it'
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath met Japanese students in Lucknow on Friday (21 Aug). When the students performed a Japanese song, Yogi encouraged them by applauding, he then posed for photographs with the group. As some students began taking selfies from a distance, Yogi called them closer and happily posed with them. During one selfie, a Japanese student placed her hand on the CM’s shoulder, prompting Yogi to burst into laughter. On the occasion, Ishan from Uttar Pradesh also performed ‘Kaushalya Dashrath Ke Nandan’, a song dedicated to Lord Ram. Japanese student Miyagi Moto said, “I wore a bindi for the first time and liked it very much." She described her experience in India as "unique". See pictures… Yogi welcomes students with ‘Ohayo Gozaimasu’ CM Yogi organized the 'A Dialogue with the Future' program at the Chief Minister's residence under the UP Japan Investment Meeting. In this, 13 students from Japan and their faculty members interacted with students from Lucknow. Yogi began his address with the Japanese greeting 'Ohayo Gozaimasu'. He said, “Uttar Pradesh is the country's largest state with a population of more than 25 crore. It is a major center of India's spiritual and cultural heritage.” Yogi, 'Meeting of the younger generations of 2 countries' CM Yogi said, “This is not just a meeting of students, but a dialogue between two cultures, traditions and young generations of India and Japan. Such programs will help in further strengthening friendship and relations between both countries.” He further added, “For students coming from Japan, the visit to Uttar Pradesh is also an opportunity to closely understand the spirituality, culture and historical heritage here.”

stories.title: Action against BHU MA student Raunak Mishra:Suspended and barred from campus entry; decision taken at permanent committee meeting
stories.summary: Banaras Hindu University (BHU) has taken strict disciplinary action against MA student Raunak Mishra over multiple alleged incidents of indiscipline. The university has suspended him under ECR-264 and imposed several restrictions during the suspension period. He will not be allowed to access the university’s academic facilities, hostel or library. His entry into the university campus has also been restricted for the duration of the suspension. According to an order issued by Deputy Registrar Ranjit Shandilya, five FIRs are registered against Raunak Mishra, while previous incidents of alleged indiscipline have also been reported against him. The cases were presented before the university’s Standing Committee by the BHU Chief Proctor’s Office. After reviewing the allegations, case details and the student’s previous record, the committee recommended disciplinary action. Standing Committee meeting held on 11 August According to the university administration's order, a Standing Committee meeting regarding matters related to Raunak Mishra was held on 11 August. In the meeting, a detailed review was conducted of the cases registered against the student, previous actions taken, and facts that came to light. Considering the seriousness of the matter, the committee decided to impose various restrictions including suspension on the student. Based on the Standing Committee's recommendation, the university administration has now issued an official order. Suspension had been revoked earlier too The university administration has also referred to Raunak Mishra’s previous disciplinary case in its order. According to the university, his suspension and other restrictions were revoked on February 27, 2025. At the time, he was advised to refrain from any further acts of indiscipline. However, the administration said that despite the warning, fresh allegations of indiscipline were later reported against him. Taking the previous action and subsequent cases into account, the Chief Proctor’s Office placed the matter before the Standing Committee. Following the committee’s review and recommendation, the university has once again taken strict disciplinary action against the student. Banned from academic facilities, hostel and library During the suspension period, Raunak Mishra will not be able to participate in the university's academic activities. He will also not be permitted to use the university's academic facilities. Additionally, hostel facilities and use of the university library have also been restricted. The most significant restriction is regarding entry to the university campus. Until the order remains in effect, the student will not be able to enter the campus. The BHU administration's action has come at a time when the administration is continuously emphasizing strictness regarding student safety and discipline on the university campus. The administration states, “Cases of indiscipline in the university are examined under prescribed rules and action is taken based on the recommendations of relevant committees.” Fresh cases emerged despite previous action The administration's order specifically mentions, "Action had been taken against Raunak Mishra before and later, giving him relief, the suspension was withdrawn. At that time, he was advised to stay away from undisciplined activities in the future. Now after allegations surfaced again, the university has taken the matter seriously and imposed suspension and other restrictions based on the standing committee's recommendation.

stories.title: Search for 4 people drowned in Ganga enters fifth day:Sister pleads, ‘Find my brother; who will I tie Rakhi to now?’
stories.summary: Five days after four youths drowned in the Ganga at Bithoor and Dyodhi Ghat in Kanpur, the search for them remains unsuccessful. Police, NDRF, PAC divers and family members have been searching across more than 100 km, but no trace of the youths has been found. At Dyodhi Ghat, the sister of the only brother who drowned broke down while pleading with police officers and divers. With folded hands, she said, “I am holding your feet, please find my only brother.” Family members have spent five days following the search teams, often without food or water, and are now exhausted and deeply disappointed. According to police, the strong current in the Ganga and water levels near the warning mark are making the search difficult. Despite this, teams continue to search for the missing youths from Kanpur to Prayagraj. Sister grieves losing only brother before Rakshabandhan On 17 August, at Dyodhi Ganga Ghat in the Maharajpur police station area of Kanpur, Krishna (16), a resident of Raja Market Ahirwan, and Shiva Shukla (17), a resident of Patel Nagar, drowned while bathing in the Ganga. Four friends, Surya, Virag, Krishna, and Shiva, had come together to Dyodhi Ganga Ghat for a bath in the Ganga. While bathing, Krishna and Shiva suddenly got caught in the strong current of the Ganga and were submerged in deep water. Upon receiving information about his son's drowning, Shiva's father Alok Shukla reached the ghat and informed the police. Police from Maharajpur station, NDRF, and PSC divers have been continuously combing the area since the incident. Combing was conducted for more than 100 km up to Fatehpur, but no clue has been found. After the only son drowned, father Alok Shukla, mother, and both sisters Kanchan and Juhi became distraught. For five days continuously, family members have been engaged in searching for Shiva at every ghat along with the combing teams. Shiva's sisters Kanchan and Juhi became inconsolable crying at the ghat. They said, “Before Raksha Bandhan, my brother was taken away, now to whom will I tie the rakhi, please find my brother somehow...” Seeing the sisters crying so much, even the eyes of the police officers and other people present at the ghat became moist. DCP East Satyajit Gupta informed that police teams along with PAC divers and NDRF teams are engaged in searching for Shiva and Krishna who drowned at Dyodhi Ghat. The search for both bodies is being conducted from Kanpur to Prayagraj. Due to flooding in the Ganga, no trace of either has been found. Grief grips families after cousin brothers drown Sachendi police station area resident Abhishek Sonkar of Chakarpur Mandi had reached Bithoor's Gudara Ganga Ghat with his cousin brother Ashiq Sonkar (16) and maternal cousin Satish Sonkar (18) on a bike at around 3 am on the morning of 17 August to bathe in the Ganga. During bathing, Ashiq and Satish started drowning in the strong current due to going too far from the ghat. Both were bathing after crossing the rope placed at the warning point, due to which even the people present there could not gather the courage to save them. After the accident, family members and police reached the spot. For the fifth consecutive day, teams of police along with PAC and NDRF are combing, but due to strong current in the Ganga and increased water level, no trace has been found so far. Families devastated as search for both youths continues Since the accident, Ashiq's mother Rani, sister Shalu, and family members have been inconsolable with grief. Along with this, Satish's mother Anita and elder brother Vikas are also devastated with crying. Both families are engaged in the search along with police and divers. DCP West SM Kasim Abidi informed that along with the police, PAC divers and NDRF team are engaged in searching for both of them. Due to the flood in the Ganga, no clue about both of them has been found yet.

stories.title: Yogi says, 'Akhilesh insulted Kalyan Singh':Didn’t even pay tribute; ‘They’re vultures that devour the tree they climb’
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party on the 5th death anniversary of former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Kalyan Singh. Speaking in Lucknow on Friday, he said, “Akhilesh Yadav did not even pay tribute to “Babuji,” calling it a reflection of his hatred for the BJP leader.” Yogi said, "The act was not only an insult to Kalyan Singh but also a caste-based insult. He said, This was an insult to every Hindu who believes that Babuji's life was dedicated to Sanatan values and Hindu pride. Sakshi Maharaj rightly said that what will these people say now, there is no trust. They are like vultures who will devour the very tree they climb. CM Yogi Adityanath also took a dig at the Samajwadi Party’s PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) formula. He said, "Those who ‘change colours like chameleons’ according to the situation keep giving different meanings to the letter ‘P’.” He claimed, “They sometimes define 'P' as backward, at other times as Pandit, and one day may even start defining it as Pakistan.” The BJP observes Kalyan Singh’s death anniversary as Hindu Pride Day. A programme was organized at Lucknow’s Ekana Stadium on the occasion. Minister of State (Independent Charge) Sandeep Singh, Kalyan Singh’s grandson, and his son and former MP Rajveer Singh, popularly known as “Raju Bhaiya,” were also present. CM Yogi praised BSP supremo Mayawati “Babuji’s demise was an unbearable moment for us. PM Modi cancelled all his programmes and came directly from Delhi to Lucknow to pay tribute to Babuji. As a matter of courtesy, former CM Mayawati also came and paid her respects to Babuji.", said CM Yogi. Now read the CM's important statements 1. 'A great person is not great because of position, but because of their thinking...' The CM said, “I got the opportunity to be with Babuji for a long time in various programs. A great person is not great because of their position, but becomes great and noble through their thinking and actions. Born in an ordinary farmer's family in Atrauli, Babuji was steadfast in his diligence, values and principles.” He worked with the spirit of serving the nation. He was a volunteer trained in the school of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. He fulfilled all important constitutional responsibilities as a farmer, teacher, MLA, Minister, Chief Minister, MP and Governor. 2. Babuji used to say, ‘Kalyan Singh can break, but cannot bend…’ For every Indian for whom the nation comes first and India's eternal values and ideals are paramount, Babuji will always remain a source of inspiration. His life was filled with simplicity, penance, dedication and struggle. He fought against injustice. He confronted oppression. While protecting eternal values, he dedicated his entire life to villages, the poor, farmer food-providers, youth and society. No matter how much pressure was put on Babuji for wrong work, he never worked under pressure. He used to say, "Kalyan Singh can break, but cannot bend." He lived up to this promise throughout his life. 3. ‘Babuji accepted losing power, but never ordered firing on Ram devotees’ During the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, he had said, “Struggle is acceptable and losing power is also acceptable, but disrespect to Lord Shri Ram is not acceptable. Today when we see the grand temple of Lord Shri Ram in Ayodhya, Babuji's memory always rises in our hearts." He continued, "Babuji openly supported the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. He accepted losing power, but said that bullets will not be fired on Ram devotees.” 4. Government will not hesitate to fulfil Babuji’s dreams Babuji gave UP an identity. Protected India's Sanatan values. Paved the way for Ram Mandir by demolishing the structure of slavery in Ayodhya. The double engine government will walk on Babuji's ideals. Will take every step to realize his dreams. Will not hesitate in this.
