‘Patently unlawful’: US judge strikes down Trump admin’s immigrant visa freeze for 75 countries
'No compromise': BJP passes resolution against Congress on Vande Mataram; vows nationwide protest
stories.summary: The BJP has condemned the Congress party's decision to sing only two stanzas of Vande Mataram. This move is seen by the BJP as undermining the national song's significance and legacy. The party passed a resolution to protect the honor and national character of the complete Vande Mataram. Union Home Minister Amit Shah also attacked the Congress Working Committee's resolution as anti-national.

stories.title: Age limit, two-term cap: DMK passes nine resolutions for sweeping organisational overhaul
Plea in SC seeks Manan Mishra's removal after he refuses to step down amid NALSAR row
IndiGo A321neo grounded after tail impact during Gorakhpur landing
stories.summary: An IndiGo Airbus A321neo aircraft experienced a tail impact during its landing approach. The flight from Delhi to Gorakhpur made a successful landing on its third attempt. Scratches were observed around the APU inlet during a post-flight inspection. The aircraft remains grounded at Gorakhpur airport for necessary maintenance. Technical and regulatory clearances are awaited before the plane resumes operations.

stories.title: BJP forms Gen Z outreach team: Nitin Nabin, Smriti Irani and Vinod Tawde among key faces
BJP plans nationwide 'Seva Pakhwada' from Sept 17 ahead of PM Modi's 25 years in public office
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is set to launch a nationwide 15-day campaign, 'Seva Sankalp Mahotsav', to highlight Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 25-year journey in public life and organise service-oriented programmes across the country.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Socrates: "The difficulty, my friends, is not in avoiding death, but..."
Asia’s high-mountain ‘water tower’ is losing 24 billion tonnes of groundwater annually, new research finds
stories.summary: Groundwater reserves in High Mountain Asia are experiencing severe depletion annually due to a combination of climate impacts and excessive human water usage. The irrigation needs in the lower basins dramatically exacerbate groundwater storage losses. If current consumption trends continue, projections suggest that depletion will persist. Although temporary glacier melt may provide a short reprieve, this will be followed by a more rapid decline.

stories.title: New snake species named after Guns N’ Roses guitarist Slash; here’s why scientists chose him
stories.summary: In a fascinating discovery, scientists have unveiled a new non-venomous snake species from New Guinea, named Lielaphis slashi. This remarkable naming pays tribute to Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash, also known as Saul Hudson, who has always been captivated by reptiles and the natural world. First encountered during past fieldwork, this small ground-dwelling snake signifies the incredible biodiversity and urgent conservation efforts needed in New Guinea.

stories.title: Logan Paul has listed his 78-acre California ranch with an extraordinary past for sale at $3 million
stories.summary: Logan Paul has put his notorious California ranch on the market for three million dollars. Once the base for Timothy Leary's LSD operation, this secluded 78-acre property boasts an off-grid retreat experience. Acquired by Paul in 2019, the ranch has seen numerous enhancements. Speculation suggests he may now shift his real estate focus to Puerto Rico.

Jaishankar to visit Russia on August 23-24; focus on trade, scientific cooperation

This $15 million New York home almost disappears into the forest on its 19.5-acre wooded estate
stories.summary: Nestled in Pound Ridge, New York, this extraordinary home is listed for fifteen million dollars. Its mirrored facade seamlessly merges with the lush forest while reflecting the beauty of each season. Crafted by KieranTimberlake, the design emphasizes harmony with nature. Inside, expansive glass walls invite vibrant woodland views, creating a tranquil indoor-outdoor flow. This distinctive residence promises both privacy and proximity to New York City.

stories.title: AICTE opens select MTech programmes to 4-year BSc graduates
Of funds from 19 common donors in 2024, BJP got nearly four times as much as Congress
stories.summary: During FY2024-25, national political parties disclosed over ₹6,600 crore in donations, with the BJP claiming the lion's share at more than ₹6,000 crore. Notably, nineteen donors were recorded on filings for both BJP and Congress, contributing nearly ₹258 crore collectively. This highlights the significant sway that the business and corporate sectors hold over political financing in India.

stories.title: Rs 5 crore to suppress rape case? NHRC directs Punjab to probe allegations against CM Mann’s wife
BJP chief Nitin Nabin holds first meeting with new team ahead of polls
stories.summary: Nitin Nabin led the BJP's new national team in their first meeting. They discussed upcoming assembly elections and grassroots outreach efforts. The party unveiled a 65-member team with many new faces appointed. Key positions saw Vasundhara Raje and Ram Madhav named vice presidents. Piyush Goyal returned as treasurer while other roles were also filled.

stories.title: 14 yrs on, NMC still trying to update national register of docs
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission is putting forth a new proposal for mandatory re-registration of doctors across the nation. In the past, efforts to modernize the national registry faced significant challenges. The current regulations suggest that registration would be recognized nationwide, eliminating the need for state-level re-registration. This initiative aims to refresh the medical register while pinpointing active practitioners, striving for an electronic sync between national and state medical registers.

stories.title: Bottle Caps Transform Home: Olga Kostina turns 30,000 into folk-art mosaic; remote house becomes landmark
stories.summary: In a remarkable display of creativity, Olga Kostina, a pensioner from Russia, has transformed her wooden home into a stunning folk art installation. By affixing over thirty thousand colorful plastic bottle caps onto her house, she has crafted intricate patterns that captivate both locals and visitors alike. This project highlights the innovative repurposing of waste materials into a meaningful and eye-catching art piece, positioning her home as a noteworthy landmark.

stories.title: In 2000, Cornell began pulling water from 250 feet below Cayuga Lake to cool its campus; now its energy use has been reduced by 85%
stories.summary: Launched in 2000, Cornell University's lake source cooling system exemplifies sustainable innovation, utilizing the icy waters of Cayuga Lake to meet the campus's cooling demands. This groundbreaking initiative, which commenced construction in 1999, achieved an extraordinary eighty-five percent cut in annual energy consumption, positioning the university at the forefront of eco-friendly solutions for the future.

stories.title: 'Antisemitic dictator': Netanyahu slams Erdogan after Turkey seeks Interpol action
stories.summary: Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu fiercely criticized Turkey's President Erdogan after Ankara sought an Interpol notice. Erdogan's government requested the notice concerning an interception of a Gaza aid flotilla. Netanyahu's office labeled Erdogan an antisemitic dictator with numerous accusations. This exchange escalates existing tensions between the two nations over Syria. Both countries are engaged in a diplomatic and legal dispute over these matters.

stories.title: 'Arrogance brings downfall': Jayant Chaudhary on Akhilesh Yadav's 'chavanni' remark
Jammu and Kashmir: NIA raids residential houses in Anantnag as part of terror probe
stories.summary: The National Investigation Agency conducted raids at two locations in Anantnag. These searches occurred in Bijbehara and Dooru areas of south Kashmir. NIA officers, with police and CRPF support, searched residential houses. The agency also raided SICOP in Bijbehara as part of its investigation. Details regarding the outcome of these searches are currently awaited.

At least 2 killed, nine injured in reactor blast at Telangana pharma unit
'We are in position of power': Iran's Pezeshkian seeks end to US war, claims victory
stories.summary: Iranian President Pezeshkian seeks an end to the ongoing conflict, citing national strength and dignity. He defended a past agreement against domestic criticism while military leaders warned of retaliation. Oman and Iran discussed resuming dialogue as the Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint. US President Trump indicated Iran was not ready for a suitable agreement. Washington plans new sanctions, which Iran and China have criticized as ineffective.

After a 1962 storm battered Fire Island, Robert Moses proposed a highway along the New York barrier
stories.summary: The fierce nor'easter of 1962 became a pivotal moment for Robert Moses as he sought to introduce a highway on Fire Island. Yet, the local populace and property owners stood firm against the initiative, worried for their environment and community’s future. Their activism prompted valuable support from the federal government, leading to the creation of Fire Island National Seashore in 1964, which has preserved the island's unspoiled setting.

stories.title: Midway Atoll eradicated invasive rats after Bonin petrels had fallen to fewer than 5,000 nesting pairs
stories.summary: Invasive rats were removed from Midway Atoll, which had devastated native seabird populations. Bonin petrel numbers surged from under five thousand to over one hundred thirty-five thousand pairs. This eradication effort also allowed native vegetation to recover and stabilize the fragile islands. However, invasive house mice later emerged as a new threat to nesting albatrosses. Strict biosecurity measures now protect this vital Pacific sanctuary from further introductions.

stories.summary: 'If India's Future Is Secure, World's Is Too'

In 2005, California began eradicating 5,036 feral pigs from Santa Cruz Island as part of....
stories.summary: The successful eradication of feral pigs from Santa Cruz Island, initiated in 2005 and completed by 2006, played a pivotal role in the recovery of the island fox. Once teetering on the brink of extinction, the island fox population rebounded dramatically. In 2016, federal authorities celebrated the milestone of removing three island fox subspecies from the endangered list, marking the fastest recovery of any mammal under the Endangered Species Act.

stories.summary: In a remarkable environmental achievement, Japan has announced the successful elimination of invasive small Indian mongooses, resolving a long-standing ecological dilemma on its UNESCO World Heritage site. The culmination of rigorous trapping, tracking, and monitoring efforts has set the stage for a revitalization of local wildlife populations, positioning this program among the largest mongoose eradications observed globally.

Woman born without uterus breaks down as she raises £20K for transplant after spending £50K on IVF
stories.summary: A 28-year-old woman born without a uterus is raising £20,000 for embryo creation and testing as she hopes to qualify for a uterus transplant. Molly Eagles and fiancé Matt Crowe have spent nearly £50,000 on IVF and surrogacy, including two embryo transfers and a miscarriage. She says they refuse to give up hope.

stories.title: "Today you are students; tomorrow you will be scientists, artists, leaders": UP CM calls for deeper India-Japan youth ties
stories.summary: Speaking at an interaction in Lucknow with Yamanashi Governor Kotaro Nagasaki, 13 Japanese high school students, and 20 local students from schools across the city, the chief minister urged the younger generation to build lasting connections across borders.

A mother who spent £170k on annexe for disabled daughter’s home in Worcester now faces demolition
stories.summary: A mother who spent £170,000 building a two-storey annexe for her disabled daughter could now be forced to demolish it after losing a planning appeal. Clair Birch, 59, built the one-bedroom annexe in the garden of her semi-detached home in Worcester. She said the building was designed to give her daughter more independence and meet her specific needs.

stories.title: Florida man built a swampy retirement home that became a 12,000-sq-ft castle
stories.summary: In the heart of a Florida swamp, Howard Solomon envisioned and constructed a remarkable medieval-style castle over a span of forty years. Draped in discarded aluminium printing plates from a nearby newspaper, the castle glows with an almost ethereal beauty. This unconventional structure stands not only as a distinctive folk art landmark but also as a true testament to Solomon's creative brilliance.

stories.title: In 1890, US printed 120,000 unusual $100 'Watermelon' notes; only about 35 are known to survive
stories.summary: In October, a unique 1890 'Watermelon' $100 Treasury Note will be up for auction, presenting collectors with a rare opportunity. With only about thirty-five of these notes still in existence, this particular note symbolizes a significant political clash over monetary policy. Its distinct back design, reminiscent of watermelons, earned it this quirky nickname, making it a truly historic piece of currency.

Not just Indian techies, why the 'American Dream' died for Harry and Meghan Markle
stories.summary: The UK that awaits the Sussexes is hardly a triumphant restoration like the one that greeted Charles II post-Cromwell. The Sussexes will live privately and have to figure out how to pay their rent. The King won’t even give an allowance the way he does to the disgraced Prince Andrew, and their popularity is hitting rock bottom.

stories.summary: In Texas, a resourceful seventh-grader has crafted an underwater robot to analyze pond water quality. This clever invention measures environmental variables at varying depths across twelve ponds. Results demonstrated that artificial fountains greatly enhance water quality and support aquatic life. This remarkable endeavor secured him a spot as a finalist for national junior innovator honors, with Caden Pohlkamp now seeking to expand his environmental robotics initiatives.

stories.summary: A federal jury awarded a California family $12.7 million for their Santa Cruz Island ranch. The government had seized the 6,300-acre property using eminent domain in 1996. This verdict concluded a decades-long property dispute between park officials and the Gherini family. The family's ancestors had owned part of the island since the late 19th century. The award allowed the National Park Service to gain full control of the land.

In 1986, a family sold California's 53,000-acre Santa Rosa Island to the US for nearly $30 million
stories.summary: In 1986, the United States government acquired Santa Rosa Island for close to thirty million dollars. This pivotal purchase marked the end of longstanding private ranching and agricultural practices on the sprawling island. Following the removal of cattle in 1998 and the cessation of residency in 2011, efforts towards environmental restoration commenced. Today, the island stands as a protected national sanctuary and an important cultural landmark.

Chicago's mayor carved six Xs into a runway; 12 years later, the airfield became a 40-acre park
stories.summary: Chicago's Meigs Field airport was controversially closed overnight in 2003. Six X-shaped gouges rendered the runway unusable, stranding sixteen aircraft. The city cited security concerns following the September 11 attacks for the closure. Twelve years later, the former airfield became a natural landscape. This site now features prairie, wetlands, and wildlife habitat for migratory birds.

stories.title: 'A border state': Akali leader Majithia fuels buzz over SAD-BJP reunion, gives this reason
stories.summary: Bikram Singh Majithia of the Shiromani Akali Dal expressed that public sentiment is leaning towards an alliance with the BJP. He highlighted Punjab's strategic location and the importance of social harmony as pivotal factors. The two parties had a longstanding relationship before parting ways over farm laws. Majithia emphasised that the final decision will come from the leadership of both sides, leaving the results of this potential collaboration uncertain.

'His personal views': Punjab Congress distances itself from Deepender Hooda over Sajjan Kumar tribute row
stories.summary: Punjab Congress leaders distanced the party from Deepender Singh Hooda's remarks. Hooda described Sajjan Kumar, a 1984 riots convict, as a nationwide role model. The party stated its support for riot victims and their affected families. Hooda's comments drew sharp criticism from Sikh groups and opposition parties. Sajjan Kumar, convicted in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, died recently.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: FIR lodged over protester's pellet injury; govt explains why T'gana CM's US visit was scrapped, and more
stories.summary: In a significant action, Delhi Police have filed an FIR concerning a student protester’s complaint about a pellet injury. Meanwhile, the Ministry of External Affairs has denied political clearance for Telangana CM Revanth Reddy's trip to the US, deeming the visit inappropriate. In another incident, an Andhra MP's son faced charges after allegedly causing a fatal incident involving his Aston Martin.

stories.title: An English town installed a bridge whose deck contains 140 recycled plastic bottles
stories.summary: A vibrant addition to an English town's landscape, a six-meter swing bridge constructed from recycled plastic bottles has just been unveiled. This bridge, which opens manually for river traffic, is integral to a multi-million-pound project aimed at restoring the Wilts & Berks Canal and establishing a public 600-meter stretch of waterway. Its completion represents a bold step toward enhancing local heritage.

Scientists find a new frog species hidden in a museum drawer for a century
stories.summary: In a surprising revelation, a common frog species from Ecuador and Colombia remained misnamed for more than a century. Researchers uncovered this taxonomic blunder through a careful review of historical museum specimens and identified it as Pristimantis milpe. This finding underscores the vital role that archived collections play in advancing scientific knowledge and correcting longstanding misconceptions in taxonomy.

Rahul Gandhi dharna: Police register FIR on protester's pellet injury complaint
stories.summary: Delhi Police registered an FIR regarding a student protester's alleged pellet-gun injury. Rahul Gandhi staged a sit-in after alleging the complaint was initially refused. The student, Sahil Lochab, claims over 200 pellets lodged in his body. He stated his vision in one eye remains unclear after surgery. The protest concerned alleged irregularities and the NEET paper-leak controversy.

stories.title: Louisiana man’s floating hunting lodge can move for duck season and is listed at $5.5 million
stories.summary: A unique luxury lodge named Fowl Play is available for $5.5 million in Louisiana. This property is built on floating barges and can be towed into the marsh. It offers waterfront living and outdoor adventure for up to twenty-two people. The lodge provides a commercial-grade kitchen and upscale amenities for guests. This mobile retreat combines hunting and fishing experiences from a single base.

stories.summary: Over the last two centuries, Ohio has witnessed a drastic decline in wetlands, significantly affecting wildlife habitats. However, the land preserved around a nuclear power plant serves as an essential sanctuary for endangered spotted turtles. These turtles thrive in shallow waters rich in vegetation, and the plant's ongoing operations offer a critical generational opportunity for their survival. This unexpected refuge demonstrates nature's remarkable ability to endure amidst human expansion.

stories.title: Congress’s renewed youth outreach: How CJP has forced political parties to course correct
stories.summary: Student protests at Jantar Mantar have prompted political parties to rethink their youth engagement strategies. The Congress party is now focusing on youth issues and expanding its outreach programs nationwide. Rahul Gandhi's recent actions highlight the party's renewed commitment to addressing student concerns. The Congress Working Committee has proposed an education-to-employment roadmap for young people. This shift reflects a broader effort to regain support among the nation's youth.

stories.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy's planned visit to the US has been denied political clearance by the Ministry of External Affairs, which found the proposed activities unsuitable. However, he has secured clearance for his trip to the UK. As a result, the Chief Minister's office confirmed the cancellation of the US portion, prompting an earlier return to Hyderabad than originally planned.

stories.summary: Eliza Homans made a remarkable contribution of 140 acres to establish Acadia National Park, incorporating breathtaking locations like the Bowl and the Beehive. This generous act marked the first significant donation to the Hancock County Trustees of Public Reservation, laying the groundwork for the park's creation. In recognition of her impact, Homans Path was later integrated into the park's expansive trail system, ensuring her legacy persists within its natural beauty.

stories.title: 'Attention-seeking': Nadda says Rahul's sit-in bid to divert attention from Vande Mataram row
stories.summary: Union minister JP Nadda slammed Rahul Gandhi for staging a protest outside a police station, labeling it a desperate bid for media coverage. Nadda asserted that the demonstration was merely an effort to distract from the ongoing Vande Mataram controversy tied to Congress. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi sought to address police brutality towards students—an issue the Supreme Court is currently reviewing following the July 20 incident.

stories.title: 'What's going on in the country?' Kejriwal slams BJP over attack on CJP volunteers in Rajasthan
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal has accused BJP supporters of assaulting volunteers from the Cockroach Janata Party during their inspection of a local school. Reports indicate that the volunteers faced violence and had their vehicles damaged by villagers. They expressed frustration over police inaction, demanding that those responsible be arrested within 48 hours.

stories.title: CM Dhami says government is committed to making women, youth and rural entrepreneurs self-reliant
‘Politics of anarchy’: BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi over police station protest
stories.summary: The BJP criticized Rahul Gandhi for protesting outside a police station. He sought an FIR regarding alleged pellet gun injuries suffered by a student. The BJP stated an FIR was already registered and a committee was investigating. Rahul Gandhi accused the Home Minister of being scared of justice. The Congress leader continued his protest until an FIR was filed.

Did CM Vijay 'dilute' Tamil Nadu's delimitation stand? TVK, DMK clash in assembly
Streamer Nitro_Camden’s Twitch stream takes an unexpected turn after StableRonaldo sends 15,000 viewers
stories.summary: Nitro_Camden, a Twitch streamer, saw his viewer count skyrocket following a raid. However, the celebration was short-lived when his mother barged in, frustrated with the noise, and unplugged his gaming gear. The unexpected showdown became a viral sensation on social media, emphasizing the unpredictable dynamics of live streaming and the impact of personal life on online popularity.

stories.title: UAE is turning desert sand into eco-friendly bricks, the method cuts cement needed for construction to nearly half
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking study, researchers have engineered eco-friendly bricks using desert sand and various industrial by-products. These bricks boast enhanced sulfate resistance when compared to traditional cement options. An innovative curing process at room temperature minimizes energy use, offering a sustainable alternative to Portland cement. However, further industrial evaluations are essential for these bricks to gain traction in the market.

stories.title: In 1962, 5 Swans escaped a Maryland estate; 40 years later, about 4,000 threatened the Bay
stories.summary: Five mute swans escaped from an estate in Maryland in 1962 and their descendants multiplied to nearly 4,000 in the Chesapeake Bay region within four decades. The invasive birds eat large amounts of underwater grasses and have also been linked to the displacement of native birds, raising concerns among wildlife managers about their growing impact on the Bay's ecosystem.

stories.title: 19-year-old Canadian student's invention helps people with cerebral palsy paint and write; sold in 25+ countries
stories.summary: Lianna Genovese, a Canadian student, has created an inspiring device called Guided Hands to assist children with cerebral palsy in expressing their creativity through painting. This innovative tool harnesses arm and shoulder movements, enabling young artists to engage with touch screens effectively. Originally composed of basic materials, Guided Hands has transformed into a recognized commercial assistive technology, earning accolades worldwide for its significant impact.

stories.title: Delhi government orders construction ban for 42 days to tackle winter air pollution
stories.summary: Delhi will ban all construction activities from December 10 to January 20. This measure aims to control the city's severe winter air pollution levels. AI-enabled cameras and a Dust Portal will monitor construction sites for violations. The government will issue warnings and fines for non-compliance with the new rules. Citizens are encouraged to report any observed construction work during this period.

stories.summary: A 16-year-old Tennessee girl is facing assault and disorderly conduct charges after authorities said she ran onto a football field during a middle school game and tackled a player involved in a scuffle. The game was ended early, and the girl was later released to her parents. She has also been banned from school properties for life and from Cornersville Middle School athletic events for one year.

Iowa family moves a $12,000 farmhouse four miles on wheels for dream home
stories.summary: An adventurous Iowa family took on the challenge of rescuing an abandoned farmhouse they believed held untold stories. By moving the century-old building four miles to their land, they endeavored to preserve history while crafting their dream home. Faced with surprising renovations and repair costs, they shared their transformative journey online, earning a global audience and ultimately building a unique family haven that mingled modern life with historical charm.

US scientists are building a $12 million 'digital brain' for drones inspired by insects
stories.summary: At Penn State, a research team is pioneering advanced drone decision-making systems modeled after insect neural mechanisms. Utilizing analogue computing alongside graphene materials, this initiative focuses on onboard data processing that replicates the natural filtering and coincidence detection seen in biology. With annual demonstrations of evolving prototypes, the goal is to enable fully autonomous drone swarms independent of external support.

stories.title: Detroit school students can earn $100 every week just by attending all their classes
In 1944, 29 reindeer were left on a remote island in Alaska, decades later, they had eaten themselves
stories.summary: Twenty-nine reindeer introduced to St. Matthew Island in 1944 grew to over 6,000 animals. This population boom led to severe overgrazing of the island's lichen food sources. An extreme winter in 1963-1964 brought devastating blizzards and deep snow. These harsh conditions prevented reindeer from accessing their depleted food supplies. Ultimately, the entire reindeer herd perished, leaving the island devoid of these animals.

stories.title: 'Waiting for astrologer to fix date?' Udhayanidhi Stalin challenges Vijay to prove corruption claims

stories.summary: On Thursday, North Korea fired ten short-range ballistic missiles into eastern waters, a provocative move following the United States' decision to reduce joint military exercises with South Korea. The South Korean military enhanced its monitoring efforts and shared intelligence with its allies. Meanwhile, North Korea dismissed diplomatic outreach from the US President as unworthy of a response. Such missile tests violate United Nations Security Council resolutions.

stories.title: UP mother killed by train while trying to save son threatening suicide over liquor money
stories.summary: A mother tragically died after pushing her son from a train's path. The son had attempted suicide following an argument over money for alcohol. He had rushed onto the railway tracks as a train approached. His mother intervened, saving his life but losing her own. The injured son was hospitalized for treatment in Varanasi.

This led to significant ecological issues, as the absence of natural predators allowed their numbers to explode, resulting in harm to delicate coastal ecosystems and native species. A comprehensive eradication initiative was launched, successfully culling almost 7,000 reindeer, thereby aiding the natural recuperation of the damaged habitats, with native flora and seabirds starting to reappear.

She defended her longtime artist, Anko, explaining that he creates her livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his creative process. Valkyrae said she understands why people may suspect AI but stressed, “But it’s not AI.” She also expressed concern about AI threatening artists’ jobs and livelihoods.

stories.title: Vande Mataram row: BJP chief Nabin slams Congress, calls it new Muslim League
Owens Questions SD Card Handling: Video shows Terrell pocket card; chain of custody remains debated
stories.summary: Candace Owens’ newly highlighted footage has reignited scrutiny over an SD card removed from a camera positioned behind Charlie Kirk. Owens questions why the card was allegedly taken so quickly and why the person involved appeared to use his phone rather than collect other cards. She stresses that her interpretation is opinion, while raising questions about the footage’s handling, possible communication and why that recording was prioritized.

NCERT recasts political science textbook panel; 4 with RSS links among 20 members
stories.summary: NCERT has recast the team for preparing political science textbooks for Classes XI and XII, with one of the two books slated to be ready by Nov. The 20-member panel includes faculty from JNU, DU, IGNOU and NLU Delhi, among others. At least four members have links, past or present, with organisations associated with RSS-BJP.

stories.title: Maine’s Millinocket lost more than jobs after 2008 mill closure; locals now hope for revival
stories.summary: Millinocket, Maine, once thrived around Great Northern Paper Company, but the mill’s 2008 closure transformed the community. In Peter Santenello’s exploration, longtime residents recall lost jobs, stability and a shared way of life, while local businesses and tourism offer hope. As the town seeks new industry, its resilient residents remain determined to rebuild.

If accused has right to silence, cops have right to arrest: SC
stories.summary: Counsel for Sumit Roy emphasized his right to silence in a land-grabbing case, while the Supreme Court highlighted the police's equal authority to make arrests. Following court directives, Roy presented himself to the investigation officer but chose not to respond to the questions asked by the authorities. The court had previously granted him interim pre-arrest bail, providing some protection amidst this legal turmoil.

82-year-old Tony Fahey builds ‘walking on water’ machine for charity record
stories.summary: At 82, Tony Fahey embarks on a daring 24-hour world record attempt on water using a unique human-powered vessel named the aqua elliptica. This remarkable challenge seeks to generate funds for Make-A-Wish UK, reflecting his commitment to supporting children with serious health conditions. Following a serious accident years ago, Fahey returns to the water to showcase his remarkable endurance and innovative spirit.

stories.title: Collectors of border states to decide citizenship applications under CAA
Meet Audrey Zheng, the 17-year-old Pennsylvania student who developed a...
stories.summary: A talented high school student has pioneered a cutting-edge bioengineering method for the early detection of pancreatic cancer. By utilizing magnetic beads to isolate tumor-derived particles from blood samples, her clinical trials demonstrated remarkable accuracy. Her extraordinary research has secured her a spot as a national finalist in a prestigious science competition, offering a promising new avenue for timely diagnosis and improved patient survival outcomes.

stories.title: Disability rights groups raise concern over Census enumeration framework
In 1961, British scientists stopped farming a 4-hectare barley field and left it alone; 60 years later...
stories.summary: A groundbreaking six-decade study reveals that passive rewilding effectively fosters the development of lush native woodlands. Through protective thorny scrub, young trees thrived, shielded from herbivores, while wind and jays ingeniously spread seeds, outlining the woodlands’ unique patterns. After fifty years, the area began to mirror the characteristics of ancient woodlands, showcasing an eco-friendly and budget-friendly approach to achieving woodland restoration objectives.

stories.title: PM Modi's Gen Z, Gen Alpha outreach: Ministers told to visit universities, govt schools
In 1963, a California builder made a house that rotates 320 degrees using two washing-machine motors
stories.summary: A remarkable rotating house, built in 1963 by the imaginative Sam Harkleroad, is now available for sale, showcasing a one-of-a-kind design. Overlooking busy Highway 101, this property comprises seven homes, all presently leased, with a total price tag of $3.3 million. Harkleroad's distinctive architectural legacy thrives across Marin County, but his grandson has chosen to list the asset, citing the complexities of maintenance as a challenge.

stories.title: Giant 746lb bluefin tuna caught off Yorkshire after nearly 90 years as scientists explain UK return
stories.summary: A giant 746lb (338kg) Atlantic bluefin tuna has been caught off the Yorkshire coast, around 10 miles from Whitby, after nearly 90 years. Scientists say warming seas, recovering fish stocks and tighter fishing controls may be behind the species’ return. The catch comes near Whitby, where an 851lb British record was set in 1933.

stories.title: Florida’s python invasion was followed by a huge drop in native mammals
CCPA fines Amazon Rs 1 lakh for misleading ‘Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad’ listings
At least 100 killed after illegal gold mine collapses in Central African Republic
Man and his dog uncover a 3,400-year-old Bronze Age axe in England
stories.summary: In an English forest, a fortunate man and his dog uncovered an astonishing 3,400-year-old axe head emblematic of Britain's Bronze Age. This remarkable find sheds light on the enduring mysteries of our ancient past, revealing the metalworking capabilities of prehistoric communities. Artifacts like this one remind us that hidden treasures await discovery in even the most familiar settings.

stories.title: Missouri engineer hand-built an underground home into a hillside; 50yrs later, it remains leak-free
stories.summary: A Missouri engineer spent years carving an underground home into an Ozarks hillside, building it largely by hand without an architect. Designed to resemble a natural cave, the property features steel-reinforced concrete, an earth-based ventilation system, heavy oak beams and railroad-inspired details. His son Zane now restores the remarkable 50-year-old home and surrounding 225-acre property.

stories.title: Indian caregiver fatally stabbed in Israel, elderly couple’s grandson indicted
Uttarakhand HC rejects bail pleas of 3 convicts in Ankita Bhandari murder case
More than 100,000 ancient shipwrecks may be hiding beneath the Baltic Sea
Meet Natalie Muro, 18-year-old Colorado student who used an invasive plant to fight algal blooms
stories.summary: A remarkable eighteen-year-old student has developed an ingenious device aimed at eradicating toxic algal blooms. Utilizing wind-driven waves and invasive plant species, this unique system demonstrated impressive results in field tests, removing nearly all cyanobacteria and trapping decayed cell matter. This groundbreaking solution offers a cost-effective way to restore and revitalize unhealthy freshwater ecosystems.

stories.title: Amit Shah to chair meeting with CMs, top officials of southern states to resolve inter-state issues
stories.summary: In Mahabalipuram, Home Minister Amit Shah will oversee the Southern Zonal Council meeting, where crucial discussions about water sharing and education priorities among states will take place. Following this, he is set to travel to Siliguri to inaugurate new border security projects, and engage with personnel from Sashastra Seema Bal. His visit will wrap up with a comprehensive review meeting on border security.

stories.title: 1958, the US secretly detonated 3 nuclear devices 100–500 km above the South Atlantic
stories.summary: In a clandestine effort, Operation Argus conducted nuclear tests in the stratosphere over the South Atlantic Ocean. These detonations resulted in spectacular artificial auroras and fleeting radiation belts around our planet. The mission’s intent was to shield against Soviet missile threats and radar detection systems. Yet, the swift vanishing of these barriers caused significant communication disturbances, leading to the formulation of international accords banning nuclear experiments in space.

stories.title: Scientists simulate nuclear strike to stop a 160-metre asteroid impact
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking study, scientists conducted simulations showcasing the potential of nuclear warheads to neutralize hazardous asteroids. These experiments focused on strategies for fragmenting large asteroids prior to their collision with Earth. While this approach holds promise for planetary protection, it is viewed as a last resort, especially for threats detected late. Ongoing research is crucial for insights into fragment dynamics and their long-lasting consequences.

stories.title: 71-year-old woman donated her farm to create America’s arts park
California couple restores 136-acre farm into thriving wildlife habitat
In the 1970s, a New Mexico architect built Earthships from tyres and cans for extreme weather
stories.summary: Michael Reynolds pioneered the Earthship concept, creating innovative homes constructed from repurposed materials that encourage self-sufficiency. These structures harness recycled resources and natural systems for energy and water usage. Earthships serve as a robust solution against infrastructure breakdowns and natural calamities. This approach is now shaping a wider trend in sustainable construction practices, showcasing an off-grid living model.

stories.title: Indian-origin couple die of major impact trauma in light plane crash in UK

Government planning to bring E10 back? Clamour grows after top bureaucrat's remark
stories.summary: E20 is petrol containing 20% ethanol and 80% petrol. The government has promoted higher ethanol blending as a way to reduce crude oil imports, save foreign exchange and improve India's energy security. India also achieved its 20% blending target ahead of the original 2030 deadline. However, the nationwide shift has generated concerns among some vehicle owners, particularly those with older vehicles.

stories.title: 'Terrible': UK PM Burnham after Palestinian refugee dies alongside wife, daughter in swimming tragedy

4,000-year-old painted stone in Indonesia reveals art carried by ancient Austronesian voyagers
stories.summary: A painted stone found on Indonesia's Wetar Island offers ancient insights. This artifact dates back over 4,000 years and shows early artistic traditions. The artwork predates Neolithic pottery, revealing a significant cultural development. Portable symbols likely traveled with Austronesian voyagers across islands. This discovery reshapes our understanding of ancient maritime cultural exchanges.

stories.title: EasyJet to end all flights from key UK airport from January 2027
AI analysed 15,000 bird skeletons spanning 45 million years
Two Mumbai doctors to receive Pakistan’s highest civilian honour for keeping Jinnah’s illness secret
stories.summary: In a remarkable recognition, two Parsi physicians have been nominated posthumously for Pakistan's prestigious civilian award. They upheld the confidentiality surrounding Muhammad Ali Jinnah's terminal health condition prior to Partition, demonstrating a silent commitment to their professional ethics. This discreet dedication played an inadvertent yet significant role in the formation of Pakistan. The award ceremony is scheduled for March 2027.

stories.title: Destroyed by a 2015 storm, a Virginia refuge beach lot is now moving 2.5 miles north
stories.summary: Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge is relocating its beach facilities to a more secure northern position following significant storm damage. This proactive approach not only aims to cut future repair costs but also accommodates the natural shifts of the island. While new parking arrangements will be established, the former site will transition back into its native ecosystem.

stories.title: Delhi Jal Board case: Satyendar Jain, four others sent to 14-day judicial custody
South Korea turns to China as Trump warms up to Kim
Modi govt's Gen Z outreach: One Union minister to visit one university every day
stories.summary: The proposed initiative, called 'One Day, One University', is aimed at strengthening the government's engagement with young people. During these visits, ministers are expected to hold discussions with students, hear their views on issues affecting the country and explain government schemes meant for students and young people. The plan comes at a time when student protests over the NEET paper leak issue have intensified in parts of the country.

stories.title: BEL, Ananth Technologies ink pact
Evening news wrap: Kiren Rijiju rejects China incursion claim; US envoy Sergio Gor visits Srinagar, and more
stories.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju acknowledged border delineation problems in Arunachal Pradesh while rejecting Chinese incursion claims. US Ambassador Sergio Gor visited Srinagar and will review the travel advisory for Jammu and Kashmir. A Bengal court issued an arrest warrant for TMC MP Mahua Moitra in a hate speech case. Rahul Gandhi supported tribal residents protesting the Ken-Betwa River Link Project in Bundelkhand.

stories.title: At 14, Sheri Lynch got a grey hippo; 40 years later, she had 1,086 items
stories.summary: Sheri Lynch has achieved Guinness World Records fame for her extraordinary hippo collection, which began with a single plush toy gifted to her in her teenage years. Over the span of more than forty years, she has gathered more than a thousand hippo-themed treasures from various corners of the globe.

stories.title: Jharkhand students suspend 26-day protest over JPSC-JSSC exam; give 2-month ultimatum to Soren govt
Bought in 2016, Indiana bishop’s former home with chapel is now listed at $1.28 million
stories.summary: After nine years of dedication, an Indiana family has lovingly restored a historic home that once served as a Catholic bishop's residence, complete with a private chapel. Purchased at auction in 2016, they meticulously preserved its original features and completed extensive renovations. Now listed for $1.284 million, the family is ready to embark on new adventures and explore the world.

stories.title: European wild boars escaped a North Carolina hunting ranch in 1912; a century later...
stories.summary: Invasive European wild boars, originally introduced to the area in 1912, are wreaking havoc within Great Smoky Mountains National Park. To mitigate damage to delicate ecosystems, park management annually removes around 275 of these feral hogs. The boars breed with domestic pigs, creating hybrid species that further disrupt native wildlife. Efforts to control their population involve trapping, shooting, and implementing fencing strategies.

stories.title: Sumit Sarkar: The Citizen Historian
stories.summary: Professor Sumit Sarkar significantly impacted the understanding of Indian nationalism, illuminating its intricacies through comprehensive analysis. He explored the evolution of nationalism, internal disputes, and collective movements, while challenging conventional binaries. His focus on ordinary people's cravings for justice defined his contributions as a public thinker and citizen historian. This article pays tribute to his influential teaching and the lasting academic heritage he leaves behind.

stories.title: FSSAI action prompts Amway, Emami, four other brands to drop '100%' product claims
stories.summary: FSSAI said Bonn Biscuits had used a "100%" claim in an for its Bonn Cummin Flavor Jeera Bite Biscuits, 76 gm. The company has since removed the claim from its website. Emami was also asked to address its use of a 100 per cent claim for Zhandu Honey. According to FSSAI, the company complied with its advisory and took corrective action.

stories.title: Quote of the day by John Cena: "A man's character is not judged after he celebrates a victory, but by…"
A 9-year-old girl in the Philippines raised money to help one of the world's rarest birds
A British duke sent six Himalayan tahr to New Zealand in 1904; five survived the voyage, and...
stories.summary: Himalayan tahr were introduced to New Zealand's South Island by British aristocrats in pursuit of sport hunting back in 1904. Quickly multiplying, these creatures turned into an invasive species, wreaking havoc on native alpine ecosystems. Control measures, including government-led aerial shooting, have not proven entirely effective, creating a challenging situation for conservationists and hunters alike. The management of tahr remains an ongoing struggle within New Zealand's wildlife strategy.

stories.title: Young YouTuber Buys NYC Apartment: Eden Masliah mixes savings and inheritance; questions feeling fully proud
stories.summary: YouTuber Eden Masliah, 21, has purchased a $740,000 two-bedroom N.Y.C. apartment after saving about $250,000 from her content career and using money left by her late father for an investment. Although the purchase marks a major milestone, Masliah admits she struggles to see it as entirely her achievement because of her inheritance. She is now renovating the apartment and hopes to create a timeless space that reflects her personal style.

stories.title: Canada deports former Iranian deputy interior minister Seyed Salman Samani
3 killed, 3 injured after truck gas tank explodes at Delhi CNG station while refuelling
stories.summary: A fire service officer said all six injured people were taken to hospital, where they were receiving treatment. Further information about the rest three is awaited. Fire service personnel also took precautionary measures at the station and worked to bring the situation under control. The cause of the explosion has not yet been established. An investigation is underway to determine what led to the gas tank bursting.

stories.title: Amidst the AI data centre backlash, a Missouri farmer is inviting developers to buy his land
stories.summary: In Missouri, a farmer has taken the unexpected step of inviting data center developers to bid on his land, despite notable local opposition and recent state restrictions. He believes that data centers could revitalize struggling rural economies by creating jobs and generating tax revenue. The farmer also addresses valid concerns about water use and electricity costs, presenting his offer as an opportunity for growth even when local prospects are dim.

'Important part of India': US envoy Sergio Gor visits Srinagar, says 'will review' travel advisory
In 1964, a 27-year-old woman bought an abandoned Maine island and lived alone; 22 years later, it became a wildlife sanctuary
stories.summary: Witch Island, previously inhabited by the infamous Anna Chittenden—referred to as the 'Witch of Wall Street'—has transformed into a wildlife sanctuary. After her brief stay, Jane Sewall took on the responsibility of safeguarding the isle from irresponsible tourists. In 1986, Sewall gifted the island to the Maine Audubon Society, which is now overseen by the Coastal Rivers Conservation Trust.

stories.title: 'I stand with them': Rahul Gandhi backs protest by Bundelkhand tribals against 'Ken-Betwa project'
'There's a problem at the border': Rijiju admits delineation issue in Arunachal, rejects China incursion claim

Harvard to pay Rs 507 crore settlement after morgue manager stole, sold donated body parts
What happened to TikTok star Ayesha Gilamana who died at 28? Everything we know as police detain 3 suspects
stories.summary: Tragedy struck when TikTok sensation Ayesha Gilamana, popularly known as Shamsu Bibi, was shot and killed while driving. Assailants on a motorcycle opened fire, leading to a crash involving her vehicle. Ayesha's younger sister was injured in the wreck and is now receiving treatment. Authorities have arrested three suspects believed to be related to the attackers, as investigations continue to uncover the motive behind this shocking incident.

stories.title: Congress may move court if Pune curfew blocks Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron ki Goonj’ event
stories.summary: Congress may approach courts if Pune administration halts Rahul Gandhi's student convention. The party secured college permission for the August 22 event, facing a fortnight's gathering ban. This ban, imposed for protests and festivals, is seen as targeting the Congress program. Previous attempts to block similar conventions occurred in Dehradun, Allahabad, and Kota. The party believes the BJP is attempting to disrupt its youth outreach efforts.

stories.title: In 1943, Franklin Delano Roosevelt gave Springwood and 33 acres to US; estate had 1,500 acres and 500,000 trees
stories.summary: President Franklin D. Roosevelt generously bequeathed his family's Springwood estate to the government, substantially enhancing the property throughout his life. By planting over 500,000 trees, Roosevelt transformed the surrounding landscape. This pivotal donation secured the lasting preservation of this notable presidential site, which became both America’s first presidential library and a cherished national historic landmark.

stories.title: FBI puts Indian national Major Singh on Most Wanted list
Meet Kanav Jain: Scottish student who built a low-cost autonomous aircraft to deliver medicines to remote communities
stories.summary: Kanav Jain, a talented Scottish student, has been awarded the prestigious UK Young Engineer of the Year for creating AeroAid, an innovative low-cost autonomous drone aimed at delivering medical supplies. This versatile VTOL quadplane combines the best features of helicopters and airplanes, making it ideal for reaching remote locations. Jain’s mission is to leverage technology for vital humanitarian assistance, reflecting his commitment as a leader in drone technology workshops.

stories.title: Spanish woman trains 18 rescued donkeys to help prevent wildfires
'This is done because Punjab election is coming up': AAP leader Satyendar Jain cries foul after arrest
UP moving strongly towards $1 trillion economy; state has edge in infrastructure, logistics: CM Yogi Adityanath
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is moving strongly towards becoming a USD 1 trillion economy, said chief minister Yogi Adityanath, highlighting the state's advantages in infrastructure, logistics, industrial growth and good governance as key drivers of its economic expansion.

stories.title: A polar bear destroyed almost an entire seabird colony in Alaska
Queen Camilla says she nearly revealed King Charles III’s cancer diagnosis
Between 1969 and 1972, US released a weevil to fight musk thistle; it later attacked native thistles
stories.summary: A biological control initiative aimed at managing invasive thistles integrated a weevil specifically targeting musk thistle. Unfortunately, this insect extended its reach to native plant species, leading to detrimental effects on local thistles, including an endangered variety that experienced a decline in seed production. This situation underscores the critical importance of careful evaluation in invasive species control programs.

stories.title: Disney built Disneyland around a family farm that refused a $90 million offer
stories.summary: For decades, the Fujishige family refused to sell their 58-acre farm in Anaheim, even as Disneyland and surrounding development transformed the area. Disney and other developers made repeated offers for the valuable land, but the family continued growing strawberries and vegetables. After years of pressure and a bitter fight with the city, the family finally agreed to sell in 1998, shortly before Hiroshi Fujishige died. The former farm later became the Toy Story parking lot at Disneyland.

stories.title: A 2,500-year-old sacred well in Italy hid bronze offerings and two human skeletons
stories.summary: Archaeologists found an unusual ritual well at ancient Etruscan city Kainua in Italy. Two bronze statuettes and a rare bronze plate were discovered at the well's bottom. These objects were votive offerings placed during a foundation ritual centuries ago. Two adult human skeletons were also found, marking the structure's ritual closing. The findings offer new insights into Etruscan city foundations and religious traditions.

stories.title: Australian couple bought a cattle farm and planted 34,000 trees to restore rainforest
Trump claims over 24,000 noncitizens voted illegally in 2020
Netanyahu's party puts Mamdani alongside Iran, Hezbollah leaders on billboard
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's party placed Mayor Mamdani's image on a billboard. This billboard featured Mamdani alongside leaders hostile to Israel's interests. Netanyahu is campaigning for re-election amid political challenges in Israel. He has increasingly used Mamdani's criticism as campaign messaging. The exchange occurs while Gaza ceasefire efforts remain stalled.

stories.title: Oklahoma woman finds missing dog 1,100 miles away in North Carolina after 2 weeks
Pakistan govt to challenge SC order to move jailed ex-PM Imran Khan to hospital
Bihar: Water cannon used as RJD leaders march to Raj Bhavan; Tejashwi, Misa Bharti detained
Nature’s biodegradable plastic may hold clues to Earth’s crisis
1,300 Swiss villagers face danger as thawing glaciers loosen a massive Alpine rock
stories.summary: Kandersteg village in Switzerland faces a significant landslide threat from an unstable mountain. Scientists link this danger to thawing permafrost and changing glacier dynamics caused by climate change. While the threat is not immediate, authorities have prepared evacuation plans and monitoring systems. Residents are aware of the risks but remain calm, trusting the implemented safety measures. This situation highlights the increasing natural risks faced by mountain communities globally.

stories.title: Kansas couple builds tornado-resistant home from tyres, cans and boxes
stories.summary: In an innovative twist on sustainable living, a couple in Kansas is transforming discarded items into a unique residence. This Earthship features around 1,000 tires and 16,000 aluminum cans, built to endure severe weather, including tornadoes and fires. It will autonomously generate power, harvest rainwater, and process wastewater, demonstrating how waste can be creatively repurposed into a haven.

stories.title: 'Foolproof system in place, difficult to breach': Centre lists NEET exam security measures before SC
In 1993, an art historian found a forgotten painting; 33 years later, its female creator was rediscovered
stories.summary: A remarkable find by an art historian in 1993 ignited a relentless pursuit to recover the lost masterpieces of Michaelina Wautier. This accomplished 17th-century painter's works had long been misattributed to men throughout history. The pivotal recovery of her 'The Five Senses' series in 2020 heralded a new era, culminating in a landmark exhibition at London's Royal Academy in 2026, finally restoring her rightful legacy after centuries in the shadows.

stories.title: A rotating 'garbage island' spreads over 1.6 million sq km in the Pacific with 50 kilograms of plastic per square kilometre
stories.summary: Between the shores of Hawaii and California floats a staggering 1.6 million square kilometers of plastic debris. This island of waste includes not just nets and ropes but also countless microplastics that pose serious threats to marine wildlife. Animals often mistake plastics for food, while others become trapped in ghost fishing gear.

stories.title: Vijay govt revokes order barring students from Left, CJP protests in Tamil Nadu
'Voice sample is not required': Rahul Gandhi’s counsel opposes plea in Savarkar defamation case
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi's lawyer opposed a plea for his voice sample in a defamation case. The defense argued the request was premature for the ongoing court proceedings. Satyaki Savarkar's deposition also brought Godse-RSS links into focus during cross-examination. The defamation case stems from remarks made by Rahul in London during 2023. The court has directed the defense to file its formal response by September 1.

stories.title: Meet Tina Jin, 15-year-old who turned animal bones into a water-cleaning material
US soldiers hid a time capsule inside a barracks wall before deploying to Iraq
'He would get corruption done': Swati Maliwal targets Kejriwal after Satyendar Jain's arrest
Vijay rolls out slew of perks for Tamil Nadu MLAs: Vehicle, monthly allowances, bigger health cover
'We need to meet': Envoy says PM Modi wants Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman's visit to be 'memorable'
stories.summary: India's High Commissioner emphasized Prime Minister Modi's desire for a memorable visit. He assured Prime Minister Rahman of an appropriate and honorable reception. This engagement aims to benefit people and businesses in both nations. India calls for trust and dialogue to address current bilateral differences. Both countries should build on shared history and aspirations for future prosperity.

stories.title: India will take whatever action to defeat terrorism: MEA as trial move begins against Hafiz Saeed, Lakhvi
Half of Maharashtra homeopathy colleges have political links
Panel seeks 20% cap on drug, medical device mark-ups
Food labels, claims under FSSAI scanner; firms revise products after notices
